docs.text: Commands are actions: tuvl <verb> <thing> . Every command that reports supports --json with a stable, documented schema (coding agents parse it; /dev/schema/cli serves the schemas in dev mode). -d/--project-dir defaults to the current directory everywhere. Every option of every command, with its value and default, is on the generated full option reference .
docs.title: CLI reference

docs.text: Each verb makes one kind of promise, so the name tells you what a command will do. Verb Promise Things generate Writes files. Spends tokens only where a coding agent is involved spec , tasks , code , ui-spec , lock , key , rls lint Static rules over what you wrote. Offline, zero tokens project , spec verify Is one thing still in step with another? Exits 1 on drift spec , lock , ui-spec , rls , audit check Is it reachable and working right now? Touches the live environment system , agent , storage review A judgement of code code approve / reject / reopen A human decision, recorded in the audit ledger spec create / import / renumber Make or bring in specs and ideas spec / idea / idea list / show Only read ideas , specs , tasks , runs , agents , objects / idea , run , event , audit , drift , project run Run a workflow or the tests workflow , tests serve Start a server app , mcp follow / pin / replay Work with runs run / run / runs use / set / upgrade / register / update Project setup agent / project / project / project / skills export / prune Admin audit , schema / traces , memory init , dev , ship , deploy One action each
docs.title: The verbs

docs.text: Command Options tuvl init [NAME] --dev-telemetry URL , --sample , --preset gemini\|openai\|anthropic\|ollama , --decision-model laya\|none , -y/--yes , --multi-tenant , --no-ai-skills , --agent , --no-agent , --list-agents , --initials , --git/--no-git , --branch , --commit , --ci github\|gitlab\|none Scaffold a project. A preset writes llms/default.yaml with a current model id, reading the key from the environment. --sample is a ticket-triage project (spec, TaskPlan, tests, lock) that passes the CI gate as created. --decision-model laya adds llms/laya.yaml , LAYA_API_* in .env and a compose.yaml that runs laya-serve locally (asked interactively, default no). -y accepts every default. It also asks for your initials (they stamp the ids of ideas and specs you create) and, when coding agents are installed, which one tuvl may run for you ( -y picks none), writes both to .tuvl/agent.yaml (git-ignored), and runs git init on branch develop when git is installed ( --ci github or gitlab also writes the deterministic gate as CI: errors fail on pull requests, everything --strict on pushes to develop / main ) and the project is not already inside a repository ( --commit makes an initial commit) tuvl list agents / use agent <agent\|none> / check agent -d , --json (list), --force , --command (use) The coding agents on this machine (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Amp, Qwen Code, Aider, OpenCode, Goose), the one you selected, and whether tuvl can run it: yes for an agent tuvl can let draft and build (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI: their headless modes can confine a write to the folder), review only for one it can ask to review but never to write (Cursor, Copilot CLI, Amp), detected, not yet for the rest. The choice is yours alone, in .tuvl/agent.yaml (git-ignored). check agent checks the selected agent starts, then runs it once on a trivial task in a scratch folder (a few tokens; -y skips the question). use generic --command '…' selects any command that reads a prompt on stdin and edits its working directory tuvl check storage [name] / list objects <name> [prefix] --json (check); -n/--limit (list, default 100) Check each kind: Storage store by writing, reading back and deleting a probe object (read-only stores are only listed), or list a store's objects. See docs/storage.md tuvl lint project --strict , --json Contracts, data flow, types, policy, artifacts, lock; prints each workflow's determinism profile and worst-case tokens. --strict fails on warnings. Ends with needs models : every model the workflows use, its provider and the environment variables it reads (or "no LLM required"); V028 = unknown model reference, V029 = undeclared credentials (an error at ship time) tuvl generate code [WORKFLOW] --check Schemas, code-agent stubs (body-preserving merge), prompt placeholders, spec tests. --check writes nothing and exits 1 on drift tuvl generate code --spec SPEC --task 3 \| --task 1,3 \| --all --no-agent , --agent , --max-attempts 3 , --budget USD , --timeout S , --model , --base , --no-pr , --ready , --continue , --keep-worktree , --consent , --review none\|static\|agent , --review-blocking , --reviewer Build an approved spec's models and workflows from its task list. Phase 1, deterministic, zero tokens: the missing models/*.yaml from # Data , a workflows/<flow>.yaml skeleton whose steps are all pending (trigger, ends, and every step's id, inputs, outputs, routes and budget come from # Flows ), then the generated schemas, stubs, prompt placeholders and tests; one branch feature/<SPEC>-scaffold , never overwriting an existing file. Phase 2, your coding agent, one task at a time: for each selected agent task a branch feature/TASK-… stacked on the one before, in a worktree; the agent replaces that one pending step and may touch only the workflow, agents/*.py and artifacts/ ; tuvl regenerates what is generated and accepts the task only when the step is implemented and lint project and verify spec agree (findings go back to the agent), then commits and, with a remote and gh / glab , pushes and opens a draft pull request based on the previous branch. Before a task is committed its Python is reviewed ( --review static , the default: the C-rules and ruff, errors fail the task and go back to the agent; agent adds a second opinion that lands in the pull request and blocks only with --review-blocking ). Failed tasks leave no branch and stop the run ( --continue goes on with independent ones). Re-running skips what is built. Task numbers: 3 , T3 , 003 or the full id. --no-agent stops after phase 1. Without --spec , tuvl generate code never calls an agent tuvl generate ui-spec / verify ui-spec -w/--workflow , --all , --no-tests , --base-url , --check , --json , -d ( verify ui-spec takes --no-tests , --base-url , --json : exit 1 when ui/specs/ is not what generate would write now) Write ui/specs/ (zero tokens): how to build the UI on this backend , for the developers and coding agents who build it. README.md (the @tuvl/client setup, sign-in, the backend surface: which system routes a production server mounts, shared behaviour, rules for whoever builds the UI), one <workflow>.md per workflow whose tasks are done (endpoint, auth, request, every end's status and body, the run lifecycle, the approval form of human steps, real examples from the acceptance cases, a client.execute(...) snippet, a checklist), models.md for models with CRUD routes (operations, scopes, groups, fields, secure flagged), and ui-contract.json . init creates the folder; codegen --spec adds a workflow's file in the commit of the task that completes it. Text below the notes marker in a file is kept. --check exits 1 when a file is missing or out of date (add it to CI); a workflow with a pending step or open task gets no file until it is built ( --all writes it anyway) tuvl review code [PATH…] --base REF , --spec SPEC , --task 3 , --strict , --no-ruff , --explain C0xx , --json ; second opinion: --agent , --reviewer , --blocking off\|high\|medium\|low , --post , --consent , --budget , --timeout Review the Python of code agents ( agents/*.py , not _generated ); --spec or --task keeps it to the code agents those tasks created (models, steps that are not code, tests and examples have none). Tier 1, free: tuvl's rules — C001 shape ( @agent("run") async def f(inp, ctx) ), C002 processes and eval , C003 direct network (use ctx.http ), C004 os.environ , C005 file writes (use ctx.storage ), C006 non-determinism (random, uuid, clock), C007/C008 work or state kept in the module, C009 hard-coded URLs, C010 secrets, C011 a returned signal the workflow does not route, C012 a write in an effect: read agent — plus ruff (C900) when installed. Errors fail (exit 1), warnings only with --strict . Tier 2, advisory: --agent asks a coding agent that cannot change anything (Claude Code runs with only Read, Glob and Grep) to read the code, the diff and the spec and answer with JSON findings (high / medium / low / info); an answer that is not valid JSON is a failed review, never a pass. Findings only block with --blocking . --post comments the review on the branch's pull request. The reviewer is another agent than yours when you have one tuvl generate lock / verify lock --check , --mcp/--no-mcp Pin model ids, artifact hashes, judge/decision models and MCP tool schemas in tuvl.lock ; verify lock is the read-only check (exit 1 when the lock is missing or stale; --no-mcp skips listing MCP servers live) tuvl check system --live , --json , --only , --skip , --strict , --fix , -q , --verbose Is the project healthy? Runs named check groups, each check ok / warn / fail / skip: project (identity record), env (Python range, .env present and git-ignored, uv ), config (the project loads), models (each model, the variables it needs and which are missing; --live makes one minimal call per model — Laya/Jev: their /health ), storage , and, where the toolchain is installed, git (repository, branch, identity, remote) and skills ( AGENTS.md , .agents/skills ). --only / --skip take comma-separated group names. Exit 1 on any failure; --strict exits 2 when only warnings remain. --fix applies the safe repairs a check offers ( git init -b develop , adding .env to .gitignore ) and re-checks; nothing destructive. A production server runs the model check at startup and refuses to start on a missing variable; /health reports each model's readiness tuvl run tests --live , --allow-uncertain , --strict , -k/--only TEXT , --json Run Test documents offline ( --live lets unmocked model/tool agents call out). Results are PASS, STUBBED (expectations met only through unmocked pending placeholders — not counted) or FAIL; --strict (CI) also fails on stubbed results and untrusted judge calibration tuvl show project --json The project's identity from .tuvl/project.yaml : the immutable, self-checking id ( prj_<uuidv7>-<2 check characters> , minted by tuvl init ; the check catches typos and hand edits, it is not a signature), name, author, email, type ( poc\|dev\|production ), version, registry status. Also editable in Insight → Settings → Project. Full reference: project tuvl upgrade project --name , --new-id Create project.yaml for a project that predates it. Never changes an existing id; --new-id replaces a malformed or copied id and clears its registration tuvl set dev-telemetry [URL] --off , --identity initials\|full , --token-env VAR , --commands/--no-commands , --forget , --rotate-token Share developer actions through your team's collector (optional, off by default; tuvl init can ask for it). Writes .tuvl/dev-telemetry.yaml (commit it); your token is never in it. --forget removes your token from this machine. See developer telemetry tuvl register developer --name , --email , --code Register yourself at the team's collector with its join code and keep the token of your own in your config folder; it sends your events and reads the team's tuvl show dev-telemetry / check dev-telemetry --json / --flush Whether it is on, who you are at the collector, what is queued and the last delivery; ask the collector who your token is (exit 1 when it does not accept it) and, with --flush , send everything queued tuvl list team-activity --actor , --entity , --kind , -n , --json What the team did on this project, from the collector tuvl set project FIELD VALUE Update name , author , email , type , version , description , license or repo (validated). The description is Markdown (up to 2000 characters): VALUE of @about.md reads a file, - reads stdin; show project renders it tuvl register project --nest URL , -y List the project in the public catalogue. Prints the exact payload first and asks; signs in with GitHub's device flow; the author and email are sent for contact and never shown publicly. Also available as Insight → Settings → Project → Register / Update listing (same payload preview and login) tuvl update skills --diff Refresh AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/ to this tuvl version (removes 1.x skills; mirrors to .claude/skills/ )

docs.text: Command Options tuvl verify spec [SPEC_FILE…] --strict , --no-tests , --json Does the implementation match the spec? Zero tokens; rules R001–R010 and a traceability matrix (step → agent → tests). Exits 1 on a mismatch ( --strict : also on unfinished work) tuvl create spec NAME --owner , --workflow Write specs/<name>.md from the template tuvl import idea [PATH…] --url (repeatable), --allow-private , --title , --supersedes , --initials , --include , --exclude , --max-size , --commit , --dry-run , --json Copy an idea (files, a folder, or a snapshot of a web page, Jira issue, Confluence page or GitHub issue given with --url ; see authoring ) into idea/IDEA-<INITIALS>-NNNN/source/ as a numbered, immutable record, with IDEA.yaml (file hashes, who, when) and idea/INDEX.yaml . Text is extracted from Markdown/text directly, from Word files with no extra install, and from PDFs with tuvl[pdf] (a scanned PDF has no text layer and gets a warning; there is no OCR) into extracted/ . Secret and key files, hidden files, symbolic links and unsupported types are skipped and listed. Editing the body afterwards makes the approval stale (S017). reject sends it back to draft with a reason; reopen withdraws an approval tuvl generate tasks SPEC --dry-run Derive the task list from an approved spec, with no model: one task per new model, step and example, a manual task for each external-system step. Keeps ids, refreshes section hashes, marks removed ones obsolete ; --dry-run previews a draft tuvl list specs --json Each spec's id, status (draft / approved / approved but changed), approver and ideas tuvl prune memory COLLECTION --key OWNER or --older-than 30d (exactly one), -d Erases what agents remember: every memory of one owner, or all older than an age, in one memory collection. Prints how many rows went and deletes nothing else (knowledge-base rows and other collections are untouched). See Remembering across runs tuvl show audit / show event REF / verify audit / export audit / prune traces --entity , --actor , --kind , --since 2d , -n , --follow , --json (log); --format json\|csv , -o (export); --older-than DAYS (prune) The local audit ledger .tuvl/audit/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl (git-ignored): one hash-chained event per action with side effects — init, agent choice, idea import, id renumber, spec create / approve / reject / reopen (refusals too, with the reason), task derivation. It holds ids, hashes and short details, never file contents, prompts or secrets (full prompts and agent output go to .tuvl/trace/ by hash). --entity on an idea also shows its specs and tasks. verify finds an edited, removed or reordered line (exit 1); prune deletes old trace files, never the ledger. The ledger belongs to one machine and one developer: what the team shares through git is the spec's own approval fields tuvl create spec NAME --idea IDEA-… Also numbers the spec SPEC-XX-NNNN-NN after its first idea, links it to the idea(s) and records status: draft tuvl generate spec --idea IDEA-… \| --from PATH --title , --agent , --max-attempts 3 , --budget USD , --timeout S , --model , --base , --dry-run , --show-prompt , -y , --consent , --no-pr , --ready , --keep-worktree , --here A coding agent writes a draft spec from an idea. tuvl numbers it ( SPEC-XX-NNNN-NN ), creates branch spec/<id> in a worktree under .tuvl/worktrees/ , builds the prompt (the idea's text, the spec grammar, the rules), runs your agent headlessly, lets it change only that spec file (anything else is reverted and fed back), puts back the lifecycle fields it must not set ( id , ideas , status , no approval), runs lint spec and retries with the findings, then commits and, with a remote and gh / glab , pushes and opens a draft pull request. It never merges and never approves. --here skips the branch and the pull request and writes specs/<id>.md into your working folder, uncommitted (the terminal UI uses it, so the draft shows up in the tree). Needs git; the idea must be committed ( spec import --commit ; --from does it). With Claude Code the run is restricted at the source (no code-running tools, files confined to the folder, nothing may prompt); generic ( tuvl use agent generic --command '…' ) cannot be restricted, only checked afterwards. Idea text is sent to your agent only after you consent once ( --consent , stored in .tuvl/agent.yaml ) tuvl lint spec [SPEC_FILE…] --strict , --json Is the spec complete and consistent? Zero tokens; rules S001–S016 with line numbers, plus P001–P005 on its task list ( spec-driven ). Exits 1 on a blocking finding ( --strict : on warnings too) tuvl list tasks [SPEC_FILE] --strict , --no-tests , --json , --watch , --interval Derived task statuses. --strict exits 1 unless every live task is done and none is blocked or stale. --watch keeps refreshing (recomputing only when a project file changes) and overlays live generate code progress (queued, running attempt n/N and its gate, failed, in review) from .tuvl/live/tasks.json tuvl show drift [SPEC_FILE] --json Stale tasks and spec sections no task covers

docs.text: Command Options tuvl dev -p/--port (8885), --auto-login , --no-tui , --show-key , --no-browser , --no-tui , -H/--allow-host Dev server with Insight and the dev API, reloading on YAML changes. The session key is stored in .tuvl/.dev-session (0600); --show-key prints it. On a terminal it also starts a terminal UI ( tuvl[tui] , part of tuvl[standard] ): a tree of your ideas → specs → tasks (status, and live progress while generate code runs), the actions that apply to what you select (check, approve, derive tasks, scaffold, build with your agent, validate, test, ship…), and three logs: the command you ran, the engine, and the audit trail. Every action runs the same tuvl command you would type, so the gates and the audit trail are the same; anything that spends your agent's tokens or is hard to undo asks first ( Run it / Cancel ) and says so. The project's own actions (lint, test, check, review, run a workflow, import an idea, show the project and the audit log, ship) are listed under every selection. Each command ends with a tokens · line: what your coding agent used (input, output, cost), or that none was. q quits and stops the engine, r refreshes, x stops a running command, c copies the last command's output (or the open log) to the clipboard. The logs are selectable too: drag with the mouse, or click in a log and use the keyboard, then copy with ctrl+c . --no-tui , or no terminal (CI, a pipe, ssh without a tty), runs the engine in this terminal with plain output tuvl serve app -p/--port , --host , -w/--workers , --role all\|api\|worker , -c/--concurrency (8), -H/--allow-host , --graceful-timeout , --drain-timeout , --forwarded-allow-ips , --limit-max-requests Production server (uvicorn, which replaces the tuvl process so it is PID 1 in a container and receives SIGTERM directly). api serves HTTP and runs synchronous requests inline; worker executes the queue. On SIGTERM it stops taking requests, lets open ones finish for --graceful-timeout seconds (20), then waits --drain-timeout seconds (20) for running runs; one still going is interrupted and another worker resumes it from its last checkpoint. --forwarded-allow-ips names the proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted (an IP or CIDR list: set your ingress network so --allow-host and the logs see the real client; * lets a client spoof its address). --limit-max-requests restarts a worker after that many requests. The Server header is off. tuvl run with no subcommand does the same tuvl serve mcp --allow-write Dev tools for coding agents over MCP (stdio); --allow-write adds codegen_write , run_workflow , pin_fixture . Refuses production

docs.text: These talk to a running server: -u/--url ( TUVL_URL , default http://localhost:8885 ) and -t/--token ( TUVL_TOKEN , needs runs:read ). Command Options tuvl list runs -w/--workflow , -s/--status , -n/--limit , --json Recent runs, newest first tuvl show run RUN_ID One run as JSON tuvl follow run RUN_ID / run workflow NAME -p/--payload JSON (run workflow) Follow a run's events until it ends, or start a run of a workflow on the server and follow it; exits 1 if it fails tuvl pin run RUN_ID -n/--name Export the journal to tests/fixtures/<workflow>/<name>.journal.json tuvl replay runs FIXTURES… --json Re-run pinned journals offline; fail if the end or output differ

docs.text: Command Options tuvl ship -t/--tag , --no-image (was --no-build ), --push , --force , --strict , --extra , --with-laya/--without-laya , --format image\|archive\|both , --archive-format tar.gz\|zip , --out , --allow-incomplete , --allow-dirty Gate (validate, no pending agents — V010 is an error at ship time, current lock; then, once the files are written, the deterministic spec gate : every spec under approval is approved and unchanged, lint spec and verify spec have no errors, every task is done ( --allow-incomplete ), generated files are current ( codegen --check , for projects with specs), no C-rule errors in the agents' Python, a current uv.lock (an error for the archive), and a clean git tree ( --allow-dirty ; what ship writes itself does not count). A spec with no status: only warns), then .dockerignore as an allowlist (only models, workflows, agents, artifacts, datasources, llms, federation, config, lock and .tuvl/system.yaml / telemetry.yaml enter the image; specs, task lists, tests, agent rules and skills, compose files and anything else stay out — V027 refuses development files), deploy/Dockerfile (pins the locked tuvl version and installs only the extras the project uses: mcp for use: mcp tools, loop MCP servers and MCP export, redis for a redis datasource, vector for collections and tuvl.data_* , otel-grpc for otlp_protocol: grpc ; it also stops when agents/*.py imports a package pyproject.toml does not declare. --extra NAME adds one the scan cannot see; the choice is recorded as the image label io.tuvl.extras ) and a Helm chart ( split: true for api + worker Deployments; a Laya Deployment + Service, with LAYA_API_BASE set for the engine, when a model uses provider: laya or with --with-laya — laya.enabled in values.yaml) and docker build , labelled io.tuvl.runtime-hash (one sha256 over the runtime files) and io.tuvl.git-commit . --format archive instead writes dist/<name>-<version>.tar.gz (or .zip ) plus a .sha256 : the same runtime files with run.sh , RUN.md , .env.example and BUILD-INFO.json , reproducible byte for byte from the same files, for hosts without Docker. On the host: tar xzf … , cp .env.example .env , fill it in, ./run.sh (needs uv ; it installs the locked dependencies and tuvl==<locked> with the same extras as the image, and serves on port 8885) tuvl deploy -d/--project-dir Coming soon: deploy to a hosted, managed tuvl engine that runs your backend services. Today it prints a message, deploys nothing and exits 1 tuvl generate key -w/--write , -f/--force A persistent Ed25519 key for signing access tokens ( TUVL_SIGNING_KEY ) tuvl generate rls -o/--out Idempotent row-level-security SQL for tenant-scoped tables tuvl verify rls Exit 1 if a tenant-scoped table lacks its RLS policy
docs.title: Shipping and operations

docs.text: tuvl installs lean. Features with their own packages are extras, and tuvl ship reads the project and installs tuvl[<only those>]==<locked version> : Extra Package tuvl ship installs it when mcp mcp a use: mcp tool, a loop mcp tool, or a workflow with trigger.mcp.enabled redis redis a kind: DataSource with type: redis , or agents/*.py imports redis vector pgvector a Collection or Embedding document, tuvl.data_search / tuvl.data_ingest , or an import of pgvector otel-grpc OTLP gRPC exporter .tuvl/telemetry.yaml has otlp_protocol: grpc generate code , run tests libcst , aiosqlite never: tuvl generate code , tuvl init --sample and tuvl run tests are development tools tuvl[standard] installs Insight and every extra, so a development install needs nothing else. The model providers and blob storage (S3, Azure, GCS, local) are part of tuvl and need no extra. tuvl ship prints the extras it chose and why and records them as the image label io.tuvl.extras ( docker inspect shows what an image carries). Beyond the extras: It also scans agents/*.py : an import of a package that pyproject.toml does not declare aborts the ship, because the image would fail at run time. Declared packages that no agent imports are listed and kept. --extra NAME adds an extra the scan cannot see, for example a feature switched on by an environment variable. It accepts mcp , redis , vector and otel-grpc . A kept deploy/Dockerfile (no --force ) that lacks an extra the project now needs stops the ship. Using a feature without its extra fails with pip install 'tuvl[name]' ; the same message appears for tuvl generate code , tuvl run tests and tuvl serve mcp on a bare install. tuvl deploy is for managed hosting and is not available yet: it prints a message and exits 1. Until then, install the chart tuvl ship writes with helm .

docs.text: The decide engine ¶ decide routes a run through ordered rules first , then — only if no rule matches — an optional decision model . Rules-only agents are deterministic and free; a model makes the agent bounded . - id: triage_refund description: Decide how a refund is handled engine: decide inputs: { order: Order, reason: str, message: str } outputs: { route: "enum[auto_refund, manager_review, reject]" } # exactly one enum output budget: { timeout: 2s, retry: { attempts: 1 } } # applies to the model call decide: rules: # first match wins - { when: "order.total > 500", then: manager_review } - { when: "reason == 'fraud_flag'", then: reject } # or: rules: artifact://refund-rules@4 (a `type: rules` artifact) model: # optional ref: triage-classifier # AgentModel (type: decision) or an llm AgentModel min_confidence: 0.8 shadow: false # true: rules decide; the model runs alongside, journaled only routes: auto_refund: issue_refund manager_review: approval reject: END.rejected low_confidence: approval # required when a model is set error: END.failed # no_rule_matched, decision_model_unavailable Semantics ¶ Situation Result A rule matches Its then . The model is not called. Source rule#<n> No rule matches, no model error ( no_rule_matched ) No rule matches, model confident (≥ min_confidence ) The model's value. Source model No rule matches, model below min_confidence low_confidence (proposal and confidence journaled) No rule matches, model unavailable (down, auth, timeout after retries) error ( decision_model_unavailable ). Never a fallback to rules, a default or another model shadow: true Rules decide ( no_rule_matched if none matches). The model runs every time; its answer is journaled for comparison and its failures are logged, not errors Rules are TEL conditions over the agent's inputs, type-checked by tuvl lint project . The output enum must equal the set of normal route keys, and every then must be one of its values (V012). A rule { when: "true", then: x } at the end is the usual default. Every invocation journals a decision event: { decision, source: rule#n | model | shadow, confidence?, model_ref?, latency_ms } . Tests assert on it with expect.decisions: { triage_refund: { source: "rule#1" } } ; Insight shows it on the run timeline. Decision models ¶ kind: AgentModel metadata: { name: triage-classifier } spec: type: decision provider: llm # laya | jev | llm model: gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite # pinned in tuvl.lock Laya and Jev (System One) ¶ laya and jev speak the System One protocol ( POST /v1/systemone ): the agent's inputs are sent as the state , and its enum output as one choice question. The answer comes back with a probability for every option, and tuvl uses the server's calibrated confidence for min_confidence . kind: AgentModel metadata: { name: laya } spec: type: decision provider: laya model: english # english | auto | multilingual | typed-decisions api_base: ${LAYA_API_BASE:http://localhost:8000} api_key: ${LAYA_API_KEY:} # optional; must be an ${ENV_VAR} reference Laya is self-hosted: the tuvl/laya-serve image ( source ) serves it on CPU, amd64 or arm64, with its weights pinned and verified, so the image version is what pins the model. model: english runs the English-only -en image (about 2 GiB of memory); model: auto routes by language and multilingual need the full image (about 3.5 GiB), because an -en image fails on non-English text. tuvl init --decision-model laya scaffolds an english model and a compose.yaml for local development, and tuvl ship adds Laya to the Helm chart with the image that matches model . Jev is TypeSafe's hosted service: set api_base to its endpoint and pin model to a version ( jev-1.13.0 ); an unpinned Jev model is a V026 warning. Confidence thresholds do not transfer between Laya and Jev (or between checkpoints) — calibrate min_confidence for the model you deploy. OpenAI-compatible endpoints ¶ A decision model behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (a gateway, a self-hosted classifier) connects through provider: llm : kind: AgentModel metadata: { name: hosted-classifier } spec: type: decision provider: llm model: openai/my-classifier # the OpenAI-compatible route api_base: ${CLASSIFIER_API_BASE} api_key: ${CLASSIFIER_API_KEY} # must be an ${ENV_VAR} reference llm asks the model for {"decision": <one of the choices>, "confidence": <0..1>} as structured output. An llm -type AgentModel can also be referenced directly; it uses the same adapter. Where the confidence comes from. A type: decision model's reported confidence is used first, then token logprobs. An llm model's logprobs come first, because a general LLM's self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated. An answer with neither (or a confidence outside 0..1) is decision_model_unavailable — never treated as certain. All providers ¶ Other providers can be registered through the tuvl.decision_providers entry point. A decide agent with an LLM-backed model must declare budget.max_tokens and budget.timeout . /health reports each configured decision model's readiness. Rules as artifacts ¶ A type: rules artifact is a reusable decision table, edited and tried in Insight (Artifacts page): kind: Artifact metadata: { name: refund-rules, version: 4 } spec: type: rules rules: - { when: "order.total > 500", then: manager_review } - { when: "true", then: auto_refund } Policy ¶ policy.model_only_decisions: warn | error | allow flags (V013) a model-only decision (no rules) that feeds a write or destructive effect without a human, approval or compensate . allow records that the workflow accepts this on purpose — for example a screen whose negative verdict blocks and whose unsure verdict goes to a human — so the choice is reviewed in the YAML instead of silenced. Changing an agent's engine to or from decide in Insight keeps its contract and re-checks it against the workflow's pinned fixtures ( Insight ).

docs.text: Developer telemetry ¶ An optional way for a team to see what every developer on a project is doing, and to see it from their own Insight. When it is on, each development action is shared through a collector your team runs: ideas imported, specs created, approved or sent back, tasks derived, each coding-agent attempt, branches, commits and pull requests, gate results, reviews, ships, and one cli.command event per command. The same collector lets each developer read the team's events back (the Audit page's Team view, the Team activity section of a task, and who built each branch). It is off by default and development only : nothing here reaches production ( tuvl ship refuses the config file and the outbox, check V027). It carries the same events the local audit ledger records (ids, hashes and short details, never file contents, prompts or secrets); the ledger remains the record and the collector gets a copy. Turn it on ¶ Where How At tuvl init answer the "Developer telemetry" question, or pass --dev-telemetry https://collector.example.com Later, in a terminal tuvl set dev-telemetry https://collector.example.com ( --off stops it) Later, in Insight Settings → Developer telemetry This writes .tuvl/dev-telemetry.yaml . Commit it so everyone on the project uses the same collector: kind: DevTelemetry version: tuvl/v2 telemetry: enabled: true server: https://collector.example.com token_env: TUVL_DEV_TELEMETRY_TOKEN # optional override of your registered token (CI, a shared runner) identity: initials # what events say about you: initials | full (name and email) commands: true # one event per command, without its arguments Register once, with a token of your own ¶ Each developer registers at the collector with the team's join code (ask whoever runs the collector): tuvl register developer # asks for your name, email (defaults: your git ones) and the join code tuvl check dev-telemetry # the collector tells you who it thinks you are The collector answers with a token that is yours : it sends your events and reads the team's. It is kept in your own config folder ( ~/.config/tuvl/dev-telemetry.json , or $TUVL_HOME ), readable only by you, never in the project and never in git; TUVL_DEV_TELEMETRY_TOKEN (or the variable named by token_env ) overrides it. tuvl set dev-telemetry --rotate-token gets a new one (the old stops working) and --forget removes it from the machine; an admin can revoke it at the collector. Insight → Settings → Developer telemetry does the same steps. tuvl show dev-telemetry says whether it is on, who you are there, how many events are waiting and when the last delivery happened. tuvl list team-activity prints what the team did ( --actor , --entity , --kind , -n ). What is sent, and how ¶ Never in the way. Each event is appended to .tuvl/audit/outbox.queue first and sent in the background in batches of up to 100 (at the end of a command, or within a second in a long-running tuvl dev ). If the collector is down, or you have no token yet, events stay queued and go with the next command; a command never fails or waits long because of telemetry. The queue keeps the newest 5,000. Who. The collector decides who an event is from by the token. Where tuvl gets you : the initials you gave at tuvl init , and the name and email from git config user.name / user.email (shown in Settings → Developer telemetry and by tuvl show dev-telemetry , and the defaults when you register). identity: initials sends your initials only and also takes your name and email out of the event's text (an approval's detail names the approver); full adds the git name and email. What an event claims about its actor is never trusted. Your local ledger keeps everything. Where from. Every batch says which tuvl version, the project id and name, the current git branch and a hash of the host name. Safe transport. https only (plain http is accepted for localhost to try a collector), no credentials in the URL, no redirects, no proxies, a few seconds' timeout. What it is. The events are what each developer's tuvl reports about itself: visibility for the team, not tamper-proof evidence. For an audit, rely on what the git host and CI record. The collector contract ¶ Any server can be the collector. Tuvl Flightlog is the collector we provide: self-hosted, Apache 2.0, SQLite or PostgreSQL, with retention, export, forwarding to a SIEM and a terminal-only admin. It comes in two builds of the same contract: a small Python service (the smallest surface; it stores only token hashes), and a tuvl project with the same contract on tuvl's own tokens and run journal (it needs PostgreSQL and Redis, and keeps a registration's token in the run record). All paths are under <server>/v1 ; everything except /register carries Authorization: Bearer <token> . POST /register {name, email, team_code} → {"token": "…", "developer": {name, email, team}} GET /me {name, email, team} of the token's owner (401 when the token is not known) POST /token/rotate {"token": "…"} : a new token for the caller; the old one stops working POST /dev-events {"schema": "tuvl.dev-events/1", "sender": {tuvl, project, name, host, branch}, "events": [...]} ; answer any 2xx to accept the batch, anything else leaves it queued. Delivery is at-least-once: de-duplicate on event.id (a ULID) GET /team/events {"events": [...]} newest first for the caller's team, with developer: {name} on each: filters project , actor , entity , kind , before (an event id), limit An event: {"id", "ts", "kind", "command", "actor": {"initials"}, "entities": [...], "result", "detail", "refs"} . Kinds are the audit kinds ( idea.imported , spec.approved , tasks.derived , task.attempt , task.failed , branch.created , pr.opened , gate.result , ship.packaged …) plus cli.command ( refs : exit_code , seconds ). A company's own certificate authority ¶ If the collector's certificate is signed by a private CA, set TUVL_DEV_TELEMETRY_CA (or SSL_CERT_FILE ) to the CA bundle on each developer's machine.

docs.text: Where How At tuvl init answer the "Developer telemetry" question, or pass --dev-telemetry https://collector.example.com Later, in a terminal tuvl set dev-telemetry https://collector.example.com ( --off stops it) Later, in Insight Settings → Developer telemetry This writes .tuvl/dev-telemetry.yaml . Commit it so everyone on the project uses the same collector: kind: DevTelemetry version: tuvl/v2 telemetry: enabled: true server: https://collector.example.com token_env: TUVL_DEV_TELEMETRY_TOKEN # optional override of your registered token (CI, a shared runner) identity: initials # what events say about you: initials | full (name and email) commands: true # one event per command, without its arguments
docs.title: Turn it on

docs.text: Each developer registers at the collector with the team's join code (ask whoever runs the collector): tuvl register developer # asks for your name, email (defaults: your git ones) and the join code tuvl check dev-telemetry # the collector tells you who it thinks you are The collector answers with a token that is yours : it sends your events and reads the team's. It is kept in your own config folder ( ~/.config/tuvl/dev-telemetry.json , or $TUVL_HOME ), readable only by you, never in the project and never in git; TUVL_DEV_TELEMETRY_TOKEN (or the variable named by token_env ) overrides it. tuvl set dev-telemetry --rotate-token gets a new one (the old stops working) and --forget removes it from the machine; an admin can revoke it at the collector. Insight → Settings → Developer telemetry does the same steps. tuvl show dev-telemetry says whether it is on, who you are there, how many events are waiting and when the last delivery happened. tuvl list team-activity prints what the team did ( --actor , --entity , --kind , -n ).
docs.title: Register once, with a token of your own

docs.text: Never in the way. Each event is appended to .tuvl/audit/outbox.queue first and sent in the background in batches of up to 100 (at the end of a command, or within a second in a long-running tuvl dev ). If the collector is down, or you have no token yet, events stay queued and go with the next command; a command never fails or waits long because of telemetry. The queue keeps the newest 5,000. Who. The collector decides who an event is from by the token. Where tuvl gets you : the initials you gave at tuvl init , and the name and email from git config user.name / user.email (shown in Settings → Developer telemetry and by tuvl show dev-telemetry , and the defaults when you register). identity: initials sends your initials only and also takes your name and email out of the event's text (an approval's detail names the approver); full adds the git name and email. What an event claims about its actor is never trusted. Your local ledger keeps everything. Where from. Every batch says which tuvl version, the project id and name, the current git branch and a hash of the host name. Safe transport. https only (plain http is accepted for localhost to try a collector), no credentials in the URL, no redirects, no proxies, a few seconds' timeout. What it is. The events are what each developer's tuvl reports about itself: visibility for the team, not tamper-proof evidence. For an audit, rely on what the git host and CI record.
docs.title: What is sent, and how

docs.text: Any server can be the collector. Tuvl Flightlog is the collector we provide: self-hosted, Apache 2.0, SQLite or PostgreSQL, with retention, export, forwarding to a SIEM and a terminal-only admin. It comes in two builds of the same contract: a small Python service (the smallest surface; it stores only token hashes), and a tuvl project with the same contract on tuvl's own tokens and run journal (it needs PostgreSQL and Redis, and keeps a registration's token in the run record). All paths are under <server>/v1 ; everything except /register carries Authorization: Bearer <token> . POST /register {name, email, team_code} → {"token": "…", "developer": {name, email, team}} GET /me {name, email, team} of the token's owner (401 when the token is not known) POST /token/rotate {"token": "…"} : a new token for the caller; the old one stops working POST /dev-events {"schema": "tuvl.dev-events/1", "sender": {tuvl, project, name, host, branch}, "events": [...]} ; answer any 2xx to accept the batch, anything else leaves it queued. Delivery is at-least-once: de-duplicate on event.id (a ULID) GET /team/events {"events": [...]} newest first for the caller's team, with developer: {name} on each: filters project , actor , entity , kind , before (an event id), limit An event: {"id", "ts", "kind", "command", "actor": {"initials"}, "entities": [...], "result", "detail", "refs"} . Kinds are the audit kinds ( idea.imported , spec.approved , tasks.derived , task.attempt , task.failed , branch.created , pr.opened , gate.result , ship.packaged …) plus cli.command ( refs : exit_code , seconds ).
docs.title: The collector contract

docs.text: If the collector's certificate is signed by a private CA, set TUVL_DEV_TELEMETRY_CA (or SSL_CERT_FILE ) to the CA bundle on each developer's machine.
docs.title: A company's own certificate authority

docs.text: Engines ¶ An agent's engine implements its contract. The closed set is pending , code , tool , decide , llm , loop , human , map and parallel . This page covers pending , code , tool , llm , human , map and parallel ; see decide and loop and tools for the other two. Every engine except pending can emit error . Engine parameters live under a key named after the engine ( code: , tool: , llm: , …). pending — a contract without an implementation ¶ - id: classify_ticket description: Decide which team owns the ticket engine: pending inputs: { ticket: Ticket } outputs: { team: "enum[billing, technical, general]" } routes: { billing: billing_queue, technical: kb_search, general: general_queue } tuvl lint project checks it fully as a contract (data flow, types, routes). It is a V010 warning. In dev and in tests it returns a typed stub : schema-valid placeholder outputs and its first normal signal. Tests override it with mocks . tuvl ship refuses a project with pending agents, and the production runner won't load one. A pending agent is a typed placeholder for a step the spec names but nobody has built yet; tuvl verify spec reports it as unfinished and tests through it are stubbed , not passed. code — a Python function ¶ - id: issue_refund description: Calculate the refund amount and record it engine: code effect: write # read | write | destructive; default write inputs: { order: Order, reason: str } outputs: { refund: Refund } code: { run: issue_refund, with: { currency: EUR } } routes: { default: reply, error: END.failed } # agents/issue_refund.py — one @agent per file from tuvl import agent, Ctx from agents._generated.schemas import IssueRefundIn, IssueRefundOut @agent("issue_refund") async def issue_refund(inp: IssueRefundIn, ctx: Ctx) -> IssueRefundOut: """Calculate the refund amount and record it.""" amount = inp.order.total if inp.reason != "partial" else inp.order.total / 2 refund = await ctx.db.create("Refund", order_id=inp.order.id, amount=amount) return IssueRefundOut(refund=refund) Signature async def f(inp: <Id>In, ctx: Ctx) -> <Id>Out or tuple[<Id>Out, str] . tuvl generate code writes the decorator, signature and docstring; you write the body. Signals Returning Out emits default ; (Out, "signal") emits that signal (it must be routed); an exception emits error ( code_exception ). ctx.db Unit of work restricted to spec.models ; read-only when effect: read (a write raises). Writes commit with the step's checkpoint. ctx ctx.log (structlog, bound to the run and agent), ctx.run_id , ctx.principal , ctx.idempotency_key , ctx.http (shared HTTP client), ctx.artifact(ref) , ctx.params (rendered code.with ), ctx.agent_id effect Declared, because it can't be derived from Python. It drives policy ( require_human_before ) and MCP annotations. Built-ins. run: tuvl.data_search and run: tuvl.data_ingest are vector search and ingest with typed contracts, configured by code.with ( collection , query / document , top_k , filter , metadata , scope: global | run ). Search writes [{content, metadata, score}] to its single list output; ingest writes the new document id to its optional single output. The tuvl. prefix is reserved. Memory built-ins. tuvl.memory_remember and tuvl.memory_recall let an agent remember across runs, in an ordinary kind: Collection : - { id: recall, engine: code, effect: read, inputs: { question: str }, outputs: { memories: "list[json]" }, code: { run: tuvl.memory_recall, with: { collection: support_memory, query: "{{ question }}", window: 5, top_k: 3 } } } - { id: remember, engine: code, inputs: { turn: str }, outputs: { stored: bool }, code: { run: tuvl.memory_remember, with: { collection: support_memory, text: "{{ turn }}" } } } Whose memory. The owner is code.with.key when given, otherwise the signed-in principal; with neither, the step fails ( tool_args_invalid ). Reads and writes are filtered by that owner in the query itself, so a run for one user never sees another's memories. Name a key from run input only when the trigger is not public: whoever can start the run chooses the owner. Recall returns the owner's last window memories (default 5, 0-50) and up to top_k older ones most related to query (default 3, 0-20), as [{content, source: recent | related, at | score}] , older context first. The step journals memory_recalled with the text it handed to the agent. Remember stores text (embedded) with the owner, run and agent in its metadata. A step that runs again after a crash stores it once. What to store is the author's choice: store the agent's answer or a summary, never a secure field. Treat recalled text as data, not instructions (an earlier user wrote it): put it in the prompt inside a labelled block, as tool results are. Erase with tuvl prune memory <collection> --key <owner> ; expire with --older-than 30d . In tests, mock them by agent id like any code agent. tool — database, HTTP, MCP and storage operations ¶ One engine, four use variants. The effect is derived ; a declared effect may only strengthen it (V015), except that an HTTP POST / PUT / PATCH may declare effect: read (search APIs often read via POST). use: db ¶ tool: { use: db, model: Order, op: read, where: { id: "{{ order_id }}" } } tool: { use: db, model: Refund, op: create, values: { order_id: "{{ order.id }}", amount: "{{ amount }}" } } tool: { use: db, model: Ticket, op: list, where: { status: open }, order_by: [-created_at], limit: 20 } op : create , read , update , delete , list , upsert . The model must be in spec.models (V018). The result lands in the agent's single output — a row, or list[Model] for list ; delete has none. Untyped where values are coerced to the column type. op Effect Reserved signals read read not_found list read — create , update , upsert write conflict delete destructive not_found use: http ¶ tool: use: http method: POST url: https://payments.example.com/refunds headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ${PAYMENTS_KEY}" } body: { order: "{{ order.id }}", amount: "{{ amount }}" } expect: { status: [200, 201] } map: { refund_ref: response.body.id } # response.status | headers | body paths → outputs idempotency: auto # auto | none — sends Idempotency-Key GET / HEAD are read ; other methods are write (override to destructive allowed). Without map , a single output receives the body. An unexpected status emits http_<status> when that signal is routed; otherwise error ( rate_limit for 429 and transient for 5xx are retryable, http_error otherwise). ${VAR} reads the environment. use: storage ¶ tool: { use: storage, store: invoices, op: put, key: "{{ id }}.pdf", body: "{{ pdf_b64 }}", encoding: base64 } tool: { use: storage, store: invoices, op: get, key: "{{ id }}.pdf", as: base64 } op : put , get , head , list , copy , delete , presign , on a store declared in storage/*.yaml (S3 and compatible services, Azure Blob, GCS, local disk). The result lands in the single output — the blob for put / head / copy , the content for get , the items for list , the URL for presign — or is spread by map . get , head and copy emit not_found ; put and copy emit conflict unless if_exists: overwrite ; delete is destructive. Object bytes are never journaled. Details: docs/storage.md . use: mcp ¶ tool: { use: mcp, server: artifact://zendesk@3, name: add_comment, args: { ticket: "{{ ticket.id }}", body: "{{ text }}" } } The effect comes from the server's readOnlyHint / destructiveHint , else write . The tool's structured content (or parsed text) fills a single output, or spreads an object across several. The tool's input schema is pinned in tuvl.lock . Each worker process keeps the MCP session open between calls, one per tenant and server (a stdio server is started once, not per call). A change to the server's artifact or to an environment variable it reads opens a new session; a session that dies is replaced on the next call. An unused session closes after TUVL_MCP_IDLE_SECONDS (default 300); 0 opens a new session for every call. Side effects and crashes ¶ Runs are at-least-once per agent ( runtime ). tool: db writes on the primary datasource commit with the step's checkpoint (exactly-once under transaction: per_agent ); HTTP calls get a stable Idempotency-Key ; MCP calls are at-least-once, so give write/destructive tools a compensate agent (V015). llm — one structured model call ¶ - id: reply description: Write the customer confirmation engine: llm inputs: { order: Order, refund: Refund } outputs: { text: str } budget: { timeout: 20s, max_tokens: 1500, retry: { attempts: 2, errors: [parse_error, timeout] } } llm: model: default # AgentModel name (type llm) or a provider/model id (see `docs/models.md`) system: artifact://support-voice@3 # text or a prompt artifact prompt: Write a short confirmation of the refund. skills: [artifact://refund-policy@2] guardrails: { output: [artifact://refund-reply-quality@2] } routes: { default: END, guardrail_violation: END.failed, error: END.failed, parse_error: END.failed, timeout: END.failed, budget_exceeded: END.failed } Every input is serialised into the prompt inside a <data name="…" type="…"> fence, and the system prompt tells the model that fenced text is data, never instructions. A value can't close its fence early ( </data> inside it is escaped), so retrieved documents, user text or web content can't pass themselves off as part of the prompt. loop agents fence every tool result the same way ( <data tool="…"> ). Text you interpolate into llm.prompt with {{ … }} is not fenced: pass untrusted values as inputs. The model answers with structured output whose schema is the agent's outputs . With more than one normal route, an outcome: enum[<those signals>] field is added and its value becomes the signal; a free-form model string can never become a signal. budget.max_tokens and budget.timeout are required (V011). Guardrails: input / output lists of guardrail or judge artifacts. A failing output judge emits guardrail_violation ; an unavailable or uncertain judge fails closed ( error ). Showing the answer while it is written. llm: { stream_tokens: true, stream_field: draft } sends the text of one str output to the run's event stream as the model produces it ( token_delta events, see API ), so a UI is not frozen for the length of the call. stream_field names the output; it can be left out when the agent has exactly one str output. The model still returns its normal structured answer: the result, its validation, tokens, retries and journal are unchanged, and the draft is only a preview. When the answer is then rejected ( parse_error , a cut-off budget_exceeded , an error in the stream) or the agent runs again, the client receives token_reset and discards the draft. Not allowed together with guardrails.output (V039): the text would reach a user before a guardrail could refuse it. A model that reasons before it answers sends nothing until its answer starts. Secure model fields can't be inputs unless policy.allow_secure_to_llm: true (V020). Remembering across runs ( llm.memory , loop.memory ) ¶ llm: model: gpt-4o-mini prompt: "Answer the customer: {{ question }}" memory: collection: support_memory # a kind: Collection that holds the memories key: principal # whose memory: principal (default) | tenant | "{{ some_input }}" window: 5 # the owner's latest memories handed to the agent recall_top_k: 3 # plus older ones related to the prompt max_tokens: 1000 # most recalled text in the prompt (about 4 characters a token) write: [question, answer] # inputs and outputs stored after a successful run; default: every output; [] only reads retention: 90d # optional: memories older than this are deleted by the runtime Before the call the owner's memories are added to the prompt under "Earlier context (from previous sessions)" inside a <data name="memory"> fence, and the model is told that text in <data> is data, never instructions. After a successful answer the write fields are stored (in the step's own transaction, once even if the step runs again). Journal events: memory_recalled (what was handed over) and memory_written . The owner is chosen in YAML, never by the model. A key templated from input on a public trigger is refused (V043): anyone could name another person's memory. A run with no owner fails with tool_args_invalid . write may name only fields of the agent, and never one that carries secure model fields (V043). max_tokens is added to the agent's worst-case tokens, so policy.max_tokens_per_run accounts for memory. retention deletes memories past that age, for every agent that names the collection (the shortest wins); the runtime sweeps every five minutes. Erase by hand with tuvl prune memory or the Memory page in Insight. Compaction. tuvl.memory_compact ( collection , model , keep : default 5, min_rows : default 20) is a built-in to run from a scheduled workflow: for each owner with more than min_rows memories it asks the model to fold all but the latest keep into one summary row (same owner, the time of the newest row it replaces) and deletes the originals in the same transaction. It writes the number of owners compacted to its one output and journals memory_compacted . A loop agent has the same block ( loop.memory ): the recalled text goes under the opening input, the same rules and journal events apply, and the write fields are stored when the loop finishes with a result. A loop that fails, waits for an approval or runs out of budget stores nothing. human — a person fills a form ¶ - id: approval description: A manager approves or rejects a refund engine: human inputs: { order: Order, message: str } outputs: { approved: bool, note: "str?" } # the form human: title: "Refund for order {{ order.id }}" instruction: Approve this refund? show: [order, message] # inputs shown to the reviewer form: # optional; defaults from outputs approved: { label: "Approve?", widget: toggle } note: { label: Note, widget: textarea } required_group: support_manager assignee: "{{ order.owner_id }}" expires: 48h route_on: approved # bool → "true"/"false"; enum → its values routes: { "true": issue_refund, "false": END.rejected, expired: END.failed, error: END.failed } The run checkpoints, opens an approval request and becomes waiting_human . A synchronous trigger answers 202 with the run descriptor and the request. Answer with POST /api/approvals/{id} { values } (or POST /api/runs/{run_id}/human/{agent_id} ). Values are validated against outputs ; the run is re-queued and continues on any worker. Who may answer: with required_group , a holder of approvals:decide in that group who is not the triggering principal; otherwise the triggering principal or iam:admin . iam:admin bypasses the group, never the no-self-approval rule. expires closes the request and takes the expired route; a late answer gets 409 . form fields must equal outputs ; route_on must be a bool or enum output (V016). In tests, an unmocked human agent stops the run: assert it with expect.wait: human . map — a workflow for every item of a list ¶ - id: score_each description: Score every candidate engine: map inputs: { candidates: "list[json]", job_id: uuid } outputs: { scores: "list[json]" } # one list: the results, in input order map: over: candidates # an input that is a list workflow: score_candidate # the child workflow, run once per item as: candidate # the child's trigger input that receives the item (default: item) with: { job_id: "{{ job_id }}" } # further child inputs, templates over this agent's inputs concurrency: 4 # items in flight (1-32, default 4) max_items: 100 # longer lists fail the agent before any item starts (default 100) on_error: collect # fail (default) | collect effect: write # the strongest effect of the child; never weaker (V015) routes: { default: rank, partial: review, error: END.failed } Fan-out and nothing else: tuvl runs the child workflow once per item, a few at a time, and gathers the results. The step is one agent of the parent; each item is a child run of its own. Each item is a run. It has its own journal, checkpoints and cost, shows in the run list with parent_run_id set, and is replayable on its own. The step journals map_started , one map_item per item, and map_finished . Idempotent after a crash. The child of item i is keyed <agent>:<i> . A parent that is reclaimed by another worker and reaches the step again follows the children already started (or finished) instead of starting new ones, so no item runs twice. Success is per item. An item succeeds when its child completes on an end whose status is below 400; its result is that end's body . The result list keeps the input order. on_error: fail stops starting new items at the first failed item and emits error ( map_item_failed : which item, why, and how many failed or never started). Items already running finish; their runs stay in the journal. on_error: collect runs every item. A failed item is null in the results, and the agent emits partial instead of default when the workflow routes partial (otherwise default ). partial is only valid with collect (V004). A mapped workflow must finish on its own (V036): no human or pending agent and no loop tool that needs approval. A child that waits anyway fails its item. Bounded. concurrency limits parallel items, max_items the list length, and policy.max_depth how deeply workflows nest (a workflow cannot map itself, V035). Worst-case tokens in tuvl lint project are the child's worst case times max_items , and the step takes the child's strongest determinism class. Checks (V035): over is a list input; the workflow exists; as and every with key are inputs of the child; no required child input is left out; item and input types agree (V007); outputs is exactly one list (V007). Items run in this worker's process, in parallel; another worker takes over only through crash recovery. Nothing is shared between items: they are independent runs, so a map is not a fork/join of different branches, only the same workflow over many items. parallel — different read-only lookups at the same time ¶ - id: gather description: Look the customer up in three places at once engine: parallel inputs: { customer_id: uuid, name: str } outputs: { profile: json, hit: bool, notes: "list[json]" } # exactly the branches' outputs together parallel: on_error: fail # fail (default) | collect concurrency: 3 # branches in flight (default: all) branches: # 2-16 agents; each reads its `inputs` from this step's inputs - id: crm engine: tool inputs: { customer_id: uuid } outputs: { profile: json } tool: { use: db, model: Customer, op: read, where: { id: "{{ customer_id }}" } } - id: sanctions engine: tool inputs: { name: str } outputs: { hit: bool } tool: { use: http, method: GET, url: "https://screening.example/check?q={{ name }}", map: { hit: response.body.hit } } - id: knowledge engine: llm inputs: { name: str } outputs: { notes: "list[json]" } llm: { model: gpt-4o-mini, prompt: "List what we know about {{ name }}" } budget: { max_tokens: 800, timeout: 20s } budget: { timeout: 30s } routes: { default: decide, error: END.failed } The step takes about as long as its slowest branch instead of the sum. It is one agent of the workflow: one checkpoint, one route, one place in the journal. Branches only read (V040). A branch is a tool (db read / list , http GET / HEAD , storage reads), an llm , or a code agent with effect: read . Writes, destructive tools and MCP tools (their effect is unknown until listed) belong in a step of their own; so do loop , human , decide , map and a nested parallel . A session of its own. Each branch runs in its own database session with the idempotency key <step key>:<branch id> ; transaction: per_run is refused (V042). Outputs. The step's outputs are all branches' outputs together; no name twice, nothing left over (V041). A branch ends on default ; anything else is a failure. on_error: fail stops the branches still running at the first failure and emits error ( parallel_branch_failed , naming the branch). collect lets every branch finish; a failed branch's outputs are null (declare them optional), and the step emits partial when the workflow routes it, default otherwise. Timeout. budget.timeout is for the whole step; when it passes, every branch is cancelled and the step emits timeout . Journal. parallel_started , one parallel_branch per branch in the order they finish (ok, ms, tokens, reason), parallel_finished . A branch's own events ( tool_call , llm_turn , ...) carry branch in the payload. Cost. The worst-case tokens of a step are the sum of its branches' max_tokens ; its determinism class is its strongest branch's. Crash. A step is checkpointed when it completes, so a crash in the middle runs the whole step again; the branch keys make repeating a read or a model call safe. Offline tests. tuvl run tests runs the step when every branch is mocked ( mocks.crm , mocks.sanctions , ...) and names the first branch that is not; mock the step itself ( mocks.gather ) to skip its branches. Codegen. tuvl generate code writes stubs for code branches like any other code agent.
