Recall returns the owner's last window memories (default 5, 0-50) and up to top_k older ones most related to query (default 3, 0-20), as [{content, source: recent | related, at | score}] , older context first. The step journals memory_recalled with the text it handed to the agent. Remember stores text (embedded) with the owner, run and agent in its metadata. A step that runs again after a crash stores it once. What to store is the author's choice: store the agent's answer or a summary, never a secure field. Treat recalled text as data, not instructions (an earlier user wrote it): put it in the prompt inside a labelled block, as tool results are. Erase with tuvl prune memory <collection> --key <owner> ; expire with --older-than 30d . In tests, mock them by agent id like any code agent.
docs.title: code — a Python function

docs.text: One engine, four use variants. The effect is derived ; a declared effect may only strengthen it (V015), except that an HTTP POST / PUT / PATCH may declare effect: read (search APIs often read via POST).
docs.title: tool — database, HTTP, MCP and storage operations

docs.text: tool: { use: db, model: Order, op: read, where: { id: "{{ order_id }}" } } tool: { use: db, model: Refund, op: create, values: { order_id: "{{ order.id }}", amount: "{{ amount }}" } } tool: { use: db, model: Ticket, op: list, where: { status: open }, order_by: [-created_at], limit: 20 } op : create , read , update , delete , list , upsert . The model must be in spec.models (V018). The result lands in the agent's single output — a row, or list[Model] for list ; delete has none. Untyped where values are coerced to the column type. op Effect Reserved signals read read not_found list read — create , update , upsert write conflict delete destructive not_found
docs.title: use: db

docs.text: tool: use: http method: POST url: https://payments.example.com/refunds headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ${PAYMENTS_KEY}" } body: { order: "{{ order.id }}", amount: "{{ amount }}" } expect: { status: [200, 201] } map: { refund_ref: response.body.id } # response.status | headers | body paths → outputs idempotency: auto # auto | none — sends Idempotency-Key GET / HEAD are read ; other methods are write (override to destructive allowed). Without map , a single output receives the body. An unexpected status emits http_<status> when that signal is routed; otherwise error ( rate_limit for 429 and transient for 5xx are retryable, http_error otherwise). ${VAR} reads the environment.
docs.title: use: http

docs.text: tool: { use: storage, store: invoices, op: put, key: "{{ id }}.pdf", body: "{{ pdf_b64 }}", encoding: base64 } tool: { use: storage, store: invoices, op: get, key: "{{ id }}.pdf", as: base64 } op : put , get , head , list , copy , delete , presign , on a store declared in storage/*.yaml (S3 and compatible services, Azure Blob, GCS, local disk). The result lands in the single output — the blob for put / head / copy , the content for get , the items for list , the URL for presign — or is spread by map . get , head and copy emit not_found ; put and copy emit conflict unless if_exists: overwrite ; delete is destructive. Object bytes are never journaled. Details: docs/storage.md .
docs.title: use: storage

docs.text: tool: { use: mcp, server: artifact://zendesk@3, name: add_comment, args: { ticket: "{{ ticket.id }}", body: "{{ text }}" } } The effect comes from the server's readOnlyHint / destructiveHint , else write . The tool's structured content (or parsed text) fills a single output, or spreads an object across several. The tool's input schema is pinned in tuvl.lock . Each worker process keeps the MCP session open between calls, one per tenant and server (a stdio server is started once, not per call). A change to the server's artifact or to an environment variable it reads opens a new session; a session that dies is replaced on the next call. An unused session closes after TUVL_MCP_IDLE_SECONDS (default 300); 0 opens a new session for every call.
docs.title: use: mcp

docs.text: Runs are at-least-once per agent ( runtime ). tool: db writes on the primary datasource commit with the step's checkpoint (exactly-once under transaction: per_agent ); HTTP calls get a stable Idempotency-Key ; MCP calls are at-least-once, so give write/destructive tools a compensate agent (V015).
docs.title: Side effects and crashes

docs.text: - id: reply description: Write the customer confirmation engine: llm inputs: { order: Order, refund: Refund } outputs: { text: str } budget: { timeout: 20s, max_tokens: 1500, retry: { attempts: 2, errors: [parse_error, timeout] } } llm: model: default # AgentModel name (type llm) or a provider/model id (see `docs/models.md`) system: artifact://support-voice@3 # text or a prompt artifact prompt: Write a short confirmation of the refund. skills: [artifact://refund-policy@2] guardrails: { output: [artifact://refund-reply-quality@2] } routes: { default: END, guardrail_violation: END.failed, error: END.failed, parse_error: END.failed, timeout: END.failed, budget_exceeded: END.failed } Every input is serialised into the prompt inside a <data name="…" type="…"> fence, and the system prompt tells the model that fenced text is data, never instructions. A value can't close its fence early ( </data> inside it is escaped), so retrieved documents, user text or web content can't pass themselves off as part of the prompt. loop agents fence every tool result the same way ( <data tool="…"> ). Text you interpolate into llm.prompt with {{ … }} is not fenced: pass untrusted values as inputs. The model answers with structured output whose schema is the agent's outputs . With more than one normal route, an outcome: enum[<those signals>] field is added and its value becomes the signal; a free-form model string can never become a signal. budget.max_tokens and budget.timeout are required (V011). Guardrails: input / output lists of guardrail or judge artifacts. A failing output judge emits guardrail_violation ; an unavailable or uncertain judge fails closed ( error ). Showing the answer while it is written. llm: { stream_tokens: true, stream_field: draft } sends the text of one str output to the run's event stream as the model produces it ( token_delta events, see API ), so a UI is not frozen for the length of the call. stream_field names the output; it can be left out when the agent has exactly one str output. The model still returns its normal structured answer: the result, its validation, tokens, retries and journal are unchanged, and the draft is only a preview. When the answer is then rejected ( parse_error , a cut-off budget_exceeded , an error in the stream) or the agent runs again, the client receives token_reset and discards the draft. Not allowed together with guardrails.output (V039): the text would reach a user before a guardrail could refuse it. A model that reasons before it answers sends nothing until its answer starts. Secure model fields can't be inputs unless policy.allow_secure_to_llm: true (V020).
docs.title: llm — one structured model call

docs.text: llm: model: gpt-4o-mini prompt: "Answer the customer: {{ question }}" memory: collection: support_memory # a kind: Collection that holds the memories key: principal # whose memory: principal (default) | tenant | "{{ some_input }}" window: 5 # the owner's latest memories handed to the agent recall_top_k: 3 # plus older ones related to the prompt max_tokens: 1000 # most recalled text in the prompt (about 4 characters a token) write: [question, answer] # inputs and outputs stored after a successful run; default: every output; [] only reads retention: 90d # optional: memories older than this are deleted by the runtime Before the call the owner's memories are added to the prompt under "Earlier context (from previous sessions)" inside a <data name="memory"> fence, and the model is told that text in <data> is data, never instructions. After a successful answer the write fields are stored (in the step's own transaction, once even if the step runs again). Journal events: memory_recalled (what was handed over) and memory_written . The owner is chosen in YAML, never by the model. A key templated from input on a public trigger is refused (V043): anyone could name another person's memory. A run with no owner fails with tool_args_invalid . write may name only fields of the agent, and never one that carries secure model fields (V043). max_tokens is added to the agent's worst-case tokens, so policy.max_tokens_per_run accounts for memory. retention deletes memories past that age, for every agent that names the collection (the shortest wins); the runtime sweeps every five minutes. Erase by hand with tuvl prune memory or the Memory page in Insight. Compaction. tuvl.memory_compact ( collection , model , keep : default 5, min_rows : default 20) is a built-in to run from a scheduled workflow: for each owner with more than min_rows memories it asks the model to fold all but the latest keep into one summary row (same owner, the time of the newest row it replaces) and deletes the originals in the same transaction. It writes the number of owners compacted to its one output and journals memory_compacted . A loop agent has the same block ( loop.memory ): the recalled text goes under the opening input, the same rules and journal events apply, and the write fields are stored when the loop finishes with a result. A loop that fails, waits for an approval or runs out of budget stores nothing.
docs.title: Remembering across runs (llm.memory, loop.memory)

docs.text: - id: approval description: A manager approves or rejects a refund engine: human inputs: { order: Order, message: str } outputs: { approved: bool, note: "str?" } # the form human: title: "Refund for order {{ order.id }}" instruction: Approve this refund? show: [order, message] # inputs shown to the reviewer form: # optional; defaults from outputs approved: { label: "Approve?", widget: toggle } note: { label: Note, widget: textarea } required_group: support_manager assignee: "{{ order.owner_id }}" expires: 48h route_on: approved # bool → "true"/"false"; enum → its values routes: { "true": issue_refund, "false": END.rejected, expired: END.failed, error: END.failed } The run checkpoints, opens an approval request and becomes waiting_human . A synchronous trigger answers 202 with the run descriptor and the request. Answer with POST /api/approvals/{id} { values } (or POST /api/runs/{run_id}/human/{agent_id} ). Values are validated against outputs ; the run is re-queued and continues on any worker. Who may answer: with required_group , a holder of approvals:decide in that group who is not the triggering principal; otherwise the triggering principal or iam:admin . iam:admin bypasses the group, never the no-self-approval rule. expires closes the request and takes the expired route; a late answer gets 409 . form fields must equal outputs ; route_on must be a bool or enum output (V016). In tests, an unmocked human agent stops the run: assert it with expect.wait: human .
docs.title: human — a person fills a form

docs.text: - id: score_each description: Score every candidate engine: map inputs: { candidates: "list[json]", job_id: uuid } outputs: { scores: "list[json]" } # one list: the results, in input order map: over: candidates # an input that is a list workflow: score_candidate # the child workflow, run once per item as: candidate # the child's trigger input that receives the item (default: item) with: { job_id: "{{ job_id }}" } # further child inputs, templates over this agent's inputs concurrency: 4 # items in flight (1-32, default 4) max_items: 100 # longer lists fail the agent before any item starts (default 100) on_error: collect # fail (default) | collect effect: write # the strongest effect of the child; never weaker (V015) routes: { default: rank, partial: review, error: END.failed } Fan-out and nothing else: tuvl runs the child workflow once per item, a few at a time, and gathers the results. The step is one agent of the parent; each item is a child run of its own. Each item is a run. It has its own journal, checkpoints and cost, shows in the run list with parent_run_id set, and is replayable on its own. The step journals map_started , one map_item per item, and map_finished . Idempotent after a crash. The child of item i is keyed <agent>:<i> . A parent that is reclaimed by another worker and reaches the step again follows the children already started (or finished) instead of starting new ones, so no item runs twice. Success is per item. An item succeeds when its child completes on an end whose status is below 400; its result is that end's body . The result list keeps the input order. on_error: fail stops starting new items at the first failed item and emits error ( map_item_failed : which item, why, and how many failed or never started). Items already running finish; their runs stay in the journal. on_error: collect runs every item. A failed item is null in the results, and the agent emits partial instead of default when the workflow routes partial (otherwise default ). partial is only valid with collect (V004). A mapped workflow must finish on its own (V036): no human or pending agent and no loop tool that needs approval. A child that waits anyway fails its item. Bounded. concurrency limits parallel items, max_items the list length, and policy.max_depth how deeply workflows nest (a workflow cannot map itself, V035). Worst-case tokens in tuvl lint project are the child's worst case times max_items , and the step takes the child's strongest determinism class. Checks (V035): over is a list input; the workflow exists; as and every with key are inputs of the child; no required child input is left out; item and input types agree (V007); outputs is exactly one list (V007). Items run in this worker's process, in parallel; another worker takes over only through crash recovery. Nothing is shared between items: they are independent runs, so a map is not a fork/join of different branches, only the same workflow over many items.
docs.title: map — a workflow for every item of a list

docs.text: - id: gather description: Look the customer up in three places at once engine: parallel inputs: { customer_id: uuid, name: str } outputs: { profile: json, hit: bool, notes: "list[json]" } # exactly the branches' outputs together parallel: on_error: fail # fail (default) | collect concurrency: 3 # branches in flight (default: all) branches: # 2-16 agents; each reads its `inputs` from this step's inputs - id: crm engine: tool inputs: { customer_id: uuid } outputs: { profile: json } tool: { use: db, model: Customer, op: read, where: { id: "{{ customer_id }}" } } - id: sanctions engine: tool inputs: { name: str } outputs: { hit: bool } tool: { use: http, method: GET, url: "https://screening.example/check?q={{ name }}", map: { hit: response.body.hit } } - id: knowledge engine: llm inputs: { name: str } outputs: { notes: "list[json]" } llm: { model: gpt-4o-mini, prompt: "List what we know about {{ name }}" } budget: { max_tokens: 800, timeout: 20s } budget: { timeout: 30s } routes: { default: decide, error: END.failed } The step takes about as long as its slowest branch instead of the sum. It is one agent of the workflow: one checkpoint, one route, one place in the journal. Branches only read (V040). A branch is a tool (db read / list , http GET / HEAD , storage reads), an llm , or a code agent with effect: read . Writes, destructive tools and MCP tools (their effect is unknown until listed) belong in a step of their own; so do loop , human , decide , map and a nested parallel . A session of its own. Each branch runs in its own database session with the idempotency key <step key>:<branch id> ; transaction: per_run is refused (V042). Outputs. The step's outputs are all branches' outputs together; no name twice, nothing left over (V041). A branch ends on default ; anything else is a failure. on_error: fail stops the branches still running at the first failure and emits error ( parallel_branch_failed , naming the branch). collect lets every branch finish; a failed branch's outputs are null (declare them optional), and the step emits partial when the workflow routes it, default otherwise. Timeout. budget.timeout is for the whole step; when it passes, every branch is cancelled and the step emits timeout . Journal. parallel_started , one parallel_branch per branch in the order they finish (ok, ms, tokens, reason), parallel_finished . A branch's own events ( tool_call , llm_turn , ...) carry branch in the payload. Cost. The worst-case tokens of a step are the sum of its branches' max_tokens ; its determinism class is its strongest branch's. Crash. A step is checkpointed when it completes, so a crash in the middle runs the whole step again; the branch keys make repeating a read or a model call safe. Offline tests. tuvl run tests runs the step when every branch is mocked ( mocks.crm , mocks.sanctions , ...) and names the first branch that is not; mock the step itself ( mocks.gather ) to skip its branches. Codegen. tuvl generate code writes stubs for code branches like any other code agent.
docs.title: parallel — different read-only lookups at the same time

docs.text: Insight ¶ Insight is tuvl's browser editor for a project. It reads and writes the same files the CLI does, so anything you do in it is a change to YAML in git, and anything you change in git shows up in it. Specs, tasks, the workflow canvas, runs, models and settings are in one place. tuvl dev --auto-login # Insight at http://localhost:8885/insight (needs tuvl[standard]) It is a development tool: a production server ( tuvl serve app ) has no Insight and no dev routes. On a terminal tuvl dev also starts a terminal UI that runs the same commands. Pages ¶ Page What you do there Specs A tile per spec with its status. Open a spec to read it, see its Findings (the rules tuvl lint spec applies) and Traceability (step, agent, tests), approve, send back or reopen it, derive its tasks, and open a task in a panel you can drag and pop out. Graph draws the tasks in execution order; a blocked task says why Ideas The numbered, immutable ideas of the project and the specs generated from each. Upload idea takes files, a folder, links (a web page, Jira issue, Confluence page or GitHub issue) or pasted text and makes what tuvl import idea makes. Generate a spec with my agent runs tuvl generate spec --idea with the coding agent you selected, after asking for consent the first time Workflows A canvas over the workflow YAML (the YAML toggle shows the file itself). + Add step (or A ) adds an agent from a palette of presets, including Retrieve and answer , which adds a collection search routed into an answering model. Select an agent to edit it in the side panel; run a workflow with breakpoints and step mode, and check a change of engine before applying it Runs Every run with its journal, cost and approvals, live over SSE Artifacts Prompts, steering, skills, guardrails, hooks, MCP servers, judges and decision tables, with their versions and what uses them Models Data models: fields, relations, access and the CRUD operations exposed AI Models The model presets ( llms/ ) agents refer to as model: default , with provider and key variable Embeddings , Collections The vector search setup that tuvl.data_search , tuvl.data_ingest and a loop's collection: tool use. A banner appears when pgvector is not available Memory What agents remember across runs, per collection: the owners, each memory with the agent and run that wrote it, a filter by owner, and Forget for one memory or (after a second click) everything of one owner. Reads and deletes through the dev API; tuvl prune memory does the same from the command line Datasources , Storage PostgreSQL, Redis and blob stores; a store can be checked (write, read back, delete a probe object) and its objects browsed from the page IAM , Federation Users, roles, scopes and groups; Google, GitHub, Microsoft or custom sign-in providers API Docs The OpenAPI generated from your workflows' contracts Audit The local audit ledger and, when developer telemetry is on, the Team view of what everyone did Settings API access (which routes the production server exposes), developer telemetry, the project's identity and its listing in Nest The agent panel ¶ Selecting an agent on the canvas opens a panel with these tabs: Tab Holds Engine (named Rules , Prompt , Loop , Tool , Approval by engine) The engine's own settings. An llm or loop agent also has Remember across runs : the memory collection, whose memory (the signed-in user, the tenant or an input), how many recent and related memories, the prompt budget, what is stored and how long it is kept. An llm or loop agent picks its AI model from the configured presets (or types a provider/model id), and writes its system prompt, prompt or steering in place or takes it from a stored artifact pinned to a version; skills, MCP servers and collections it may search are listed here too. A tuvl.data_search or tuvl.data_ingest step picks its collection Contract The agent's typed inputs and outputs Routes Where each signal goes Budget Tokens, time and iterations Probe Run this one agent alone, live, with inputs you type (an llm or loop agent spends real tokens; save the workflow first) YAML The whole agent as it is in the workflow file, editable; its id cannot change here because routes point at it Governance Effect, guardrails, hooks and the compensating agent A code agent also has a Code tab with the Python of its function. What Insight does not do ¶ It does not hold state of its own: close it and nothing is lost, because everything is in the files. It does not run in production, and it cannot see a deployed server's data. It spends tokens only where you ask a model or a coding agent to: checking a spec, deriving tasks and linting are free.

docs.text: Judges ¶ A judge is a versioned type: judge artifact: a model, a rubric and a fixed verdict set, with a labelled calibration set. One primitive serves output guardrails, tests, loop supervisors and Insight. kind: Artifact metadata: { name: refund-reply-quality, version: 2 } spec: type: judge model: default # AgentModel or provider/model id; pinned in tuvl.lock rubric: | The reply must state the refund amount and timeline and must not promise anything outside the refund policy. verdict: [pass, fail, uncertain] min_score: 0.8 # a pass scoring below this becomes fail calibration: - { input: fixtures/judge/reply_ok.json, expect: pass } - { input: fixtures/judge/reply_overpromise.json, expect: fail } min_agreement: 0.9 A verdict is always { verdict, score, reasons } . Where judges run ¶ Site On fail On uncertain or judge unavailable guardrails.output (llm, loop) guardrail_violation Fails closed: error ( judge_unavailable / judge_uncertain ) Test.expect.judge The test fails The test fails ( tuvl run tests --allow-uncertain relaxes it) Loop supervisor.judge on_violation (pause / abort / steer) on_judge_error (ignore / pause / abort); rules still apply # in a Test expect: judge: - { judge: artifact://refund-reply-quality@2, target: "{{ text }}" } Rules ¶ Deterministic checks first. end , path , decisions , output and TEL assertions run before any judge. Prefer a TEL assertion over a judge wherever the check is exact. Verdict cache. Verdicts are cached in .tuvl/judge-cache/ by subject, judge version and content hash, so CI re-runs are deterministic and free. Commit the cache to share it. Calibration. tuvl run tests runs each judge's calibration set before first use. Agreement below min_agreement marks its verdicts untrusted (V023 warning; tuvl run tests --strict fails). Pinned. The judge's model is recorded in tuvl.lock . Building the calibration set in Insight ¶ On the Artifacts page, a judge opens in an editor: model, rubric and thresholds, a Try tab and a Calibration tab. Paste a subject (JSON) and Ask the judge — this calls the model live, using the unsaved draft. Mark the verdict ✓ right or ✗ wrong with a label: the subject is saved to fixtures/judge/<label>.json and appended to calibration with the expected verdict. Run calibration to see agreement against min_agreement . Dev API: POST /dev/judges/try , /dev/judges/label , /dev/judges/calibrate .

docs.text: The loop engine and tools ¶ A loop agent gives a model a set of tools and lets it work toward an outcome within hard budgets. Tools are other agents, other workflows, or allow-listed MCP tools; their schemas are derived from contracts, never hand-written. - id: resolve_ticket description: Resolve a support ticket using the available tools engine: loop inputs: { ticket: Ticket } outputs: { resolution: str } budget: { max_iterations: 8, max_tokens: 40000, max_tool_calls: 12, timeout: 2m } # all required loop: model: default steering: artifact://support-steering@4 # text or a steering artifact skills: [artifact://refund-policy@2] tools: - agent: lookup_order # off-spine agent in this workflow - workflow: issue_refund # another workflow as a child run approval: { when: "args.amount > 200", required_group: support_manager } - collection: kb_docs # search a collection (read-only) top_k: 3 - mcp: artifact://zendesk@3 allow: [add_comment, set_status] # required allow-list max_calls: 3 supervisor: { rules: [...], judge: artifact://resolution-judge@1 } guardrails: { tools: [artifact://no-secrets-in-observations@1] } routes: { resolved: reply, escalate: human_queue, error: ops_alert, max_iterations: human_queue, budget_exceeded: human_queue, timeout: human_queue, aborted: ops_alert } Tool sources ¶ Source Schema Execution agent: <id> The agent's inputs → parameters, description → tool description The runner executes that agent with the model's arguments; its own routes are ignored workflow: <name> The workflow's trigger.input and description A child run with its own journal, gates and budget; its tokens count toward the parent's max_tokens ; nesting capped by policy.max_depth (default 2) collection: <name> One parameter, query (a string). The tool is named search_<collection> , or name: when given The same hybrid search as tuvl.data_search , with top_k (default 5), filter and scope fixed in the YAML, not chosen by the model; returns {passages: [{content, metadata, score}]} . It is a read, so it needs no approval; tuvl lint project checks that the collection is defined mcp: artifact://x The server's tools/list , filtered by allow Through the artifact's connection; each allowed tool's schema hash is pinned in tuvl.lock The model's arguments are validated against the tool's schema before execution; invalid arguments return to the model as an error observation ( tool_args_invalid ) and count as an iteration. Tool results stay inside the loop — only the declared outputs reach the run context. Per-tool governance ¶ Field Meaning approval required , or { when: <TEL over args>, required_group? } — the loop pauses at that call max_calls Per-tool cap, on top of budget.max_tool_calls Each tool's effect is derived (the agent's, the child workflow's strongest, or the MCP hints) and shown to the model and in Insight. Write/destructive MCP calls are at-least-once; V015 asks for an approval or compensate . Calls in the same turn ¶ When a model turn asks for several MCP tools that are marked readOnlyHint and need no approval, they run at the same time: the turn takes about as long as the slowest. Events and the transcript keep the order the model asked in, and budget.max_tool_calls and max_calls are counted as before. Writes, approvals, and agent, workflow and collection tools still run one at a time (they share the run's database session). In-loop approval ¶ The model requests a call that matches approval . The runner journals the full loop state and the pending call, and the run becomes waiting_approval . An approver ( approvals:decide , plus the tool's required_group ) sees the exact arguments and approves , edits them (re-validated) or rejects with a message: POST /api/approvals/{id} { decision: approve | edit | reject, edited_args?, message? } . The run is re-queued; approve/edit executes the call, reject returns the rejection to the model. Outcome ¶ The final turn must return the outputs schema plus outcome: enum[<normal route keys>] ; the outcome is the signal. A bad parse gets one repair attempt, then error ( parse_error ). Budgets end the loop with max_iterations , budget_exceeded or timeout ; the supervisor or an operator abort ends it with aborted . Supervisor ¶ spec.supervisor applies to every loop agent unless the agent sets loop.supervisor . supervisor: rules: - { when: tool_repeated, count: 3 } # same call, same args, N times (optional tool:) - { when: budget_fraction, gt: 0.8 } # a budget more than 80 % used - { when: iteration_reached, gte: 6 } - { when: effect_count, effect: write, count: 3 } # more than N write calls judge: artifact://resolution-judge@1 # evaluates the trajectory every_n_iterations: 1 on_violation: pause # abort | pause | steer on_judge_error: ignore # ignore | pause | abort steer_message: Stop repeating lookups; decide with what you have. The supervisor reads the journal and writes control flags on the run record, so it works across workers. A pause waits for an operator ( POST /api/runs/{id}/resume ); steer injects a message (operators can also steer with POST /api/runs/{id}/steer ). Guardrails ¶ guardrails.tools lists guardrail / judge artifacts applied to tool observations before the model sees them; guardrails.output checks the final result ( guardrail_violation ).

docs.text: Models and providers ¶ tuvl calls language models and embedding models through its own HTTP client ( tuvl.llm ). A model is named provider/model ; a bare id ( gpt-4o ) is an OpenAI model. kind: AgentModel metadata: { name: default } spec: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 api_key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY} temperature: 0.2 max_tokens: 1024 timeout: 60 Built-in providers ¶ Provider Id prefix Key variable Endpoint OpenAI openai/ OPENAI_API_KEY https://api.openai.com/v1 Anthropic anthropic/ ANTHROPIC_API_KEY https://api.anthropic.com (Messages API) Google Gemini gemini/ GEMINI_API_KEY https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai Azure OpenAI azure/<deployment> AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY $AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT/openai/v1 Amazon Bedrock bedrock/<model id> AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK https://bedrock-runtime.$AWS_REGION.amazonaws.com/openai/v1 Google Vertex AI vertex_ai/google/<model> VERTEX_ACCESS_TOKEN https://<location>-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/locations/<location>/endpoints/openapi Cohere cohere/ COHERE_API_KEY https://api.cohere.ai/compatibility/v1 Voyage AI (embeddings only) voyage/ VOYAGE_API_KEY https://api.voyageai.com/v1 Ollama ollama/ , ollama_chat/ none OLLAMA_BASE_URL ( http://localhost:11434 ) Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI groq/ , mistral/ , deepseek/ , xai/ <NAME>_API_KEY provider default OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks, Perplexity openrouter/ , together_ai/ , fireworks_ai/ , perplexity/ OPENROUTER_API_KEY , TOGETHERAI_API_KEY , FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY , PERPLEXITYAI_API_KEY provider default LiteLLM proxy / any gateway litellm_proxy/<alias> LITELLM_API_KEY your api_base (required) LM Studio, vLLM lm_studio/ , vllm/ , hosted_vllm/ none http://localhost:1234/v1 , http://localhost:8000/v1 api_key on the AgentModel wins over the variable; it must be an ${ENV_VAR} reference. api_base overrides the endpoint. tuvl check system lists the variables each model needs. Cloud providers ¶ These use each vendor's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so no cloud SDK is installed. Azure OpenAI uses the v1 API ( /openai/v1 , no api-version ). The model is your deployment name : azure/my-gpt4o . Authenticate with the resource's API key; Microsoft Entra tokens are not fetched for you. Amazon Bedrock uses the bedrock-runtime OpenAI endpoint with a Bedrock API key ( AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK ) and a region ( AWS_REGION ). Only models whose Bedrock model card lists the Chat Completions API work; SigV4 / IAM-role credentials are not supported. Vertex AI uses the OpenAI endpoint of your project ( GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT , location from GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION , default us-central1 ; global selects the global host). The key is a Google access token such as gcloud auth print-access-token , which expires after about an hour — for a long-running service refresh it into VERTEX_ACCESS_TOKEN or put a gateway in front. Cohere uses its compatibility API. Structured output is sent as Cohere's {"type": "json_object", "schema": …} ; embeddings take no dimensions field. Voyage AI serves embeddings only (the output size is sent as output_dimension ). Endpoints and request shapes follow the vendors' documentation (checked 2026-10-17). Ollama is the only provider exercised against a live service in tuvl's own tests; run tuvl check system --live against yours before relying on one. Any other endpoint ¶ Anything that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions API works with api_base : spec: model: acme/my-model # any prefix; the part after "/" is sent as the model api_base: https://llm.example.com/v1 api_key: ${ACME_API_KEY} A provider with its own wire format and no OpenAI-compatible endpoint (SageMaker, watsonx, Hugging Face, Replicate) needs a gateway in front. Through a LiteLLM proxy or other gateway ¶ A LiteLLM proxy serves the OpenAI API, so tuvl reaches everything litellm supports through it, with the provider keys and routing kept on the proxy. The model is the alias from the proxy's model_list : kind: AgentModel metadata: { name: gateway } spec: model: litellm_proxy/my-claude # or openai/my-claude api_base: ${LITELLM_PROXY_URL} # e.g. http://litellm.internal:4000/v1 api_key: ${LITELLM_API_KEY} Embeddings take the same two fields: kind: EmbeddingRegistry spec: embeddings: - name: gateway-embed model: litellm_proxy/embed-alias dimensions: 1024 api_base: ${LITELLM_PROXY_URL} api_key: ${LITELLM_API_KEY} Structured output, tool calls and logprobs behave as the model behind the proxy does. Each call is one extra network hop to a service you run. What the client does ¶ Chat completions with structured output ( json_schema ), tool calls and token logprobs (where the provider offers them). Anthropic structured output is a forced tool call; Anthropic has no logprobs, so decision confidence comes from the model's reported value. Embeddings on any OpenAI-compatible endpoint ( openai/text-embedding-3-small , gemini/gemini-embedding-001 , ollama/nomic-embed-text , cohere/embed-v4.0 , voyage/voyage-3 ). Failures are classified as timeout , rate_limit (HTTP 429), transient (connection errors, 5xx) or llm_error , which is what a step's retry.errors matches. The client does not retry by itself. Streaming: tuvl.llm.astream(...) takes the arguments of acompletion and yields TextDelta events while the model writes, then one StreamEnd carrying the same Completion a plain call returns (so token counts and finish reason match). A structured response streams as pieces of the JSON text. timeout is the longest silence between chunks, not the whole call. A model that "thinks" before it answers streams nothing until its answer starts. One OpenTelemetry span per call; see observability . tuvl check system lists the variables each model needs; tuvl check system --live makes one minimal call per model.

docs.text: Observability — Structured Logging & OpenTelemetry ¶ tuvl ships enterprise-grade observability out of the box: structured JSON logging via structlog and distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry (OTel). Both are active in production and automatically disabled in dev mode. Table of Contents ¶ Architecture Overview Structured Logging Distributed Tracing Span Hierarchy Model-call spans Metrics Configuration Reference Collector Setup Dev Mode Behaviour Data Masking & PII 1. Architecture Overview ¶ trigger (HTTP / API / MCP / schedule / child run) │ FastAPI HTTP span (W3C traceparent propagated) ▼ tuvl.run one span per execution of a run (each claim: start, resume) ├── tuvl.agent <id> one per agent invocation │ └── chat <model> gen_ai.* spans for model calls (llm, loop turns, decide models, judges) └── tuvl.agent <id> … Two complementary records: The journal ( tuvl_system_run_events ) is the authoritative, durable record of what a run did — every agent start/finish, signal, model turn, tool call, decision, judge verdict, approval and pause. It drives the Insight Runs page, GET /api/runs/{id}/events (SSE), tuvl follow run , replay and test fixtures. See runtime . OpenTelemetry spans and structured logs feed your tracing and log backends, correlated by trace_id / span_id and run_id . 2. Structured Logging ¶ tuvl logs with structlog: JSON lines in production, a readable console format in development. Log format — production ¶ { "event": "Workflow execution started", "level": "info", "logger": "tuvl.core.engine.runner", "timestamp": "2026-05-26T10:00:00.000000Z", "workflow": "recruitment-pipeline", "trace_id": "4a8f3e...", "span_id": "8b2c1d..." } Log format — development ( TUVL_ENV=development ) ¶ 2026-05-26T10:00:00Z [info ] Workflow execution started workflow=recruitment-pipeline trace_id=4a8f3e... Key log events ¶ Event Level Fields runtime.started info role , agents , triggers , mcp_tools , workflows runtime.worker.started info worker id, concurrency runtime.trigger.mounted info workflow , method , path runtime.mcp.mounted info tools runtime.lease.lost warning the run moved to another worker runtime.pause_ignored warning pause requested on a per_run transaction decide.shadow_model_failed warning agent , error (shadow failures never fail the run) decision.provider.load_failed warning a decision provider entry point failed to load judge.cache_write_failed warning read-only checkout; verdicts still computed mcp.schema_drift warning a live MCP tool schema differs from tuvl.lock (once per tool) Per-run detail (what each agent did) is in the journal, not the logs. Logging from code agents ¶ from tuvl import agent, Ctx @agent("enrich") async def enrich(inp, ctx: Ctx): ctx.log.info("enrich.lookup", candidate_id=str(inp.candidate.id)) # bound to run_id and agent ... Pass data as keyword arguments, never f-strings, so values are structured fields. 3. Distributed Tracing ¶ tuvl uses the OpenTelemetry SDK with an OTLP exporter; init_telemetry() installs the TracerProvider at startup. Inbound W3C traceparent headers make run spans children of the caller's trace. Span attributes set by tuvl ¶ Attribute Span Description tuvl.run_id tuvl.run The run tuvl.workflow tuvl.run , tuvl.agent Workflow name tuvl.agent tuvl.agent Agent id tuvl.engine tuvl.agent code , tool , decide , llm , loop , human , map , parallel , pending tuvl.determinism tuvl.agent deterministic , bounded , external , pending tuvl.signal tuvl.agent The emitted signal tuvl.tokens tuvl.agent Tokens used by the invocation tuvl.attempt tuvl.agent Retry attempt tuvl.error_type tuvl.agent On error (span status ERROR) Context values are never span attributes, so secure fields can't leak into traces. 4. Span Hierarchy ¶ A run that pauses (a human form, a tool approval, a breakpoint) and resumes on another worker produces one tuvl.run span per execution segment, all carrying the same tuvl.run_id ; group by it to see the whole run. Engine work — model calls, HTTP calls, DB queries — nests under the agent's span. 5. Model-call spans ¶ The built-in model client wraps every call in a span named chat <model> ( embeddings <model> for embeddings) using the GenAI semantic conventions — gen_ai.operation.name , gen_ai.system , gen_ai.request.model , gen_ai.usage.input_tokens , gen_ai.usage.output_tokens , gen_ai.response.finish_reasons — nested under the tuvl.agent span that made them. A failed call records the exception on the span. 6. Metrics ¶ Run-level numbers (runs by status and end, tokens per agent, decision sources, approvals) come from the journal and the runs table: GET /api/runs , tuvl list runs --json , or SQL over tuvl_system_runs / tuvl_system_run_events . The one OTel counter is tuvl.hook.events (meter tuvl.hooks ), incremented when a type: hook artifact with action: metric fires ( tuvl.hook.name , tuvl.hook.event , tuvl.workflow.name ). 7. Configuration Reference ¶ All settings are read from .env or environment variables. Settings also support a per-project YAML override file at .tuvl/telemetry.yaml (see below). Environment variables ¶ Variable Default Description TUVL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED true Set false to disable all OTel export TUVL_OTLP_ENDPOINT http://localhost:4318 OTLP collector endpoint (base URL; tuvl adds /v1/traces and /v1/metrics ) OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT — Standard OTel env var — takes precedence over TUVL_OTLP_ENDPOINT when set TUVL_OTLP_PROTOCOL http/protobuf http/protobuf or grpc (needs pip install 'tuvl[otel-grpc]' ) OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL — Standard OTel env var — takes precedence over TUVL_OTLP_PROTOCOL when set TUVL_SERVICE_NAME tuvl service.name resource attribute in every span TUVL_ENV production production → JSON logs; development → coloured console logs .tuvl/telemetry.yaml override ¶ Values from this file are applied only when the corresponding environment variable is not set, making it suitable for checked-in defaults that operators can override at deployment time. kind: TelemetryConfig version: v1 spec: enabled: true otlp_endpoint: http://otel-collector:4318 otlp_protocol: http/protobuf service_name: my-tuvl-app Config resolution order ¶ For each setting, the first non-empty source wins: Environment variable ( TUVL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED , OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT , TUVL_OTLP_ENDPOINT , TUVL_SERVICE_NAME ) .tuvl/telemetry.yaml spec fields Hardcoded defaults (enabled= true , endpoint= http://localhost:4318 , protocol= http/protobuf , service= tuvl ) 8. Collector Setup ¶ tuvl exports spans and metrics over OTLP/HTTP (port 4318) to any OTLP-compatible collector. To use gRPC (port 4317) instead, install tuvl[otel-grpc] and set TUVL_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc . If you upgraded from a version that used gRPC and your endpoint still ends in :4317 , tuvl logs a warning at startup. Below are quick-start configurations for common backends. OpenTelemetry Collector (recommended) ¶ # docker-compose.yml services: otel-collector: image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest ports: - "4318:4318" # OTLP/HTTP volumes: - ./otel-config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml jaeger: image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:latest ports: - "16686:16686" # Jaeger UI # otel-config.yaml receivers: otlp: protocols: http: endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 exporters: jaeger: endpoint: jaeger:14250 tls: insecure: true service: pipelines: traces: receivers: [otlp] exporters: [jaeger] # .env TUVL_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 TUVL_SERVICE_NAME=my-app Grafana Tempo (via Alloy) ¶ TUVL_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://alloy:4318 TUVL_SERVICE_NAME=my-app Honeycomb ¶ OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://api.honeycomb.io # Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS with your API key via collector or proxy Datadog ¶ Use the Datadog Agent as an OTLP collector: TUVL_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://datadog-agent:4318 9. Dev Mode Behaviour ¶ When TUVL_DEV_MODE=true (set automatically by tuvl dev ): init_telemetry() is a no-op — no TracerProvider is installed The OTel SDK default NonRecordingSpan is returned for all start_as_current_span calls — all span operations become no-ops with negligible overhead Logs use the coloured ConsoleRenderer instead of JSON trace_id / span_id are not injected into log events (no valid span context) Dev mode never runs with TUVL_ENV=production — that combination aborts at boot. 10. Data Masking & PII ¶ Fields declared secure: true in a ModelDefinition : # models/employee.yaml spec: fields: - { name: national_id, type: string, secure: true } are redacted ( "*****" ) in journal events, SSE streams, run exports, pinned fixtures and the Insight views; checkpoints keep real values because they are the resume state; are never span attributes (tuvl puts no context values on spans); are not sent to models ( llm , loop , judges, decision models) unless policy.allow_secure_to_llm: true — a secure field in a model agent's inputs is a V020 error. The secure-field registry is built at startup from every loaded ModelDefinition .

docs.text: trigger (HTTP / API / MCP / schedule / child run) │ FastAPI HTTP span (W3C traceparent propagated) ▼ tuvl.run one span per execution of a run (each claim: start, resume) ├── tuvl.agent <id> one per agent invocation │ └── chat <model> gen_ai.* spans for model calls (llm, loop turns, decide models, judges) └── tuvl.agent <id> … Two complementary records: The journal ( tuvl_system_run_events ) is the authoritative, durable record of what a run did — every agent start/finish, signal, model turn, tool call, decision, judge verdict, approval and pause. It drives the Insight Runs page, GET /api/runs/{id}/events (SSE), tuvl follow run , replay and test fixtures. See runtime . docs.text: A run that pauses (a human form, a tool approval, a breakpoint) and resumes on another worker produces one tuvl.run span per execution segment, all carrying the same tuvl.run_id ; group by it to see the whole run. docs.text: The built-in model client wraps every call in a span named chat <model> ( embeddings <model> for embeddings) using the GenAI semantic conventions — gen_ai.operation.name , gen_ai.system , gen_ai.request.model , gen_ai.usage.input_tokens , gen_ai.usage.output_tokens , gen_ai.response.finish_reasons — nested under the tuvl.agent span that made them. docs.text: Project identity and the catalogue ¶ Every project made by tuvl init carries .tuvl/project.yaml : who built it, what it is, and a stable id. A project can optionally be listed in the public catalogue (nest.tuvl.io). Nothing is sent anywhere unless you register. The file ¶ kind: Project version: v1 metadata: name: screening spec: id: prj_01a141a1-9446-74f6-81e4-bc37135cfcf1-f8 author: Jane Doe organization: Acme organization_url: https://acme.example # optional email: jane@example.com type: dev # poc | dev | production version: 0.1.0 # the app's own semver, not the engine's description: | Screens **candidate** applications. - scores CVs - routes edge cases to a human license: Apache-2.0 # optional repo: https://github.com/acme/screening registry: # written by register, not by hand url: https://nest.tuvl.io id: prj_01a141a1-9446-74f6-81e4-bc37135cfcf1-f8 registered_at: 2026-10-15T10:00:00Z digest: 3f9a1c0b7d2e4a55 Field Rules id Minted once by tuvl init ; never changes. prj_ + a UUIDv7 + two check characters name Required type poc , dev or production version Semver ( 1.2.3 , 1.2.3-rc.1 ) author , email Captured and sent to the Nest on registration so the owner can be reached; the Nest keeps them private and never shows them. The email must be a valid address if set organization , organization_url The organization the project belongs to, and an optional http(s) link to it. Both are shown in the catalogue description Markdown , up to 2000 characters repo http(s) URL if set The file is read fail-open: a project without it boots normally and tuvl upgrade project creates it. The id is self-checking ¶ The two trailing characters are derived from the UUID. A typo or a half-edited id fails the check and every project command ( show , set , register ), Insight and register refuse it. This guards against accidents and copy-paste damage; it is not a signature : anyone can recompute the check. Ownership of a listing is decided by the Nest, which ties an id to the GitHub account that registered it first. A copied project shares its id with the original. Run tuvl upgrade project --new-id in the copy to mint its own (this also clears the registration). Command line ¶ tuvl show project [--json] # the record; description rendered as Markdown tuvl set project author "Jane Doe" tuvl set project description @about.md # read from a file cat README.md | tuvl set project description - # or stdin tuvl upgrade project [--name N] [--new-id] tuvl register project [--Nest URL] [-y] info also reports the registry state: not registered, up to date, changed since the last registration, or id differs from the registered one. Insight ¶ Settings → Project edits every field above. The description has an Edit / Preview toggle. The Catalogue card shows the listing state and a Register button ( Update listing once listed, and the card says when the project changed since). The dialog shows the exact payload and a "show my developer email publicly" checkbox. Send registers directly when this machine already has a Nest login; otherwise it shows a GitHub device code, waits for approval and then registers. The Nest token stays on the dev server and is shared with the CLI's cache. What registration sends ¶ { "id": "01a141a1-9446-74f6-81e4-bc37135cfcf1", "name": "screening", "author": "Jane Doe", "organization": "Acme", "organization_url": "https://acme.example", "type": "dev", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "…", "license": "Apache-2.0", "repo": "https://…", "tuvl_version": "2.0.0" } plus organization and, when set, contact_email . The Nest lists only the name, version, organization (with its link), type, licence, description and the optional repository link; the author and email stay private. The Nest keys the entry by the bare UUID; the check characters never leave your machine. Sign-in is GitHub's device flow (see auth ); only the account that first registered an id can update it. The Nest is https://nest.tuvl.io , or TUVL_NEST_URL / --nest for a self-hosted one. The login token is cached in ~/.config/tuvl/nest.json (mode 0600). Dev API (Insight) ¶ Served by tuvl dev only; not mounted in production. Route GET /dev/project the record plus registration_state (404 if the project has none) GET /dev/project/summary what the project holds: workflows, models, specs, tests, lock PUT /dev/project update editable fields; the id and registry block are ignored POST /dev/project/register/preview the payload that would be sent POST /dev/project/register register, or start a device login ( status: login_required ) POST /dev/project/register/poll pending until approved, then registers

docs.text: Runtime and journal ¶ tuvl 2.0 runs every workflow on a durable runner : one deterministic loop that walks the graph, invokes engines and records everything. There is no master process — any worker can continue any run, because run state lives in Postgres, not in worker memory. Storage ¶ Table ( tuvl_system_ prefix) Contents runs id, workflow name + content hash, status, trigger ( http , api , schedule , mcp , child , child:<agent>:<item> for a map item, dev ), principal, tenant, parent run, current agent, lease owner + expiry, tokens used, output, error run_events The journal : append-only (run_id, seq) events with type, agent, payload, tokens and latency run_checkpoints The context after each completed agent — the resume state approvals Open human forms and tool-call approvals: run, agent, kind, payload, required group, expiry run_deltas The live draft of an agent's answer while it is still being written: text pieces and resets, written in batches by the worker and read by the event stream. Not part of the journal. Rows stay for a minute after the run ends (a client may still be reading the last pieces) and a sweep then removes them; a run that never finished loses them after a day On boot tuvl builds the indexes on the vector store, and run_deltas (created_at) for the draft sweep, including the partial indexes agent memory uses (by memory_key and by step ). They are built with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS , so upgrading a deployment with a large table does not block writes. One process builds them (an advisory lock; the others skip) and an index an interrupted build left invalid is rebuilt. Statuses: queued , running , waiting_human , waiting_approval , paused , completed , failed , aborted , compensated ( compensating while compensators run). Lifecycle ¶ Trigger — HTTP route, POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs , schedule, MCP or a parent loop. The principal is verified, the input validated against trigger.input , and a run is queued. Sync path (HTTP): the receiving process claims the run and executes it inline. If it ends within trigger.http.sync_timeout (default 30 s) the response is the end's status / body ; otherwise 202 with { run_id, status_url, events_url, … } , and the run keeps going. Async path: workers claim queued runs with SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and hold a heartbeat-renewed lease . Per agent: agent_started → engine → output validation → agent_completed + signal → checkpoint → route. The step's database writes commit in the same transaction as its checkpoint. Pause (human form, tool approval, breakpoint, supervisor or operator): checkpoint, set the status, release the lease. A decision or resume re-queues the run; any worker continues from the last checkpoint. End: run_completed with the end name and response; compensation if the end has rollback: true . Roles ¶ tuvl serve app --role all | api | worker (Helm: split: true ): all serves HTTP and executes the queue (default); api serves HTTP and only executes synchronous requests inline; worker executes the queue (and serves /health ). --concurrency bounds runs per process. Crash recovery ¶ An expired lease returns a run to queued ; the next claimer resumes from the last checkpoint and re-executes the in-flight agent. Per-agent semantics are at-least-once , made safe by: tool: db on the primary datasource — writes commit with the checkpoint (exactly-once); tool: http — idempotency: auto sends a stable Idempotency-Key ; code — ctx.idempotency_key , and ctx.db writes commit with the checkpoint; MCP and other external calls — at-least-once; give write/destructive ones a compensate (V015). A human agent's idempotency key counts finished steps, so it is stable across suspend and resume. Transactions ¶ spec.transaction Semantics Constraints per_agent (default) Each agent's writes commit with its checkpoint. Cross-agent atomicity comes from compensation — per_run One transaction for the whole run, each step in a savepoint; committed with the run's end, rolled back on failure. No checkpoints — a crash reruns the run No human , approvals or async triggers; sync only (V021) Compensation ¶ Reaching an end with rollback: true , an unhandled error , or an abort runs the compensate agent of every completed agent that declares one, in reverse completion order . Each compensator receives the original agent's inputs and outputs. A failing compensator makes the run failed ( compensation_failed ); the rest still run. Success ends as compensated . Journal events ¶ Every event: { run_id, seq, ts, type, agent_id, engine, tokens, latency_ms, payload } . run_queued · run_started · agent_started · agent_completed · signal · llm_turn · tool_call · tool_result · map_started · map_item · map_finished · parallel_started · parallel_branch · parallel_finished · memory_recalled · memory_written · memory_compacted · decision · judge_verdict · approval_requested · approval_decided · paused · resumed · checkpoint · compensation_started · compensation_completed · run_completed · run_failed · run_aborted Read them with GET /api/runs/{id}/events (SSE: replay, then live), tuvl follow run , the Insight Runs page, or RunHandle.events() in @tuvl/client . Checkpoints keep real values (they are the resume state); secure fields are redacted on export. Replay and fixtures ¶ The journal is the recording. Replay re-executes a run's graph but serves llm , loop , decide model, tool and judge results from recorded events. tuvl pin run <run_id> (or 📌 in Insight) exports a run to tests/fixtures/<workflow>/<name>.journal.json ; a Test with replay: then runs with zero tokens, and tuvl replay runs <fixture> fails if the end or output differ. Insight's Change engine check replays fixtures with only the changed agent live. Operator control ¶ POST /api/runs/{id}/pause | resume | abort | steer (scope runs:control ). Control is read by the runner between agents and loop iterations, under the run's lock, so it works across workers. In dev mode, Insight breakpoints and step mode pause runs through the same mechanism. Production server and shutdown ¶ tuvl serve app starts uvicorn and replaces the tuvl process with it, so in a container uvicorn is PID 1 and receives SIGTERM itself. On SIGTERM it stops taking requests and lets open ones finish for --graceful-timeout seconds (20), then the runtime stops claiming runs and waits --drain-timeout seconds (20) for the running ones. A run still going is interrupted, not failed: its lease expires and another worker resumes it from the last checkpoint. terminationGracePeriodSeconds in the chart (60) must exceed the sum, and a preStop pause lets the load balancer stop sending traffic first. Behind an ingress, --forwarded-allow-ips ( forwardedAllowIps in the chart) names the proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted, so --allow-host and the logs see the real client. Leave it empty to trust only 127.0.0.1 ; * trusts every sender and lets a client spoof its address. --limit-max-requests restarts a worker after that many requests. The Server response header is off. The chart runs the pod as a non-root user with no privilege escalation, every capability dropped and the runtime-default seccomp profile ( securityContext in values.yaml ). readOnlyRootFilesystem is off by default because some admin features write under /app ; turn it on once yours do not (a writable /tmp is mounted when it is on). Scheduler ¶ trigger.schedule (cron, UTC) enqueues one run per slot across all workers, guarded by a Postgres advisory lock. A slot missed while every process was down is skipped; there is no catch-up. trigger: schedule: cron: "0 9 * * 1-5" enabled: true # false pauses it and keeps the settings input: { report: daily } # every scheduled run starts with this; checked against trigger.input A bare cron string ( schedule: "0 9 * * 1-5" ) is the same schedule with no input. Scheduled runs have no caller, so a workflow whose trigger.input has required fields needs them in input . tuvl lint project reports a mismatch (V019). The schedule is read at boot; in dev the server reloads when the YAML changes. Multi-tenant mode ¶ When the project is locked to multi_tenant , the run tables carry a tenant_id column and every run belongs to one tenant: Starting a run needs a tenant. An HTTP or API run takes it from the caller's token ( tenant claim); code that starts runs binds it with tuvl.tenancy.tenant_scope() . A run started with no tenant is refused ( MissingTenantContextError ) unless TUVL_REQUIRE_TENANT_CONTEXT=false . Workers execute a run under its tenant. The tenant is bound while the run executes, so its db calls, logs, journal rows and child runs carry it, and the runtime engine sets app.current_tenant_id for row-level security ( tuvl generate rls ). Callers reach only their own tenant's runs. Reads, the event stream, export, pause/resume/abort, the run list and approvals are filtered by tenant, whatever scopes the caller holds, iam:admin and runs:control included. Another tenant's run answers 404 . Scheduled workflows list their tenants. A scheduled run has no request to take a tenant from: trigger: schedule: "0 6 * * *" tenants: [acme, globex] Each slot enqueues one run per tenant (trigger schedule:<slot>:<tenant> ), once, across all workers. A scheduled workflow with no tenants is not scheduled in multi-tenant mode (the runtime logs workflow.schedule_needs_tenants ); in single-tenant mode tenants is ignored. - Upgrading. A database first booted in multi-tenant mode by an earlier build lacks the column; the runtime adds it at boot ( ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS , default default_tenant ).
docs.title: Runtime and Journal

docs.text: tuvl 2.0 runs every workflow on a durable runner : one deterministic loop that walks the graph, invokes engines and records everything. There is no master process — any worker can continue any run, because run state lives in Postgres, not in worker memory.
docs.title: Runtime and journal

docs.text: Table ( tuvl_system_ prefix) Contents runs id, workflow name + content hash, status, trigger ( http , api , schedule , mcp , child , child:<agent>:<item> for a map item, dev ), principal, tenant, parent run, current agent, lease owner + expiry, tokens used, output, error run_events The journal : append-only (run_id, seq) events with type, agent, payload, tokens and latency run_checkpoints The context after each completed agent — the resume state approvals Open human forms and tool-call approvals: run, agent, kind, payload, required group, expiry run_deltas The live draft of an agent's answer while it is still being written: text pieces and resets, written in batches by the worker and read by the event stream. Not part of the journal. Rows stay for a minute after the run ends (a client may still be reading the last pieces) and a sweep then removes them; a run that never finished loses them after a day On boot tuvl builds the indexes on the vector store, and run_deltas (created_at) for the draft sweep, including the partial indexes agent memory uses (by memory_key and by step ). They are built with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS , so upgrading a deployment with a large table does not block writes. One process builds them (an advisory lock; the others skip) and an index an interrupted build left invalid is rebuilt. Statuses: queued , running , waiting_human , waiting_approval , paused , completed , failed , aborted , compensated ( compensating while compensators run).
docs.title: Storage

docs.text: Trigger — HTTP route, POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs , schedule, MCP or a parent loop. The principal is verified, the input validated against trigger.input , and a run is queued. Sync path (HTTP): the receiving process claims the run and executes it inline. If it ends within trigger.http.sync_timeout (default 30 s) the response is the end's status / body ; otherwise 202 with { run_id, status_url, events_url, … } , and the run keeps going. Async path: workers claim queued runs with SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and hold a heartbeat-renewed lease . Per agent: agent_started → engine → output validation → agent_completed + signal → checkpoint → route. The step's database writes commit in the same transaction as its checkpoint. Pause (human form, tool approval, breakpoint, supervisor or operator): checkpoint, set the status, release the lease. A decision or resume re-queues the run; any worker continues from the last checkpoint. End: run_completed with the end name and response; compensation if the end has rollback: true .
docs.title: Lifecycle

docs.text: tuvl serve app --role all | api | worker (Helm: split: true ): all serves HTTP and executes the queue (default); api serves HTTP and only executes synchronous requests inline; worker executes the queue (and serves /health ). --concurrency bounds runs per process.
docs.title: Roles

docs.text: An expired lease returns a run to queued ; the next claimer resumes from the last checkpoint and re-executes the in-flight agent. Per-agent semantics are at-least-once , made safe by: tool: db on the primary datasource — writes commit with the checkpoint (exactly-once); tool: http — idempotency: auto sends a stable Idempotency-Key ; code — ctx.idempotency_key , and ctx.db writes commit with the checkpoint; MCP and other external calls — at-least-once; give write/destructive ones a compensate (V015). A human agent's idempotency key counts finished steps, so it is stable across suspend and resume.
docs.title: Crash recovery

docs.text: spec.transaction Semantics Constraints per_agent (default) Each agent's writes commit with its checkpoint. Cross-agent atomicity comes from compensation — per_run One transaction for the whole run, each step in a savepoint; committed with the run's end, rolled back on failure. No checkpoints — a crash reruns the run No human , approvals or async triggers; sync only (V021)
docs.title: Transactions

docs.text: Reaching an end with rollback: true , an unhandled error , or an abort runs the compensate agent of every completed agent that declares one, in reverse completion order . Each compensator receives the original agent's inputs and outputs. A failing compensator makes the run failed ( compensation_failed ); the rest still run. Success ends as compensated .
docs.title: Compensation

docs.text: Every event: { run_id, seq, ts, type, agent_id, engine, tokens, latency_ms, payload } . run_queued · run_started · agent_started · agent_completed · signal · llm_turn · tool_call · tool_result · map_started · map_item · map_finished · parallel_started · parallel_branch · parallel_finished · memory_recalled · memory_written · memory_compacted · decision · judge_verdict · approval_requested · approval_decided · paused · resumed · checkpoint · compensation_started · compensation_completed · run_completed · run_failed · run_aborted Read them with GET /api/runs/{id}/events (SSE: replay, then live), tuvl follow run , the Insight Runs page, or RunHandle.events() in @tuvl/client . Checkpoints keep real values (they are the resume state); secure fields are redacted on export.
docs.title: Journal events

docs.text: The journal is the recording. Replay re-executes a run's graph but serves llm , loop , decide model, tool and judge results from recorded events. tuvl pin run <run_id> (or 📌 in Insight) exports a run to tests/fixtures/<workflow>/<name>.journal.json ; a Test with replay: then runs with zero tokens, and tuvl replay runs <fixture> fails if the end or output differ. Insight's Change engine check replays fixtures with only the changed agent live.
docs.title: Replay and fixtures

docs.text: POST /api/runs/{id}/pause | resume | abort | steer (scope runs:control ). Control is read by the runner between agents and loop iterations, under the run's lock, so it works across workers. In dev mode, Insight breakpoints and step mode pause runs through the same mechanism.
docs.title: Operator control

docs.text: tuvl serve app starts uvicorn and replaces the tuvl process with it, so in a container uvicorn is PID 1 and receives SIGTERM itself. On SIGTERM it stops taking requests and lets open ones finish for --graceful-timeout seconds (20), then the runtime stops claiming runs and waits --drain-timeout seconds (20) for the running ones. A run still going is interrupted, not failed: its lease expires and another worker resumes it from the last checkpoint. terminationGracePeriodSeconds in the chart (60) must exceed the sum, and a preStop pause lets the load balancer stop sending traffic first. Behind an ingress, --forwarded-allow-ips ( forwardedAllowIps in the chart) names the proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted, so --allow-host and the logs see the real client. Leave it empty to trust only 127.0.0.1 ; * trusts every sender and lets a client spoof its address. --limit-max-requests restarts a worker after that many requests. The Server response header is off. The chart runs the pod as a non-root user with no privilege escalation, every capability dropped and the runtime-default seccomp profile ( securityContext in values.yaml ). readOnlyRootFilesystem is off by default because some admin features write under /app ; turn it on once yours do not (a writable /tmp is mounted when it is on).
docs.title: Production server and shutdown

docs.text: trigger.schedule (cron, UTC) enqueues one run per slot across all workers, guarded by a Postgres advisory lock. A slot missed while every process was down is skipped; there is no catch-up. trigger: schedule: cron: "0 9 * * 1-5" enabled: true # false pauses it and keeps the settings input: { report: daily } # every scheduled run starts with this; checked against trigger.input A bare cron string ( schedule: "0 9 * * 1-5" ) is the same schedule with no input. Scheduled runs have no caller, so a workflow whose trigger.input has required fields needs them in input . tuvl lint project reports a mismatch (V019). The schedule is read at boot; in dev the server reloads when the YAML changes.
docs.title: Scheduler
