docs.text: Spec-driven development ¶ Intent lives in a spec. The coding agent builds; tuvl referees. Every tuvl step below is deterministic and spends no tokens — only the agents you build (llm, loop, decision models) call models at run time. spec (.md) ──spec check──▶ checked spec ──coding agent (skills)──▶ task list + workflows, models, code, tests ▲ │ │ spec diff / P005: stale tasks ▼ │ codegen: schemas, stubs, prompt placeholders, tests │ │ └── derived task status ◀── spec verify · validate · test (honest) ◀─────┘ │ lock · ship 1. Write the spec ¶ A spec is Markdown. Prose sections ( # Intent , # Policies , anything else) are for people and the coding agent. Three sections are structured and checked: # Data , # Flows and the tuvl-example blocks under # Acceptance . tuvl create spec refund-request writes a template that passes tuvl lint spec . --- name: refund-request owner: payments-team --- # Intent Customers request refunds. Small ones are paid automatically; large ones need a finance lead. # Data - **Order** (existing) — `id` (uuid), `customer_email` (string; secure), `total` (numeric) - **Refund** (new) — `order_id` (uuid → Order; required), `amount` (numeric; required), `status` (enum: requested | approved | rejected | paid; required; default requested) # Flows ## Flow: refund_request Trigger: POST /refunds · signed-in Input: `order_id` (uuid), `amount` (float), `reason` (str) Ends: default 201 · unknown_order 404 · rejected 200 · failed 500 1. `load_order` — tool db read Order · in `order_id` · out `order` (Order) - not_found → END.unknown_order 2. `check_amount` — decide rules · in `amount` · out `lane` (enum[auto, review]) - `amount <= 100` → auto - otherwise → review - auto → `record_refund` - review → `finance_review` 3. `finance_review` — human group finance_lead · expires 24h · in `order`, `amount` · out `approved` (bool) - true → `record_refund` - false, expired → END.rejected 4. `record_refund` — tool db create Refund · in `order_id`, `amount`, `reason` · out `refund` (Refund) - conflict → END.failed # Acceptance ```tuvl-example name: a small refund is recorded given: { Order: [{ id: "6f1c0a52-2a8e-4d0b-9a77-0b9d7c2f1e10", total: 120 }] } as: { user: u-customer } input: { order_id: "6f1c0a52-2a8e-4d0b-9a77-0b9d7c2f1e10", amount: 40, reason: "Arrived broken." } expect: { end: default } ``` Grammar ¶ Element Form Model - **Name** (new\|existing) — fields ; a bullet may wrap onto indented lines Field `name` (type; flags) — types string text integer numeric boolean uuid date timestamptz jsonb , enum: a \| b , uuid → Model ; flags required unique secure , default <v> Flow ## Flow: <workflow_name> under # Flows Trigger Trigger: POST /path · signed-in — or group <g> / public ; schedule <cron> ; tool (only called as a loop's workflow tool) Input / Ends Input: `f` (type), … · Ends: default 201 · <name> <status> · failed 500 ( default and failed are required) Step N. `id` — <engine …> · in `a`, `b`? · out `x` (type) · budget 800 tok, 20s, retry 2 · effect write · expires 24h · guardrails `g@1` — a trailing `b`? marks an optional input; long steps continue on an indented · … line Engines code · tool db read\|list\|create\|update\|upsert\|delete <Model> · tool http <METHOD> <name> · tool mcp <server> · llm <model> · loop <model> (with tools: `t1`, workflow `w` (approval <group> when `expr`; max 1 call) ) · decide rules · decide model <ref> ≥ 0.8 · decide rules + model <ref> ≥ 0.7 · human group <g> Route - signal[, signal] → `step` or → END / → END.<end> ; (out f (type)) names outputs a reserved signal carries Rule - `TEL condition` → value , last - otherwise → value Waiver - <signal>: waived — <reason> under a step; - tests: waived — <reason> for a step no offline test can run (e.g. it needs pgvector) — reported by verify spec , counted by task status; - <end>: no example — <reason> (indented) under Ends: Off-spine T1. steps — a loop's tools ( tool of loop ), compensators (a step's · compensate undo_x ` part: runs on a rollback end to undo it) and alternate paths, which route default` explicitly Implicit: default goes to the next numbered step (or END ), and error to END.failed . 2. Check it ¶ tuvl lint spec [SPEC] [--strict] [--json] (MCP spec_check , GET /dev/specs/check ) — zero tokens, deterministic. It reports every finding with its line; blocking findings fail. Rule Finding S001 ✗ A line in # Data / # Flows doesn't parse — never skipped silently S002 ✗ A route targets an end not in Ends: , an unknown step or a loop tool S003 ✗ A listed end is unreachable from the trigger S004 ✗ An engine-implied signal is neither routed nor waived (db read/delete → not_found , create/update/upsert → conflict , llm → parse_error timeout budget_exceeded , loop → max_iterations budget_exceeded timeout aborted , decide model → low_confidence , human … expires → expired , guardrails → guardrail_violation , each enum value of a decide/human output) — or a routed signal the engine never emits S005 ✗ A model step lacks its safeguards: decide model without a ref, threshold or time budget; decide with neither rules nor a model, or rules without otherwise and no model; llm / loop without a model or a token + time budget S006 ✗ A step reads a field not produced on every path to it (mark it optional with ? if that's intended) S007 ✗ A model or field isn't declared in # Data , an (existing) model or field isn't in models/ , an unknown column type, or an enum default outside its values S008 ✗ A secure field (or a model holding one) is an input of a model-backed step S009 ✗ A step output reuses a name the trigger input or an earlier step on its path already holds S010 ✗ An HTTP trigger declares no access ( signed-in , public or group <g> ) S011 ! An end has no tuvl-example and no no example waiver S012 ✗ An example names an unknown flow, step, end or model, or a mock sets outputs the step doesn't declare for that signal S013 ! A human step has no group or no expiry S014 ! A free-text acceptance bullet — listed, not checked S015 ✗ A decide rule doesn't compile or type-check against the step's inputs, reads a non-input, or yields a value outside the output enum S016 ✗ A loop tool isn't a T step of the flow (or a ## Flow: /project workflow), an approval condition doesn't compile, or an off-spine step is never used S017 ✗ The spec is approved but its body changed since: approve it again ( tuvl approve spec ) or reopen it S018 ✗ ideas: names an idea that is not in idea/ S019 ! The spec id is malformed, differs from the file name, or its idea is missing from ideas: S020 ! An idea the spec comes from was superseded by a newer one S021 ! A file of an idea changed (or went missing) since it was imported — ideas are immutable T001 ! An example mocks deterministic logic ( code , tool db , decide rules) — seed given: and as: instead Prose sections are listed as unchecked . A waived signal or end is reported (·) so a reviewer sees it. 3. Verify the implementation ¶ tuvl verify spec [SPEC] [--strict] [--no-tests] [--json] (MCP spec_verify , GET /dev/specs/verify ) — zero tokens. It compares each ## Flow: with its workflow, each # Data model with its ModelDefinition , and runs the tests (offline) to see which steps they exercise. Errors are contradictions; warnings are unfinished work (a missing workflow, a pending agent, an untested step), which --strict — the CI gate — also fails. Rule Checks R001 The flow has a workflow of that name; trigger method, path, schedule, access ( public ↔ trigger.http.public , group <g> ↔ metadata.required_scope ) and input names and types match R002 Each step is an agent with the same id and engine family ( tool db read Order ↔ use: db, op: read, model: Order ; decide rules + model ↔ both); pending is reported as not implemented; agents the spec doesn't name are reported R003 Inputs and outputs match the step's contract R004 Every spec route (including the implicit default and waivers) is in the workflow with the same target; a workflow route to an end the spec doesn't have is reported R005 Ends and their HTTP statuses match the workflow's outputs R006 Data fields exist in the ModelDefinition with a compatible type, the same enum values and the same required / unique / secure / default R007 Model steps use the spec's model, threshold and budget (tokens, time, iterations, tool calls); decide rules match in order; loop tools, approvals and max_calls match R008 Human steps use the spec's group and expiry R009 Each tuvl-example has its generated test, and it passed (stubbed doesn't count) R010 Each step is run by a passing test; deterministic steps must run for real (mocked-only is reported), model, external and human steps count through their mocks specs/triage-ticket.md triage_ticket classify llm default :23 ✓ mocked in 3 prioritise code :25 ✓ 3 passed review human group support_leads :28 ✓ mocked in 1 store tool db create Ticket :32 ✓ 1 passed 0 mismatch(es) · steps implemented 4/4 · exercised by real tests 2/4 4. The task list ¶ tuvl generate tasks <spec> derives the task list from an approved spec — one task per new model, step and example, a manual task for each step that calls an external system — with no model. Re-running it keeps ids, refreshes section hashes and marks tasks whose step or example left the spec obsolete . The coding agent (skill tuvl-plan ) adds only what cannot be derived, such as a manual task for a policy or credentials. tuvl checks the list as part of tuvl lint spec and derives each task's status. A spec is a draft until someone runs tuvl approve spec , which records who, when and a hash of the body in the front matter ( status , approved_by , approved_at , approved_hash ). Editing the body afterwards makes the approval stale (S017) and the spec a draft again; the front matter is not hashed. tuvl reject spec --reason and tuvl reopen spec send it back. Anyone on the project may approve; the review of the commit that records it is the control. tuvl list specs shows each spec's state. kind: TaskPlan version: tuvl/v2 metadata: { name: refund-request, spec: specs/refund-request.md, spec_hash: 9f2c… } spec: tasks: - id: T3 title: Route refunds by amount (decide rules) type: agent # model | workflow | agent | artifact | integration | test | policy | manual spec_ref: { anchor: flow-refund-request, hash: 41ad… } target: { workflow: refund_request, agent: check_amount } depends_on: [T2] - id: T7 title: "Example: a small refund is paid automatically" type: test spec_ref: { anchor: acceptance, hash: 7be0… } target: { workflow: refund_request, example: a small refund is paid automatically } - id: T9 title: Payments API credentials type: manual # only manual tasks set a status target: { workflow: refund_request, agent: pay_refund } status: todo One task per new model, per step, per example, and a manual task per external integration ( tool http / mcp ); dependencies follow the flow. No estimates. After a spec change the agent adds tasks for new steps and marks removed ones obsolete: true (never deletes them). Rule Finding P001 ✗ The file isn't a valid TaskPlan , or a non-manual task has no target P002 ✗ A task targets something the spec doesn't declare (model, flow, step or example) P003 ! Coverage: a new model, step, example or external integration has no task (or there is no task list yet) P004 ✗ A task carries an estimate ( effort ) or a hand-set status (only manual tasks may) P005 ! A task's spec section changed since it was written — the agent should update it Derived status ¶ Status Rule todo Target agent is pending , the target file is absent, or an example has no generated test in_progress Target exists but validate reports errors on it, or it contradicts the spec ( verify spec ) implemented Target validates cleanly and matches the spec tested A passing Test covers it (stubbed results don't count), and its acceptance examples pass done Nothing blocks ship : lock current, no warnings on the target blocked (overlay) The spec has blocking lint spec findings, or a depends_on task isn't done stale (overlay) The spec section changed since the task was written Only type: manual tasks take a manual status. Models and artifacts skip tested . A task tuvl can't measure is untracked . tuvl list tasks --json # derived statuses (runs the tests offline; --no-tests caps at implemented) tuvl list tasks --strict # exit 1 unless every live task is done and none is blocked or stale tuvl show drift # stale tasks and spec sections no task covers 5. Codegen ¶ tuvl generate code [<workflow>] [--check] — deterministic, no model: Output Rule agents/_generated/schemas.py <Id>In / <Id>Out models per agent (per-signal variants, <Id>Signal ), <Workflow>Input , <Workflow>End . Never hand-edited agents/<run>.py A stub per code agent when missing; otherwise a libcst merge that regenerates decorator, signature and docstring and keeps parameter names and the body artifacts/<name>.md A prompt placeholder for a missing artifact:// referenced by an llm / loop agent decide agents A block with neither rules nor model gets one never-matching rule per enum value tests/<workflow>/<example>.yaml Test documents from the spec's tuvl-example blocks; hand-written tests are never touched --check exits 1 if anything would change (the CI drift gate). tuvl never writes function bodies. 6. Lock ¶ tuvl generate lock writes tuvl.lock : the tuvl version, each AgentModel's model id, each artifact:// ref's version and sha256, judge and decision-model versions, and each allowed MCP tool's input-schema hash (listed live; --no-mcp compares by name only). tuvl verify lock verifies it; tuvl ship requires it (V024) and pins the locked tuvl version in the image. 7. The CI gate ¶ tuvl lint spec && tuvl lint project --strict && tuvl generate code --check && tuvl verify lock && tuvl run tests --strict && tuvl verify spec --strict && tuvl list tasks --strict tuvl init <name> --sample creates a project that passes this gate as created. Coding agents ¶ tuvl serve mcp [-d <project>] [--allow-write] serves the same operations over MCP (stdio): validate , spec_check , spec_verify , spec_status , spec_diff , get_contract , list_agents , explain_error , get_run , get_run_events , codegen , test ; with --allow-write also codegen_write , run_workflow , pin_fixture . It refuses TUVL_ENV=production . .agents/skills/ (refreshed by tuvl update skills [--diff] , mirrored to .claude/skills/ ): tuvl-spec , tuvl-plan , tuvl-task-loop , agent-code , agent-tool , agent-llm , agent-loop , agent-decide , agent-human , agent-map , agent-parallel , tuvl-data , tuvl-test , tuvl-harden , tuvl-ship , plus a root AGENTS.md with the non-negotiable rules. Every read command has --json with a documented schema ( /dev/schema/cli in dev mode).

docs.text: Element Form Model - **Name** (new\|existing) — fields ; a bullet may wrap onto indented lines Field `name` (type; flags) — types string text integer numeric boolean uuid date timestamptz jsonb , enum: a \| b , uuid → Model ; flags required unique secure , default <v> Flow ## Flow: <workflow_name> under # Flows Trigger Trigger: POST /path · signed-in — or group <g> / public ; schedule <cron> ; tool (only called as a loop's workflow tool) Input / Ends Input: `f` (type), … · Ends: default 201 · <name> <status> · failed 500 ( default and failed are required) Step N. `id` — <engine …> · in `a`, `b`? · out `x` (type) · budget 800 tok, 20s, retry 2 · effect write · expires 24h · guardrails `g@1` — a trailing `b`? marks an optional input; long steps continue on an indented · … line Engines code · tool db read\|list\|create\|update\|upsert\|delete <Model> · tool http <METHOD> <name> · tool mcp <server> · llm <model> · loop <model> (with tools: `t1`, workflow `w` (approval <group> when `expr`; max 1 call) ) · decide rules · decide model <ref> ≥ 0.8 · decide rules + model <ref> ≥ 0.7 · human group <g> Route - signal[, signal] → `step` or → END / → END.<end> ; (out f (type)) names outputs a reserved signal carries Rule - `TEL condition` → value , last - otherwise → value Waiver - <signal>: waived — <reason> under a step; - tests: waived — <reason> for a step no offline test can run (e.g. it needs pgvector) — reported by verify spec , counted by task status; - <end>: no example — <reason> (indented) under Ends: Off-spine T1. steps — a loop's tools ( tool of loop ), compensators (a step's · compensate undo_x ` part: runs on a rollback end to undo it) and alternate paths, which route default` explicitly Implicit: default goes to the next numbered step (or END ), and error to END.failed .
docs.title: Grammar

docs.text: tuvl lint spec [SPEC] [--strict] [--json] (MCP spec_check , GET /dev/specs/check ) — zero tokens, deterministic. It reports every finding with its line; blocking findings fail. Rule Finding S001 ✗ A line in # Data / # Flows doesn't parse — never skipped silently S002 ✗ A route targets an end not in Ends: , an unknown step or a loop tool S003 ✗ A listed end is unreachable from the trigger S004 ✗ An engine-implied signal is neither routed nor waived (db read/delete → not_found , create/update/upsert → conflict , llm → parse_error timeout budget_exceeded , loop → max_iterations budget_exceeded timeout aborted , decide model → low_confidence , human … expires → expired , guardrails → guardrail_violation , each enum value of a decide/human output) — or a routed signal the engine never emits S005 ✗ A model step lacks its safeguards: decide model without a ref, threshold or time budget; decide with neither rules nor a model, or rules without otherwise and no model; llm / loop without a model or a token + time budget S006 ✗ A step reads a field not produced on every path to it (mark it optional with ? if that's intended) S007 ✗ A model or field isn't declared in # Data , an (existing) model or field isn't in models/ , an unknown column type, or an enum default outside its values S008 ✗ A secure field (or a model holding one) is an input of a model-backed step S009 ✗ A step output reuses a name the trigger input or an earlier step on its path already holds S010 ✗ An HTTP trigger declares no access ( signed-in , public or group <g> ) S011 ! An end has no tuvl-example and no no example waiver S012 ✗ An example names an unknown flow, step, end or model, or a mock sets outputs the step doesn't declare for that signal S013 ! A human step has no group or no expiry S014 ! A free-text acceptance bullet — listed, not checked S015 ✗ A decide rule doesn't compile or type-check against the step's inputs, reads a non-input, or yields a value outside the output enum S016 ✗ A loop tool isn't a T step of the flow (or a ## Flow: /project workflow), an approval condition doesn't compile, or an off-spine step is never used S017 ✗ The spec is approved but its body changed since: approve it again ( tuvl approve spec ) or reopen it S018 ✗ ideas: names an idea that is not in idea/ S019 ! The spec id is malformed, differs from the file name, or its idea is missing from ideas: S020 ! An idea the spec comes from was superseded by a newer one S021 ! A file of an idea changed (or went missing) since it was imported — ideas are immutable T001 ! An example mocks deterministic logic ( code , tool db , decide rules) — seed given: and as: instead Prose sections are listed as unchecked . A waived signal or end is reported (·) so a reviewer sees it.
docs.title: 2. Check it

docs.text: tuvl verify spec [SPEC] [--strict] [--no-tests] [--json] (MCP spec_verify , GET /dev/specs/verify ) — zero tokens. It compares each ## Flow: with its workflow, each # Data model with its ModelDefinition , and runs the tests (offline) to see which steps they exercise. Errors are contradictions; warnings are unfinished work (a missing workflow, a pending agent, an untested step), which --strict — the CI gate — also fails. Rule Checks R001 The flow has a workflow of that name; trigger method, path, schedule, access ( public ↔ trigger.http.public , group <g> ↔ metadata.required_scope ) and input names and types match R002 Each step is an agent with the same id and engine family ( tool db read Order ↔ use: db, op: read, model: Order ; decide rules + model ↔ both); pending is reported as not implemented; agents the spec doesn't name are reported R003 Inputs and outputs match the step's contract R004 Every spec route (including the implicit default and waivers) is in the workflow with the same target; a workflow route to an end the spec doesn't have is reported R005 Ends and their HTTP statuses match the workflow's outputs R006 Data fields exist in the ModelDefinition with a compatible type, the same enum values and the same required / unique / secure / default R007 Model steps use the spec's model, threshold and budget (tokens, time, iterations, tool calls); decide rules match in order; loop tools, approvals and max_calls match R008 Human steps use the spec's group and expiry R009 Each tuvl-example has its generated test, and it passed (stubbed doesn't count) R010 Each step is run by a passing test; deterministic steps must run for real (mocked-only is reported), model, external and human steps count through their mocks specs/triage-ticket.md triage_ticket classify llm default :23 ✓ mocked in 3 prioritise code :25 ✓ 3 passed review human group support_leads :28 ✓ mocked in 1 store tool db create Ticket :32 ✓ 1 passed 0 mismatch(es) · steps implemented 4/4 · exercised by real tests 2/4
docs.title: 3. Verify the implementation

docs.text: tuvl generate tasks <spec> derives the task list from an approved spec — one task per new model, step and example, a manual task for each step that calls an external system — with no model. Re-running it keeps ids, refreshes section hashes and marks tasks whose step or example left the spec obsolete . The coding agent (skill tuvl-plan ) adds only what cannot be derived, such as a manual task for a policy or credentials. tuvl checks the list as part of tuvl lint spec and derives each task's status. A spec is a draft until someone runs tuvl approve spec , which records who, when and a hash of the body in the front matter ( status , approved_by , approved_at , approved_hash ). Editing the body afterwards makes the approval stale (S017) and the spec a draft again; the front matter is not hashed. tuvl reject spec --reason and tuvl reopen spec send it back. Anyone on the project may approve; the review of the commit that records it is the control. tuvl list specs shows each spec's state. kind: TaskPlan version: tuvl/v2 metadata: { name: refund-request, spec: specs/refund-request.md, spec_hash: 9f2c… } spec: tasks: - id: T3 title: Route refunds by amount (decide rules) type: agent # model | workflow | agent | artifact | integration | test | policy | manual spec_ref: { anchor: flow-refund-request, hash: 41ad… } target: { workflow: refund_request, agent: check_amount } depends_on: [T2] - id: T7 title: "Example: a small refund is paid automatically" type: test spec_ref: { anchor: acceptance, hash: 7be0… } target: { workflow: refund_request, example: a small refund is paid automatically } - id: T9 title: Payments API credentials type: manual # only manual tasks set a status target: { workflow: refund_request, agent: pay_refund } status: todo One task per new model, per step, per example, and a manual task per external integration ( tool http / mcp ); dependencies follow the flow. No estimates. After a spec change the agent adds tasks for new steps and marks removed ones obsolete: true (never deletes them). Rule Finding P001 ✗ The file isn't a valid TaskPlan , or a non-manual task has no target P002 ✗ A task targets something the spec doesn't declare (model, flow, step or example) P003 ! Coverage: a new model, step, example or external integration has no task (or there is no task list yet) P004 ✗ A task carries an estimate ( effort ) or a hand-set status (only manual tasks may) P005 ! A task's spec section changed since it was written — the agent should update it
docs.title: 4. The task list

docs.text: Status Rule todo Target agent is pending , the target file is absent, or an example has no generated test in_progress Target exists but validate reports errors on it, or it contradicts the spec ( verify spec ) implemented Target validates cleanly and matches the spec tested A passing Test covers it (stubbed results don't count), and its acceptance examples pass done Nothing blocks ship : lock current, no warnings on the target blocked (overlay) The spec has blocking lint spec findings, or a depends_on task isn't done stale (overlay) The spec section changed since the task was written Only type: manual tasks take a manual status. Models and artifacts skip tested . A task tuvl can't measure is untracked . tuvl list tasks --json # derived statuses (runs the tests offline; --no-tests caps at implemented) tuvl list tasks --strict # exit 1 unless every live task is done and none is blocked or stale tuvl show drift # stale tasks and spec sections no task covers
docs.title: Derived status

docs.text: tuvl generate code [<workflow>] [--check] — deterministic, no model: Output Rule agents/_generated/schemas.py <Id>In / <Id>Out models per agent (per-signal variants, <Id>Signal ), <Workflow>Input , <Workflow>End . Never hand-edited agents/<run>.py A stub per code agent when missing; otherwise a libcst merge that regenerates decorator, signature and docstring and keeps parameter names and the body artifacts/<name>.md A prompt placeholder for a missing artifact:// referenced by an llm / loop agent decide agents A block with neither rules nor model gets one never-matching rule per enum value tests/<workflow>/<example>.yaml Test documents from the spec's tuvl-example blocks; hand-written tests are never touched --check exits 1 if anything would change (the CI drift gate). tuvl never writes function bodies.
docs.title: 5. Codegen

docs.text: tuvl generate lock writes tuvl.lock : the tuvl version, each AgentModel's model id, each artifact:// ref's version and sha256, judge and decision-model versions, and each allowed MCP tool's input-schema hash (listed live; --no-mcp compares by name only). tuvl verify lock verifies it; tuvl ship requires it (V024) and pins the locked tuvl version in the image.
docs.title: 6. Lock

docs.text: tuvl lint spec && tuvl lint project --strict && tuvl generate code --check && tuvl verify lock && tuvl run tests --strict && tuvl verify spec --strict && tuvl list tasks --strict tuvl init <name> --sample creates a project that passes this gate as created.
docs.title: 7. The CI gate

docs.text: tuvl serve mcp [-d <project>] [--allow-write] serves the same operations over MCP (stdio): validate , spec_check , spec_verify , spec_status , spec_diff , get_contract , list_agents , explain_error , get_run , get_run_events , codegen , test ; with --allow-write also codegen_write , run_workflow , pin_fixture . It refuses TUVL_ENV=production . .agents/skills/ (refreshed by tuvl update skills [--diff] , mirrored to .claude/skills/ ): tuvl-spec , tuvl-plan , tuvl-task-loop , agent-code , agent-tool , agent-llm , agent-loop , agent-decide , agent-human , agent-map , agent-parallel , tuvl-data , tuvl-test , tuvl-harden , tuvl-ship , plus a root AGENTS.md with the non-negotiable rules. Every read command has --json with a documented schema ( /dev/schema/cli in dev mode).
docs.title: Coding agents

docs.text: Storage ¶ Workflows read and write files — invoices, attachments, exports, model inputs — through named stores . A store is declared once in storage/*.yaml and points at S3 (or any S3-compatible service), Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, or a directory on the engine host. tuvl talks to them with its own HTTP client; no cloud SDK is installed. Declare a store ¶ kind: Storage version: v1 metadata: name: invoices # the name workflows use spec: provider: s3 # s3 | azure | gcs | local bucket: acme-invoices region: eu-west-1 access_key: ${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID} secret_key: ${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY} prefix: invoices/ # every key lives under this prefix max_object_bytes: 16777216 # per put/get through the tool (default 16 MiB, ceiling 64 MiB) Field Applies to Description provider all s3 , azure , gcs or local prefix all Keys are confined under it; list never shows keys outside it readonly all Refuses put , copy , delete and presign with PUT max_object_bytes all Largest object the tool writes or reads (default 16 MiB, at most 64 MiB) presign_max_seconds all Longest lifetime of a presigned URL (default 3600) timeout all Request timeout in seconds (default 30) endpoint s3, azure, gcs Service URL. https , or http for localhost only bucket , region , path_style s3, gcs path_style defaults to true with an endpoint access_key , secret_key , session_token s3, gcs ${ENV} references. GCS uses them as HMAC keys role_arn s3 Role for web identity (EKS); also read from AWS_ROLE_ARN account , container azure Storage account and container account_key , sas_token azure ${ENV} references; with neither, a managed identity is used credentials , access_token , project gcs Service-account JSON (or path to it) or a bearer token, as ${ENV} references root local Directory, relative to the project (default ./data/storage ) Secrets are ${ENV_VAR} references only. A literal key in the YAML is a validation error. ${VAR:default} is accepted; a variable with no value and no default fails when the store is opened. Credentials ¶ The first source that yields credentials is used. Provider Order S3 access_key / secret_key → AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY → web identity ( AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE , EKS) → ECS container credentials → EC2 instance role (IMDSv2) Azure account_key → sas_token → workload identity ( AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE , AKS) → managed identity GCS access_key / secret_key (HMAC) → access_token → service-account JSON → metadata server (GKE, GCE) Short-lived tokens are cached and refreshed a minute before they expire. Not built in: AWS shared config and SSO profiles, assume-role chains, az login and gcloud user credentials. Run with a role, a workload identity or a key instead. Other services ¶ Service Setup MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2 provider: s3 with the service's endpoint Google Cloud Storage with HMAC keys provider: gcs with access_key and secret_key (this also enables presign ) Azurite provider: azure , endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1 Use a store in a workflow ¶ storage is the fourth tool variant, next to db , http and mcp . agents: - id: save_invoice engine: tool inputs: { ticket_id: str, pdf_b64: str } outputs: { blob: json } tool: use: storage store: invoices op: put key: "{{ ticket_id }}/invoice.pdf" body: "{{ pdf_b64 }}" encoding: base64 content_type: application/pdf routes: { default: next, conflict: END.exists, error: END.failed } op Fields Result (the single output) Effect put key , body , encoding ( text , base64 , json ), content_type , metadata , if_exists ( fail or overwrite ) the blob write get key , as ( text , json , base64 ), max_bytes (default 1 MiB) the content read head key the blob read list prefix , limit (1–1000), cursor the list of blobs read copy key , to_key , to_store , if_exists the new blob write delete key none destructive presign key , method ( GET , PUT ), expires_in the URL read ( GET ), write ( PUT ) A blob is {store, key, size, content_type, etag, sha256, modified} , declared as json . The key is relative to the store's prefix. sha256 is computed on put . A local store keeps it in .meta/<key>.json beside the file, so head and list do not read the file again; a file written by an older version is hashed when it is read. key , to_key , prefix , cursor , body and metadata are templates ( {{ x }} ). With several outputs, map fills each from the result, as http.map does: map: { text: content, size: blob.size } . get exposes content and blob ; list exposes items and cursor ; presign exposes url and expires_at . Signals. get , head and copy emit not_found ; put and copy with if_exists: fail emit conflict ; put , get and copy may emit too_large . The validator requires the first two to be routed. delete of a missing key succeeds. A put whose key already holds identical content (same SHA-256) succeeds, so a retried step does not report a false conflict. Different content with if_exists: fail is a conflict . Object bytes never enter the run journal; a step records the store, op, key, size and SHA-256. A get result does land in run state as the step's output, so keep max_bytes small and move large files with presign . presign hands a person or another system a time-limited URL to download or upload a file without moving it through a run. Local stores have none. In code agents ¶ @agent("archive") async def archive(inp, ctx): store = ctx.storage("invoices") blob = await store.put(f"{inp.id}.json", payload, content_type="application/json") return {"blob": blob.to_dict()} ctx.storage(name) returns the store with put , get , head , list , delete , copy and presign . Inside an agent with effect: read the store is read-only. Calls move whole objects up to max_object_bytes . Uploads from callers ¶ A trigger can accept multipart/form-data . Each file input is written to a store and the run gets a reference to it, so a person can attach a file in one call: spec: trigger: http: path: /api/invoices upload: { store: inbox, prefix: in/, max_bytes: 5242880, max_files: 3, accept: [application/pdf, image/*] } input: invoice: file # form part "invoice" attachments: list[file]? note: str? # other parts are text; a list or object is sent as JSON text agents: - id: read engine: tool tool: { use: storage, store: inbox, op: get, key: "{{ invoice.key }}", as: base64 } inputs: { invoice: file } outputs: { content: str } A file value has store , key , name , size , content_type and sha256 . {{ invoice.key }} works anywhere an expression does; a code agent reads it with await ctx.read_file(inp.invoice) . Agents can pass it to a child workflow or a human form. Authenticated first. The caller is checked before any byte is read, so an unauthorised request stores nothing. Limits are enforced while the body streams. max_bytes (per file, at most the store's max_object_bytes ) is 413 , max_files and part limits are 400 , a content type outside accept is 415 , a field that is not a file input is 422 . accept checks the type the client declares. Keys are generated. The object lives at <prefix><random id>/<sanitised name> ; the client's name is kept only as name . A file named ../../x cannot leave the prefix. A reference cannot be forged. A JSON body or query that names a file input is 422 : the only way to get a reference is to upload through the route (a workflow or schedule can still pass one on). Nothing is left behind by a refused request. Files stored for a request whose input is then refused ( 422 ) are deleted. Files of a run that starts stay: set a lifecycle rule on the prefix to expire them. The same body works on POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs (one part per input, no input wrapper), which is what @tuvl/client uses when an input is a File or Blob . Files are held in memory while they are stored, so max_bytes is also a memory bound. Larger files should go straight to the bucket with a presign PUT. MCP export cannot take a file input. Insight's Run form has a file picker and the trigger panel edits the upload settings. Safety ¶ Concern Rule Keys Relative, forward-slashed, at most 1024 bytes, no .. , no empty or . segments, no control characters. A rendered key that breaks this fails the step Prefix Every key is placed under prefix ; list cannot leave it Local disk Paths are resolved through symlinks and must stay inside root Endpoints Only from the store file, never from a workflow; https , or http for localhost Secrets ${ENV} references only; never in logs, spans, the journal or errors. Presigned URLs are not journaled Read-only Enforced by the validator and again by the client Destructive delete has the destructive effect, so policy.require_human_before and loop-tool approval apply Logs httpx request logs have sig , X-Amz-Signature and token query values redacted Validation ¶ Code Check V030 The store exists V031 The op is allowed on the store ( readonly ) V032 A literal key or to_key is safe V033 presign.expires_in is within the store's presign_max_seconds V034 The Storage file is valid: provider fields, ${ENV} secrets, https endpoint V037 http.upload is consistent: a file input exists, the store exists, is writable and holds max_bytes An op that is missing a field, or has one it does not take, is a schema error (V001). V004 requires routing not_found and conflict where they can occur, and V007 checks the output type ( json for a blob, str for get text or base64 and presign , json for get ... as: json , list[json] for list ). Command line and Insight ¶ tuvl check storage # list, put, head, get, delete a probe object in every store tuvl check storage invoices tuvl list objects invoices 2026/ tuvl check system # also lists stores and the environment variables they still need Insight → Configure → Storage lists the stores, shows missing environment variables, checks a connection and browses objects read-only. New stores are YAML files in storage/ . Operations ¶ Retries. Connection errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx are retried up to three times with backoff; these operations are idempotent, and exclusive writes use a precondition ( If-None-Match: * , ifGenerationMatch=0 ) so a retry cannot overwrite. Telemetry. Each call is an OpenTelemetry span storage <op> with the provider, store and op. Keys and URLs are never attributes. Local stores in production. tuvl ship adds one PersistentVolumeClaim ( storage.local in values.yaml : size , storageClass , accessMode , existingClaim ) and mounts it at each local store's root, with a pod fsGroup so the non-root user can write. With split: true the API and worker pods share it: set storage.local.accessMode=ReadWriteMany and a class that supports it. Cloud stores need no volume. storage/ is on the image allowlist; a project shipped earlier needs tuvl ship --force once (ship warns when storage/ would be left out). Limits. Tool and ctx.storage calls move whole objects (default 16 MiB, at most 64 MiB). Server-side copy is native on S3-compatible stores and GCS; on Azure it reads and writes through the engine. Testing against emulators ¶ The opt-in tests in tests/storage/test_services.py run one contract suite against real services and skip any that are not running: docker run -d -p 19000:9000 -e RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY=testkey -e RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY=testsecret123 rustfs/rustfs /data docker run -d -p 10000:10000 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-storage/azurite azurite-blob --blobHost 0.0.0.0 --skipApiVersionCheck docker run -d -p 14443:4443 fsouza/fake-gcs-server -scheme http -port 4443 -public-host localhost:14443 uv run pytest tests/storage

The key is relative to the store's prefix. sha256 is computed on put . A local store keeps it in .meta/<key>.json beside the file, so head and list do not read the file again; a file written by an older version is hashed when it is read. key , to_key , prefix , cursor , body and metadata are templates ( {{ x }} ). With several outputs, map fills each from the result, as http.map does: map: { text: content, size: blob.size } . get exposes content and blob ; list exposes items and cursor ; presign exposes url and expires_at . Signals. get , head and copy emit not_found ; put and copy with if_exists: fail emit conflict ; put , get and copy may emit too_large . The validator requires the first two to be routed. delete of a missing key succeeds. A put whose key already holds identical content (same SHA-256) succeeds, so a retried step does not report a false conflict. Different content with if_exists: fail is a conflict . Object bytes never enter the run journal; a step records the store, op, key, size and SHA-256. A get result does land in run state as the step's output, so keep max_bytes small and move large files with presign . presign hands a person or another system a time-limited URL to download or upload a file without moving it through a run. Local stores have none.
docs.title: Use a store in a workflow

docs.text: @agent("archive") async def archive(inp, ctx): store = ctx.storage("invoices") blob = await store.put(f"{inp.id}.json", payload, content_type="application/json") return {"blob": blob.to_dict()} ctx.storage(name) returns the store with put , get , head , list , delete , copy and presign . Inside an agent with effect: read the store is read-only. Calls move whole objects up to max_object_bytes .
docs.title: In code agents

docs.text: A trigger can accept multipart/form-data . Each file input is written to a store and the run gets a reference to it, so a person can attach a file in one call: spec: trigger: http: path: /api/invoices upload: { store: inbox, prefix: in/, max_bytes: 5242880, max_files: 3, accept: [application/pdf, image/*] } input: invoice: file # form part "invoice" attachments: list[file]? note: str? # other parts are text; a list or object is sent as JSON text agents: - id: read engine: tool tool: { use: storage, store: inbox, op: get, key: "{{ invoice.key }}", as: base64 } inputs: { invoice: file } outputs: { content: str } A file value has store , key , name , size , content_type and sha256 . {{ invoice.key }} works anywhere an expression does; a code agent reads it with await ctx.read_file(inp.invoice) . Agents can pass it to a child workflow or a human form. Authenticated first. The caller is checked before any byte is read, so an unauthorised request stores nothing. Limits are enforced while the body streams. max_bytes (per file, at most the store's max_object_bytes ) is 413 , max_files and part limits are 400 , a content type outside accept is 415 , a field that is not a file input is 422 . accept checks the type the client declares. Keys are generated. The object lives at <prefix><random id>/<sanitised name> ; the client's name is kept only as name . A file named ../../x cannot leave the prefix. A reference cannot be forged. A JSON body or query that names a file input is 422 : the only way to get a reference is to upload through the route (a workflow or schedule can still pass one on). Nothing is left behind by a refused request. Files stored for a request whose input is then refused ( 422 ) are deleted. Files of a run that starts stay: set a lifecycle rule on the prefix to expire them. The same body works on POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs (one part per input, no input wrapper), which is what @tuvl/client uses when an input is a File or Blob . Files are held in memory while they are stored, so max_bytes is also a memory bound. Larger files should go straight to the bucket with a presign PUT. MCP export cannot take a file input. Insight's Run form has a file picker and the trigger panel edits the upload settings.
docs.title: Uploads from callers

docs.text: Concern Rule Keys Relative, forward-slashed, at most 1024 bytes, no .. , no empty or . segments, no control characters. A rendered key that breaks this fails the step Prefix Every key is placed under prefix ; list cannot leave it Local disk Paths are resolved through symlinks and must stay inside root Endpoints Only from the store file, never from a workflow; https , or http for localhost Secrets ${ENV} references only; never in logs, spans, the journal or errors. Presigned URLs are not journaled Read-only Enforced by the validator and again by the client Destructive delete has the destructive effect, so policy.require_human_before and loop-tool approval apply Logs httpx request logs have sig , X-Amz-Signature and token query values redacted
docs.title: Safety

docs.text: Code Check V030 The store exists V031 The op is allowed on the store ( readonly ) V032 A literal key or to_key is safe V033 presign.expires_in is within the store's presign_max_seconds V034 The Storage file is valid: provider fields, ${ENV} secrets, https endpoint V037 http.upload is consistent: a file input exists, the store exists, is writable and holds max_bytes An op that is missing a field, or has one it does not take, is a schema error (V001). V004 requires routing not_found and conflict where they can occur, and V007 checks the output type ( json for a blob, str for get text or base64 and presign , json for get ... as: json , list[json] for list ).
docs.title: Validation

docs.text: tuvl check storage # list, put, head, get, delete a probe object in every store tuvl check storage invoices tuvl list objects invoices 2026/ tuvl check system # also lists stores and the environment variables they still need Insight → Configure → Storage lists the stores, shows missing environment variables, checks a connection and browses objects read-only. New stores are YAML files in storage/ .
docs.title: Command line and Insight

docs.text: Retries. Connection errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx are retried up to three times with backoff; these operations are idempotent, and exclusive writes use a precondition ( If-None-Match: * , ifGenerationMatch=0 ) so a retry cannot overwrite. Telemetry. Each call is an OpenTelemetry span storage <op> with the provider, store and op. Keys and URLs are never attributes. Local stores in production. tuvl ship adds one PersistentVolumeClaim ( storage.local in values.yaml : size , storageClass , accessMode , existingClaim ) and mounts it at each local store's root, with a pod fsGroup so the non-root user can write. With split: true the API and worker pods share it: set storage.local.accessMode=ReadWriteMany and a class that supports it. Cloud stores need no volume. storage/ is on the image allowlist; a project shipped earlier needs tuvl ship --force once (ship warns when storage/ would be left out). Limits. Tool and ctx.storage calls move whole objects (default 16 MiB, at most 64 MiB). Server-side copy is native on S3-compatible stores and GCS; on Azure it reads and writes through the engine.
docs.title: Operations

docs.text: The opt-in tests in tests/storage/test_services.py run one contract suite against real services and skip any that are not running: docker run -d -p 19000:9000 -e RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY=testkey -e RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY=testsecret123 rustfs/rustfs /data docker run -d -p 10000:10000 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-storage/azurite azurite-blob --blobHost 0.0.0.0 --skipApiVersionCheck docker run -d -p 14443:4443 fsouza/fake-gcs-server -scheme http -port 4443 -public-host localhost:14443 uv run pytest tests/storage
