docs.text: tuvl 2.0 — Agentic Manual ¶ Audience: developers and coding agents authoring tuvl projects. Contract: this manual is the ground truth for tuvl 2.0 documents. Never invent kinds, engines, fields or signals that are not described here. When in doubt, ask tuvl: tuvl lint project --json , tuvl list tasks --json , or the tuvl serve mcp tools. Deeper references: runtime · engines · decide · loop and tools · judges · spec-driven workflow · Insight · API · CLI · security · observability 1. What tuvl is ¶ tuvl runs typed workflows of agents . A workflow is a graph: each agent has a typed contract ( inputs , outputs , the signals it emits) and an engine that implements it — a Python function, a database/HTTP/MCP call, a rules table, one model call, a bounded tool loop, or a person. Signals pick the next agent or a named end. Every run is durable and journaled : it survives restarts, can wait for people, and can be replayed as a test fixture. Work is spec-driven : intent lives in specs/<name>.md , in a grammar tuvl lint spec checks; the coding agent writes the task list and builds; deterministic tooling ( verify spec , generate code , lint project , run tests , generate lock ) tracks the project to done. YAML is the single source of truth — the Insight canvas and coding agents edit the same files. 2. Project layout ¶ my-project/ ├── pyproject.toml / uv.lock # Python deps (uv) ├── tuvl.lock # reproducibility pins (tuvl generate lock) ├── .env / .env.example # secrets — never in YAML ├── config.yaml # optional ProjectConfig (dirs, …) ├── specs/ # <name>.md (intent) + <name>.tasks.yaml (TaskPlan) ├── workflows/ # kind: Workflow ├── agents/ # code-engine implementations, one @agent per file │ └── _generated/ # codegen output — never hand-edited ├── models/ # kind: ModelDefinition / EmbeddingRegistry / CollectionRegistry ├── llms/ # kind: AgentModel (type llm | decision) ├── datasources/ # kind: DataSource ├── federation/ # kind: FederationProvider ├── artifacts/ # prompt/steering/skill .md + kind: Artifact YAML ├── tests/ # kind: Test; fixtures/ holds pinned run journals ├── fixtures/judge/ # labelled judge calibration subjects ├── .agents/ # coding-agent rules + skills (tuvl update skills) └── .tuvl/ # system.yaml, layout/, dev session, judge cache (managed) Folder names are conventions: discovery is recursive and dispatched by kind: . Document kinds (closed set) ¶ kind Notes Workflow version: tuvl/v2 (§4) ModelDefinition Tables and their typed variants ( Order , Order.create , …) AgentModel spec.type: llm (default) or decision ( decide ) DataSource , RedisConfig Connections EmbeddingRegistry / EmbeddingConfig , CollectionRegistry / CollectionConfig Vector search FederationProvider OAuth/OIDC login Artifact Versioned assets (below) Test version: tuvl/v2 (§8) TaskPlan version: tuvl/v2 , the task list the coding agent writes (checked by lint spec ) ProjectConfig , TelemetryConfig , SystemConfig Project and system settings Every document uses the envelope kind + metadata + spec . Workflow , Test and TaskPlan carry version: tuvl/v2 ; a 1.x-shaped workflow fails to load. Artifact types (closed set) ¶ Type Class Used by prompt prose .md llm.system , llm.prompt steering prose .md loop.steering skill prose .md llm.skills , loop.skills guardrail YAML guardrails.{input,output,tools} hook YAML agent/workflow hooks (observe-only) mcp YAML tool.use: mcp , loop MCP tools Storage YAML ( storage/ ) tool.use: storage , ctx.storage(name) — see docs/storage.md judge YAML output guardrails, tests, supervisor ( judges ) rules YAML decide.rules: artifact://… (reusable decision tables) Reference with artifact://name@N ; pin @N for production (an unpinned ref is a V017 warning). Content is capped at 512 KB. 3. Types, expressions and templates ¶ Type language ¶ Used in inputs , outputs , trigger input, end types, human forms and tests. Form Meaning str , int , float , bool , date , datetime , uuid , json Scalars file A reference to an uploaded file: {store, key, name, size, content_type, sha256} . Only a trigger's multipart upload creates one (see http.upload ); agents pass it on enum[a, b, c] Closed string set list[T] List of T Order A ModelDefinition 's read shape (model names start uppercase) Order.create / .update / .read / .expanded A specific model variant T? Optional (absent or null; defaults to null ) { type: T, description: str, default: any } Long form YAML pitfalls: inside a flow mapping, quote anything with a comma or ? — outputs: { verdict: "enum[strong, weak]", note: "str?" } . Avoid bare on / off / yes / no as keys or values; route keys true: / false: are accepted and normalised to strings. TEL (tuvl expression language) ¶ Used in decide.rules[].when , tool approval.when , test assertions and {{ }} templates. Paths: order.total , items[0].sku , args.amount — null-safe (a missing key yields null ). Literals: strings, numbers, booleans, null , lists. Operators: == != > >= < <= , in , not in , and or not , + - * / , parentheses. Comparisons don't chain; and / or / not need booleans (no truthiness); ordering against null is false . Functions (closed set): len , lower , upper , contains , starts_with , ends_with , is_empty , now , days_between . Statically type-checked by tuvl lint project against the agent's declared inputs (V008): every root name must be an input, fields are checked against models, enum literals must be enum values. Templates ¶ A string containing {{ expr }} is a template. A value that is exactly one {{ expr }} keeps the expression's type (a number stays a number); otherwise values are interpolated as text. Every path a template reads must be a declared input of that agent (V008). 4. The workflow document ¶ kind: Workflow version: tuvl/v2 metadata: name: refund_flow # unique; snake_case description: Handle a refund request end to end. # required for MCP export required_scope: refunds:write # optional token scope gate required_group: support # optional IAM group gate spec: models: [Order, Refund] # allow-list for tool:db and ctx.db trigger: http: { path: /api/refunds, method: POST, public: false, sync_timeout: 30s } # enabled: false unmounts it schedule: "0 * * * *" # optional cron (UTC); or { cron, enabled, input: {…} } tenants: [acme, globex] # multi_tenant mode: one scheduled run per tenant mcp: { enabled: true } # optional MCP export (api.md) input: { order_id: uuid, reason: str, message: str } start: load_order # entry agent; defaults to the first agent transaction: per_agent # per_agent (default) | per_run agents: [ ... ] # §5 outputs: # named ends default: { status: 200, body: { refund_id: "{{ refund.id }}" } } rejected: { status: 200, body: { status: rejected } } failed: { status: 500, rollback: true, body: { error: refund failed } } policy: { max_tokens_per_run: 5000 } # §7 supervisor: { ... } # default supervisor for loop agents hooks: [artifact://audit-log@1] Graph rules ¶ No implicit edges. Every signal an agent can emit must be mapped in routes (V004). Route targets: an agent id, END (= END.default ) or END.<name> for a declared output. Agents used only as loop tools or compensators are off-spine and can't be route targets (V003). Cycles are allowed, but each must pass through a bounded-budget or human agent (V005 warning). Named ends ¶ Field Meaning status HTTP status (default 200) body Response mapping: templates or literals type Optional declared body type (field map); otherwise inferred from body for OpenAPI/MCP rollback Reaching this end compensates every completed agent with a compensate Every template in a body must reference keys produced on every path to that end (V022). Triggers ¶ http : default-deny — a valid bearer token is required unless public: true (which can't be combined with required_scope / required_group , V019). The response is the end's status / body , or 202 with the run descriptor when the run outlives sync_timeout or waits on a person. spec.webhooks declares signed notifications to your own HTTPS endpoints when a run completes, fails, aborts, waits or finishes a named agent: { name, url: ${ENV}, secret: ${ENV}, events, stages } . They carry only a run id and what happened; the receiver pulls the run. Off unless TUVL_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=true . See docs/webhooks.md . http.upload ( { store, prefix, max_bytes, max_files, accept } ) lets the route take multipart/form-data : each file / list[file] trigger input is stored in the named kind: Storage store under a generated key and the run receives its reference, never the bytes. A JSON body cannot carry a file. See docs/storage.md . http.enabled: false keeps the route's settings but does not mount it; the workflow can still be started with POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs . schedule : cron in UTC; each slot fires once across all workers. The object form { cron, enabled, input } adds an off switch and the input every scheduled run starts with — input must satisfy trigger.input (V019). A workflow can have both an http trigger and a schedule. In multi_tenant mode add tenants: [acme, …] : each slot starts one run per tenant (see docs/runtime.md ). mcp.enabled : lists the workflow as a tool on /mcp ( API ). Every workflow can also be started with POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs . 5. The agent contract ¶ - id: score_candidate # [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, unique, stable description: Score a CV against similar profiles # required; also the tool description engine: llm # pending | code | tool | decide | llm | loop | human inputs: { cv: str, similar: list[Candidate] } outputs: { score: int, verdict: "enum[strong, weak]" } budget: timeout: 30s max_tokens: 4000 # llm / loop / decide with an LLM model max_iterations: 8 # loop max_tool_calls: 12 # loop retry: { attempts: 2, errors: [timeout, rate_limit, parse_error, transient], backoff: 1.5 } llm: { ... } # engine parameters live under the engine's name guardrails: { input: [...], output: [...] } # llm, loop hooks: [artifact://trace-hook@1] compensate: undo_score # off-spine agent run on rollback effect: write # code (and tool overrides): read | write | destructive routes: { strong: persist, weak: reject, error: END.failed } Field Rule id , description , engine , routes Required inputs / outputs Typed (§3); may be {} engine key Required for every engine except pending ; must match engine budget Required fields depend on the engine (§7, V011) Per-signal outputs ¶ When outcomes produce different data, key outputs by routed signal: outputs: valid: { invoice: Invoice.create, verification: json } incomplete: { verification: json } A field on several signals must have the same type. Data flow (V006/V007) uses the set for the signal on each edge. decide agents can't use this form. Context isolation ¶ An agent sees only its declared inputs (plus ctx for code agents). Undeclared keys are invisible. Its result is validated against outputs ; a missing, extra or mistyped key is error ( contract_violation ). Only declared outputs merge into the run context. Two agents on one path writing the same key is a V009 warning. Signals ¶ An agent emits exactly one signal per invocation: Normal: default for single-outcome agents; the enum values used for routing ( llm , decide , human.route_on , loop outcome); explicit strings from code agents. Reserved (must be mapped where the engine can emit them): Engine Reserved signals all except pending error (unmapped → V004 warning; the run fails) tool db read / delete : not_found · db create / update / upsert : conflict · http: http_<status> (only if mapped) · storage get / head / copy : not_found ; put / copy ( if_exists: fail ): conflict ; put / get / copy : too_large (optional) llm parse_error , timeout , budget_exceeded , guardrail_violation (with guardrails) loop max_iterations , budget_exceeded , timeout , aborted , guardrail_violation (with guardrails) decide low_confidence (with a model) human expired (with expires ) map partial (a normal signal: only with on_error: collect , when routed); an item failing in fail mode is error ( map_item_failed ) parallel partial (only with on_error: collect , when routed); a branch failing in fail mode is error ( parallel_branch_failed ) error carries an error_type in the journal: contract_violation , no_rule_matched , decision_model_unavailable , judge_unavailable , judge_uncertain , tool_args_invalid , http_error , db_error , mcp_error , storage_error , code_exception , compensation_failed , policy_violation , lease_lost , approval_expired , map_item_failed , map_too_many_items , max_depth . 6. Engines ¶ Engine Implementation Determinism LLM cost pending none — a typed contract; runs as a typed stub in dev and tests — 0 code an @agent Python function deterministic 0 tool db / http / mcp / storage operation deterministic 0 decide ordered rules, then an optional decision model deterministic (rules only) / bounded 0 → low llm one structured model call bounded $ loop a bounded tool-using model loop bounded $$ human a form for a person external 0 map a child workflow per item of a list, a few at a time the child's the child's × max_items parallel several different read-only agents at the same time the strongest branch's the sum of the branches Only code agents need Python. Everything else is configured in YAML. Details and full examples: engines , decide , loop and tools . # code — agents/issue_refund.py holds @agent("issue_refund") - id: issue_refund description: Calculate the refund amount and record it engine: code effect: write inputs: { order: Order, reason: str } outputs: { refund: Refund } code: { run: issue_refund } routes: { default: reply, error: END.failed } # tool — effect is derived - id: load_order description: Load the order engine: tool inputs: { order_id: uuid } outputs: { order: Order } tool: { use: db, model: Order, op: read, where: { id: "{{ order_id }}" } } routes: { default: triage, not_found: END.missing, error: END.failed } # decide — rules first; a model only when no rule matches - id: triage description: Decide how a refund is handled engine: decide inputs: { order: Order, reason: str } outputs: { route: "enum[auto_refund, manager_review, reject]" } decide: rules: - { when: "order.total > 500", then: manager_review } - { when: "reason == 'fraud_flag'", then: reject } - { when: "true", then: auto_refund } routes: { auto_refund: issue_refund, manager_review: approval, reject: END.rejected, error: END.failed } # llm — one structured call; inputs become the prompt's input block - id: reply description: Write the customer confirmation engine: llm inputs: { order: Order, refund: Refund } outputs: { text: str } budget: { timeout: 20s, max_tokens: 1500 } llm: { model: default, system: artifact://support-voice@3, prompt: Confirm the refund briefly. } routes: { default: END, parse_error: END.failed, timeout: END.failed, budget_exceeded: END.failed, error: END.failed } # human — the outputs are the form - id: approval description: A manager approves a large refund engine: human inputs: { order: Order } outputs: { approved: bool, note: "str?" } human: { title: "Refund {{ order.id }}", show: [order], required_group: support_manager, expires: 48h, route_on: approved } routes: { "true": issue_refund, "false": END.rejected, expired: END.failed, error: END.failed } 7. Determinism, budgets and policy ¶ A workflow's profile counts its agents per class ("11 agents · 8 deterministic · 2 bounded · 1 external"); tuvl lint project prints it with the worst-case tokens per run (the maximum over paths of summed max_tokens , including guardrail judges and child workflows). Required budgets (V011): llm → max_tokens , timeout ; loop → max_iterations , max_tokens , max_tool_calls , timeout ; decide with an LLM-backed model → max_tokens , timeout . policy: max_tokens_per_run: 5000 # V020 if the worst case exceeds it max_bounded_agents: 2 require_human_before: [destructive] # every path to a destructive effect passes a human or approval model_only_decisions: warn # warn | error | allow (V013; allow = accepted on purpose, reviewed) max_depth: 2 # workflow-as-tool nesting allow_secure_to_llm: false # secure model fields never reach a model (V020) 8. Testing ¶ kind: Test version: tuvl/v2 metadata: { name: small-damaged-refund-is-automatic } spec: workflow: refund_flow given: # rows that exist before the run (in-memory database) Order: [{ id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000040", total: 40, status: delivered }] as: { user: u-customer } # the caller: the run's principal (ctx.principal) input: { order_id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000040", reason: damaged, message: "Arrived broken" } mocks: # model, external and human steps only — typed against the contract classify: { outputs: { category: damaged } } replay: tests/fixtures/refund_flow/small-refund.journal.json # serve recorded model/tool results expect: end: default # or wait: human | approval path: [load_order, triage, issue_refund, reply] # or path_includes: [...] decisions: { triage: { source: "rule#3" } } output: { status: 200, body: { amount: 40 } } # partial match assertions: ["output.body.amount == 40"] judge: - { judge: artifact://refund-reply-quality@2, target: "{{ text }}" } tuvl run tests is offline : tool: db and code agents run for real against an in-memory database seeded by given: , with the as: caller as the principal; an unmocked human agent stops the run (assert with expect.wait ); unmocked model/HTTP/MCP agents fail with a hint to mock or replay them ( --live lets them call out). That database is in autocommit, so it keeps writes Postgres would roll back (an agent's error outcome, a retried attempt, a per_run rollback): test rollback against Postgres. Honest results: a test whose path goes through an unmocked pending agent (a typed placeholder) is stubbed , not passed — it is reported, doesn't count towards task status, and fails tuvl run tests --strict (the CI gate). Mock policy: mock what is non-deterministic, external or human ( llm , loop , decide with a model, tool http / mcp , human ). Mocking business logic ( code , tool db , decide rules) is warning T001 — seed given: rows and set as: instead. expect order: structure ( end / wait , path , decisions ) → output → assertions → judge . Pin any run as a fixture ( tuvl pin run <run_id> or Insight 📌); replay: then serves its recorded engine results with zero tokens. Judges are cached and calibrated ( judges ). 9. The development loop ¶ tuvl create spec refund-automation # write intent: specs/refund-automation.md tuvl lint spec # the grammar: fix every blocking finding # the coding agent writes specs/refund-automation.tasks.yaml (skill tuvl-plan) tuvl list tasks --json # derived task statuses — pick the next unblocked task # build it (YAML engine blocks; Python bodies only for code agents) tuvl generate code # schemas, code-agent stubs, prompt placeholders, tests tuvl verify spec # does the build match the spec, step by step? tuvl lint spec && tuvl lint project --strict && tuvl generate code --check && tuvl verify lock && tuvl run tests --strict && tuvl verify spec --strict && tuvl list tasks --strict That last line is the CI gate . Task statuses are derived ( todo → in_progress → implemented → tested → done , with blocked and stale overlays) — never set them by hand. See spec-driven workflow . 10. Validation rules ¶ Severity: E error, W warning (error under --strict ). tuvl lint project --json reports file:line , code and message. Code Sev Rule V001 E Unknown kind, engine, field or artifact type; missing version: tuvl/v2 V002 E Duplicate or malformed agent id V003 E Route target is not an agent, END or a declared END.<name> ; off-spine agent as a target V004 E Emittable signal unmapped, or a route for a signal never emitted (W for unmapped error ) V005 W Unreachable agent; cycle without a bounded/human guard V006 E An input isn't produced on every path to the agent V007 E Producer output type incompatible with consumer input type V008 E Template/TEL references an undeclared input or fails to type-check V009 W Two agents on one path write the same key V010 W / E (ship) pending agent present V011 E Missing required budget fields V012 E decide : enum ≠ normal route keys; rule then not in enum; model without low_confidence route V013 W Model-only decision feeds a write/destructive effect without a human/approval/compensate V014 E Loop tool source unresolved; MCP tool without allow ; nesting too deep (W: MCP schema differs from lock) V015 W Write/destructive tool without compensate when the run continues; declared effect weaker than derived V016 E human : form ≠ outputs; bad route_on ; expires without expired route V017 E Artifact ref unresolved or wrong type (W: unpinned) V018 E Model used by tool: db / ctx.db not in spec.models ; pinned model version disabled V019 E public: true with scope/group; invalid cron; MCP export without description V020 E Policy violation (worst-case tokens, bounded cap, human-before-destructive, secure field to a model) V021 E transaction: per_run with human/approval/async V022 E End body references a key not produced on every path; undeclared end V023 W Judge calibration below min_agreement (test time) V024 E (ship) tuvl.lock missing or stale V025 E code agent run not registered, or its signature doesn't match the generated schema V026 E Decision provider not installed, or unpinned hosted decision model (W) V027 E (ship) The image build context isn't the tuvl allowlist, or would contain development files V028 E A model reference ( llm , loop , decide.model.ref ) is not a defined AgentModel or a provider/model id V029 W / E (ship) A model's credentials aren't declared: literal api_key , or an unknown provider without api_key V030 E A tool: storage agent names a store that no kind: Storage file declares V031 E A write op ( put , copy , delete , presign PUT) targets a readonly store V032 E A literal storage key or to_key is unsafe: absolute, .. , empty segment, control character V033 E presign.expires_in exceeds the store's presign_max_seconds V034 E A kind: Storage file is invalid: provider fields, a literal secret instead of ${ENV} , or a non-https endpoint V035 E map : over is not a list input; the workflow is unknown, is this workflow, or lacks the as / with inputs; a required child input is not supplied V036 E map : the mapped workflow has a human or pending agent, or a loop tool that needs approval V039 E llm.stream_tokens with an output guardrail, or stream_field missing, ambiguous or not a str output V040 E parallel : a branch is not read-only (a write or destructive tool, a code agent with a write effect, an MCP tool) V041 E parallel : a branch reads an input the step does not take, two branches produce the same output, or the step's outputs are not exactly the branches' (optional with on_error: collect ) V042 E parallel under transaction: per_run V043 E memory : an owner named from input on a public trigger; write names a field the agent does not have or one that carries secure model fields V038 E / W A webhook's stages names an agent the workflow does not have (E); allow_private lets it reach internal addresses and plain http (W) V037 E / W File uploads: http.upload without a file input, an unknown, read-only or too-small store, a file nested deeper than file / list[file] , or a file input with MCP export (E); a file input on a route with no upload , or a public upload (W) tuvl serve mcp 's explain_error tool explains any code. 11. Rules for coding agents ¶ Never infer project state — ask tuvl ( --json output or tuvl serve mcp tools). Specs drive the work ; task status is derived, never set. Never hand-edit generated files : agents/_generated/ , tests with metadata.generated_from , tuvl.lock . Regenerate them. Only code agents need Python , and only the function body; tuvl generate code owns the decorator, signature and docstring. Never invent fields, engines or kinds. Every change ends green on the CI gate (§9). PII fields are secure: true and never reach a model; secrets live in .env .
docs.title: Agentic Manual

docs.text: Audience: developers and coding agents authoring tuvl projects. Contract: this manual is the ground truth for tuvl 2.0 documents. Never invent kinds, engines, fields or signals that are not described here. When in doubt, ask tuvl: tuvl lint project --json , tuvl list tasks --json , or the tuvl serve mcp tools. Deeper references: runtime · engines · decide · loop and tools · judges · spec-driven workflow · Insight · API · CLI · security · observability
docs.title: tuvl 2.0 — Agentic Manual

docs.text: tuvl runs typed workflows of agents . A workflow is a graph: each agent has a typed contract ( inputs , outputs , the signals it emits) and an engine that implements it — a Python function, a database/HTTP/MCP call, a rules table, one model call, a bounded tool loop, or a person. Signals pick the next agent or a named end. Every run is durable and journaled : it survives restarts, can wait for people, and can be replayed as a test fixture. Work is spec-driven : intent lives in specs/<name>.md , in a grammar tuvl lint spec checks; the coding agent writes the task list and builds; deterministic tooling ( verify spec , generate code , lint project , run tests , generate lock ) tracks the project to done. YAML is the single source of truth — the Insight canvas and coding agents edit the same files.
docs.title: 1. What tuvl is

docs.text: my-project/ ├── pyproject.toml / uv.lock # Python deps (uv) ├── tuvl.lock # reproducibility pins (tuvl generate lock) ├── .env / .env.example # secrets — never in YAML ├── config.yaml # optional ProjectConfig (dirs, …) ├── specs/ # <name>.md (intent) + <name>.tasks.yaml (TaskPlan) ├── workflows/ # kind: Workflow ├── agents/ # code-engine implementations, one @agent per file │ └── _generated/ # codegen output — never hand-edited ├── models/ # kind: ModelDefinition / EmbeddingRegistry / CollectionRegistry ├── llms/ # kind: AgentModel (type llm | decision) ├── datasources/ # kind: DataSource ├── federation/ # kind: FederationProvider ├── artifacts/ # prompt/steering/skill .md + kind: Artifact YAML ├── tests/ # kind: Test; fixtures/ holds pinned run journals ├── fixtures/judge/ # labelled judge calibration subjects ├── .agents/ # coding-agent rules + skills (tuvl update skills) └── .tuvl/ # system.yaml, layout/, dev session, judge cache (managed) Folder names are conventions: discovery is recursive and dispatched by kind: .
docs.title: 2. Project layout

docs.text: kind Notes Workflow version: tuvl/v2 (§4) ModelDefinition Tables and their typed variants ( Order , Order.create , …) AgentModel spec.type: llm (default) or decision ( decide ) DataSource , RedisConfig Connections EmbeddingRegistry / EmbeddingConfig , CollectionRegistry / CollectionConfig Vector search FederationProvider OAuth/OIDC login Artifact Versioned assets (below) Test version: tuvl/v2 (§8) TaskPlan version: tuvl/v2 , the task list the coding agent writes (checked by lint spec ) ProjectConfig , TelemetryConfig , SystemConfig Project and system settings Every document uses the envelope kind + metadata + spec . Workflow , Test and TaskPlan carry version: tuvl/v2 ; a 1.x-shaped workflow fails to load.
docs.title: Document kinds (closed set)

docs.text: Type Class Used by prompt prose .md llm.system , llm.prompt steering prose .md loop.steering skill prose .md llm.skills , loop.skills guardrail YAML guardrails.{input,output,tools} hook YAML agent/workflow hooks (observe-only) mcp YAML tool.use: mcp , loop MCP tools Storage YAML ( storage/ ) tool.use: storage , ctx.storage(name) — see docs/storage.md judge YAML output guardrails, tests, supervisor ( judges ) rules YAML decide.rules: artifact://… (reusable decision tables) Reference with artifact://name@N ; pin @N for production (an unpinned ref is a V017 warning). Content is capped at 512 KB.
docs.title: Artifact types (closed set)

docs.text: Used in inputs , outputs , trigger input, end types, human forms and tests. Form Meaning str , int , float , bool , date , datetime , uuid , json Scalars file A reference to an uploaded file: {store, key, name, size, content_type, sha256} . Only a trigger's multipart upload creates one (see http.upload ); agents pass it on enum[a, b, c] Closed string set list[T] List of T Order A ModelDefinition 's read shape (model names start uppercase) Order.create / .update / .read / .expanded A specific model variant T? Optional (absent or null; defaults to null ) { type: T, description: str, default: any } Long form YAML pitfalls: inside a flow mapping, quote anything with a comma or ? — outputs: { verdict: "enum[strong, weak]", note: "str?" } . Avoid bare on / off / yes / no as keys or values; route keys true: / false: are accepted and normalised to strings.
docs.title: Type language

docs.text: Used in decide.rules[].when , tool approval.when , test assertions and {{ }} templates. Paths: order.total , items[0].sku , args.amount — null-safe (a missing key yields null ). Literals: strings, numbers, booleans, null , lists. Operators: == != > >= < <= , in , not in , and or not , + - * / , parentheses. Comparisons don't chain; and / or / not need booleans (no truthiness); ordering against null is false . Functions (closed set): len , lower , upper , contains , starts_with , ends_with , is_empty , now , days_between . Statically type-checked by tuvl lint project against the agent's declared inputs (V008): every root name must be an input, fields are checked against models, enum literals must be enum values.
docs.title: TEL (tuvl expression language)

docs.text: A string containing {{ expr }} is a template. A value that is exactly one {{ expr }} keeps the expression's type (a number stays a number); otherwise values are interpolated as text. Every path a template reads must be a declared input of that agent (V008).
docs.title: Templates

docs.text: kind: Workflow version: tuvl/v2 metadata: name: refund_flow # unique; snake_case description: Handle a refund request end to end. # required for MCP export required_scope: refunds:write # optional token scope gate required_group: support # optional IAM group gate spec: models: [Order, Refund] # allow-list for tool:db and ctx.db trigger: http: { path: /api/refunds, method: POST, public: false, sync_timeout: 30s } # enabled: false unmounts it schedule: "0 * * * *" # optional cron (UTC); or { cron, enabled, input: {…} } tenants: [acme, globex] # multi_tenant mode: one scheduled run per tenant mcp: { enabled: true } # optional MCP export (api.md) input: { order_id: uuid, reason: str, message: str } start: load_order # entry agent; defaults to the first agent transaction: per_agent # per_agent (default) | per_run agents: [ ... ] # §5 outputs: # named ends default: { status: 200, body: { refund_id: "{{ refund.id }}" } } rejected: { status: 200, body: { status: rejected } } failed: { status: 500, rollback: true, body: { error: refund failed } } policy: { max_tokens_per_run: 5000 } # §7 supervisor: { ... } # default supervisor for loop agents hooks: [artifact://audit-log@1]
docs.title: 4. The workflow document

docs.text: No implicit edges. Every signal an agent can emit must be mapped in routes (V004). Route targets: an agent id, END (= END.default ) or END.<name> for a declared output. Agents used only as loop tools or compensators are off-spine and can't be route targets (V003). Cycles are allowed, but each must pass through a bounded-budget or human agent (V005 warning).
docs.title: Graph rules

docs.text: Field Meaning status HTTP status (default 200) body Response mapping: templates or literals type Optional declared body type (field map); otherwise inferred from body for OpenAPI/MCP rollback Reaching this end compensates every completed agent with a compensate Every template in a body must reference keys produced on every path to that end (V022).
docs.title: Named ends

docs.text: http : default-deny — a valid bearer token is required unless public: true (which can't be combined with required_scope / required_group , V019). The response is the end's status / body , or 202 with the run descriptor when the run outlives sync_timeout or waits on a person. spec.webhooks declares signed notifications to your own HTTPS endpoints when a run completes, fails, aborts, waits or finishes a named agent: { name, url: ${ENV}, secret: ${ENV}, events, stages } . They carry only a run id and what happened; the receiver pulls the run. Off unless TUVL_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=true . See docs/webhooks.md . http.upload ( { store, prefix, max_bytes, max_files, accept } ) lets the route take multipart/form-data : each file / list[file] trigger input is stored in the named kind: Storage store under a generated key and the run receives its reference, never the bytes. A JSON body cannot carry a file. See docs/storage.md . http.enabled: false keeps the route's settings but does not mount it; the workflow can still be started with POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs . schedule : cron in UTC; each slot fires once across all workers. The object form { cron, enabled, input } adds an off switch and the input every scheduled run starts with — input must satisfy trigger.input (V019). A workflow can have both an http trigger and a schedule. In multi_tenant mode add tenants: [acme, …] : each slot starts one run per tenant (see docs/runtime.md ). mcp.enabled : lists the workflow as a tool on /mcp ( API ). Every workflow can also be started with POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs .
docs.title: Triggers

docs.text: - id: score_candidate # [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, unique, stable description: Score a CV against similar profiles # required; also the tool description engine: llm # pending | code | tool | decide | llm | loop | human inputs: { cv: str, similar: list[Candidate] } outputs: { score: int, verdict: "enum[strong, weak]" } budget: timeout: 30s max_tokens: 4000 # llm / loop / decide with an LLM model max_iterations: 8 # loop max_tool_calls: 12 # loop retry: { attempts: 2, errors: [timeout, rate_limit, parse_error, transient], backoff: 1.5 } llm: { ... } # engine parameters live under the engine's name guardrails: { input: [...], output: [...] } # llm, loop hooks: [artifact://trace-hook@1] compensate: undo_score # off-spine agent run on rollback effect: write # code (and tool overrides): read | write | destructive routes: { strong: persist, weak: reject, error: END.failed } Field Rule id , description , engine , routes Required inputs / outputs Typed (§3); may be {} engine key Required for every engine except pending ; must match engine budget Required fields depend on the engine (§7, V011)
docs.title: 5. The agent contract

docs.text: When outcomes produce different data, key outputs by routed signal: outputs: valid: { invoice: Invoice.create, verification: json } incomplete: { verification: json } A field on several signals must have the same type. Data flow (V006/V007) uses the set for the signal on each edge. decide agents can't use this form.
docs.title: Per-signal outputs

docs.text: An agent sees only its declared inputs (plus ctx for code agents). Undeclared keys are invisible. Its result is validated against outputs ; a missing, extra or mistyped key is error ( contract_violation ). Only declared outputs merge into the run context. Two agents on one path writing the same key is a V009 warning.
docs.title: Context isolation

docs.text: An agent emits exactly one signal per invocation: Normal: default for single-outcome agents; the enum values used for routing ( llm , decide , human.route_on , loop outcome); explicit strings from code agents. Reserved (must be mapped where the engine can emit them): Engine Reserved signals all except pending error (unmapped → V004 warning; the run fails) tool db read / delete : not_found · db create / update / upsert : conflict · http: http_<status> (only if mapped) · storage get / head / copy : not_found ; put / copy ( if_exists: fail ): conflict ; put / get / copy : too_large (optional) llm parse_error , timeout , budget_exceeded , guardrail_violation (with guardrails) loop max_iterations , budget_exceeded , timeout , aborted , guardrail_violation (with guardrails) decide low_confidence (with a model) human expired (with expires ) map partial (a normal signal: only with on_error: collect , when routed); an item failing in fail mode is error ( map_item_failed ) parallel partial (only with on_error: collect , when routed); a branch failing in fail mode is error ( parallel_branch_failed ) error carries an error_type in the journal: contract_violation , no_rule_matched , decision_model_unavailable , judge_unavailable , judge_uncertain , tool_args_invalid , http_error , db_error , mcp_error , storage_error , code_exception , compensation_failed , policy_violation , lease_lost , approval_expired , map_item_failed , map_too_many_items , max_depth .
docs.title: Signals

docs.text: Engine Implementation Determinism LLM cost pending none — a typed contract; runs as a typed stub in dev and tests — 0 code an @agent Python function deterministic 0 tool db / http / mcp / storage operation deterministic 0 decide ordered rules, then an optional decision model deterministic (rules only) / bounded 0 → low llm one structured model call bounded $ loop a bounded tool-using model loop bounded $$ human a form for a person external 0 map a child workflow per item of a list, a few at a time the child's the child's × max_items parallel several different read-only agents at the same time the strongest branch's the sum of the branches Only code agents need Python. Everything else is configured in YAML. Details and full examples: engines , decide , loop and tools . # code — agents/issue_refund.py holds @agent("issue_refund") - id: issue_refund description: Calculate the refund amount and record it engine: code effect: write inputs: { order: Order, reason: str } outputs: { refund: Refund } code: { run: issue_refund } routes: { default: reply, error: END.failed } # tool — effect is derived - id: load_order description: Load the order engine: tool inputs: { order_id: uuid } outputs: { order: Order } tool: { use: db, model: Order, op: read, where: { id: "{{ order_id }}" } } routes: { default: triage, not_found: END.missing, error: END.failed } # decide — rules first; a model only when no rule matches - id: triage description: Decide how a refund is handled engine: decide inputs: { order: Order, reason: str } outputs: { route: "enum[auto_refund, manager_review, reject]" } decide: rules: - { when: "order.total > 500", then: manager_review } - { when: "reason == 'fraud_flag'", then: reject } - { when: "true", then: auto_refund } routes: { auto_refund: issue_refund, manager_review: approval, reject: END.rejected, error: END.failed } # llm — one structured call; inputs become the prompt's input block - id: reply description: Write the customer confirmation engine: llm inputs: { order: Order, refund: Refund } outputs: { text: str } budget: { timeout: 20s, max_tokens: 1500 } llm: { model: default, system: artifact://support-voice@3, prompt: Confirm the refund briefly. } routes: { default: END, parse_error: END.failed, timeout: END.failed, budget_exceeded: END.failed, error: END.failed } # human — the outputs are the form - id: approval description: A manager approves a large refund engine: human inputs: { order: Order } outputs: { approved: bool, note: "str?" } human: { title: "Refund {{ order.id }}", show: [order], required_group: support_manager, expires: 48h, route_on: approved } routes: { "true": issue_refund, "false": END.rejected, expired: END.failed, error: END.failed }
docs.title: 6. Engines

docs.text: A workflow's profile counts its agents per class ("11 agents · 8 deterministic · 2 bounded · 1 external"); tuvl lint project prints it with the worst-case tokens per run (the maximum over paths of summed max_tokens , including guardrail judges and child workflows). Required budgets (V011): llm → max_tokens , timeout ; loop → max_iterations , max_tokens , max_tool_calls , timeout ; decide with an LLM-backed model → max_tokens , timeout . policy: max_tokens_per_run: 5000 # V020 if the worst case exceeds it max_bounded_agents: 2 require_human_before: [destructive] # every path to a destructive effect passes a human or approval model_only_decisions: warn # warn | error | allow (V013; allow = accepted on purpose, reviewed) max_depth: 2 # workflow-as-tool nesting allow_secure_to_llm: false # secure model fields never reach a model (V020)
docs.title: 7. Determinism, budgets and policy

docs.text: kind: Test version: tuvl/v2 metadata: { name: small-damaged-refund-is-automatic } spec: workflow: refund_flow given: # rows that exist before the run (in-memory database) Order: [{ id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000040", total: 40, status: delivered }] as: { user: u-customer } # the caller: the run's principal (ctx.principal) input: { order_id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000040", reason: damaged, message: "Arrived broken" } mocks: # model, external and human steps only — typed against the contract classify: { outputs: { category: damaged } } replay: tests/fixtures/refund_flow/small-refund.journal.json # serve recorded model/tool results expect: end: default # or wait: human | approval path: [load_order, triage, issue_refund, reply] # or path_includes: [...] decisions: { triage: { source: "rule#3" } } output: { status: 200, body: { amount: 40 } } # partial match assertions: ["output.body.amount == 40"] judge: - { judge: artifact://refund-reply-quality@2, target: "{{ text }}" } tuvl run tests is offline : tool: db and code agents run for real against an in-memory database seeded by given: , with the as: caller as the principal; an unmocked human agent stops the run (assert with expect.wait ); unmocked model/HTTP/MCP agents fail with a hint to mock or replay them ( --live lets them call out). That database is in autocommit, so it keeps writes Postgres would roll back (an agent's error outcome, a retried attempt, a per_run rollback): test rollback against Postgres. Honest results: a test whose path goes through an unmocked pending agent (a typed placeholder) is stubbed , not passed — it is reported, doesn't count towards task status, and fails tuvl run tests --strict (the CI gate). Mock policy: mock what is non-deterministic, external or human ( llm , loop , decide with a model, tool http / mcp , human ). Mocking business logic ( code , tool db , decide rules) is warning T001 — seed given: rows and set as: instead. expect order: structure ( end / wait , path , decisions ) → output → assertions → judge . Pin any run as a fixture ( tuvl pin run <run_id> or Insight 📌); replay: then serves its recorded engine results with zero tokens. Judges are cached and calibrated ( judges ).

docs.text: tuvl create spec refund-automation # write intent: specs/refund-automation.md tuvl lint spec # the grammar: fix every blocking finding # the coding agent writes specs/refund-automation.tasks.yaml (skill tuvl-plan) tuvl list tasks --json # derived task statuses — pick the next unblocked task # build it (YAML engine blocks; Python bodies only for code agents) tuvl generate code # schemas, code-agent stubs, prompt placeholders, tests tuvl verify spec # does the build match the spec, step by step? tuvl lint spec && tuvl lint project --strict && tuvl generate code --check && tuvl verify lock && tuvl run tests --strict && tuvl verify spec --strict && tuvl list tasks --strict That last line is the CI gate . Task statuses are derived ( todo → in_progress → implemented → tested → done , with blocked and stale overlays) — never set them by hand. See spec-driven workflow .

docs.title: 11. Rules for coding agents

docs.text: Webhooks ¶ A workflow can tell another system that a run reached a stage, so the other system does not have to poll. A webhook is a small, signed HTTPS notification. It says that something happened and which run , nothing more; the receiver then pulls the run with its own token. Webhooks are declared in the workflow YAML and delivered to the receiver you name there. A caller cannot choose where notifications go. They are meant to be received with @tuvl/client ( verifyWebhook , webhookHandler ), which is the supported way to verify one; the request format is internal and may change. Turn it on ¶ Delivery is off until the deployment enables it: set TUVL_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=true . Without it nothing is queued and nothing is sent, whatever the workflows declare. Declare a webhook ¶ spec: webhooks: - name: ops-pager url: ${OPS_WEBHOOK_URL} # an environment reference, or an https:// literal secret: ${OPS_WEBHOOK_SECRET} # at least 32 bytes; only an environment reference events: [completed, failed, waiting] stages: [classify] # also notify each time this agent finishes Field name Unique in the workflow; shown in the delivery list url ${ENV} (read when sent) or an https:// URL without credentials secret ${ENV} reference holding at least 32 bytes. It signs every call; it is never written in the YAML previous_secret ${ENV} of the secret being replaced. While set, each call is signed with both (see Rotation) events completed , failed , aborted , waiting (a person or an approval is needed) stages Agent ids. One notification each time one of them finishes allow_private Permit an internal address or plain http:// (a receiver inside your network). tuvl lint project warns A webhook must subscribe to something ( events or stages ). tuvl lint project checks the stage ids (V038). What is sent ¶ One POST with a JSON body and a fixed set of headers ( Tuvl-Event , Tuvl-Delivery , Tuvl-Signature , Content-Type , User-Agent ). The body names the run and what happened (workflow, run id, event type, the run's journal position and, for a stage or a wait, the agent) and carries no input, output or error text . A notification that reaches the wrong place discloses only that a run exists. The receiver pulls the run: GET /api/runs/{id} (or the events from the journal position) with its own token, so the usual scopes and tenant checks decide what it may read. A service token with runs:read is enough. Security ¶ No caller-chosen targets. URLs come from the workflow and the environment. Signed. Each call carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature over its timestamp and body, with the webhook's secret. The client verifies it in constant time and rejects a timestamp more than five minutes from now, so a captured call cannot be replayed later. Destination checks, twice. https only, no credentials in the URL, no internal host names or numeric address tricks ( 2130706433 , 0x7f.1 , IPv4-mapped IPv6, NAT64, 6to4). When sending, the name is resolved and refused if any address is loopback, private, link-local (including the cloud metadata address), carrier-grade NAT, multicast or reserved, then the connection goes to the address that was checked, so a second lookup cannot return something else. No redirects, no proxies from the environment, no response body kept. A 3xx is a failure. A body of up to 16 KiB with a declared length is read and dropped, so the connection can be reused. Connections are reused only for the same destination. A kept-alive connection serves the same host name and checked address only; each notification is still resolved and checked before it is sent. Fixed request. Authors cannot add headers or change the body. Nothing sensitive is stored. The outbox holds the webhook's name and the event, not the URL or the secret; both are read from the current declaration when sending, so removing or rotating takes effect at once. A declaration that no longer exists drops its queued notifications. Fails closed. A secret shorter than 32 bytes, a refused URL or an internal address ends the notification (it is not retried); an unset environment variable is retried, since it can be fixed. Contained. A receiver that keeps failing is paused for five minutes after five failures. Delivery ¶ At-least-once. A row is written with the journal event and sent by a background loop on each worker, so nothing is lost between the event and the send. A non-2xx answer or a timeout (10 s) is retried with backoff (10 s, 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h), then marked dead. 410 Gone marks it dead at once. A receiver may see the same notification twice and should de-duplicate on its id . Order within a run is by the journal position, not guaranteed on the wire. GET /api/runs/{id}/webhooks lists a run's notifications with status, attempts and the last error (scope runs:read , owner or admin). POST /api/runs/{id}/webhooks/{delivery_id}/redeliver sends one again ( runs:control ). Receive with @tuvl/client ¶ import { TuvlClient, webhookHandler } from "@tuvl/client"; const client = new TuvlClient({ baseUrl, token: serviceToken }); export const POST = webhookHandler({ secrets: [process.env.OPS_WEBHOOK_SECRET!], onNotification: async (n) => { if (await seen(n.id)) return; // de-duplicate const run = await client.run(n.run_id).get(); // pull await notifyDevices(run); }, }); Answer quickly: the sender waits ten seconds. Do the work after acknowledging, or put it on a queue. A phone should never hold the secret. Receive on your backend, verify, and push only the run id to the device; the app then pulls the run with the user's own token. Rotation ¶ Set previous_secret to the old secret's variable, put the new value in secret , and give receivers both secrets. Calls are signed with both until you remove previous_secret .

docs.text: A workflow can tell another system that a run reached a stage, so the other system does not have to poll. A webhook is a small, signed HTTPS notification. It says that something happened and which run , nothing more; the receiver then pulls the run with its own token. Webhooks are declared in the workflow YAML and delivered to the receiver you name there. A caller cannot choose where notifications go. They are meant to be received with @tuvl/client ( verifyWebhook , webhookHandler ), which is the supported way to verify one; the request format is internal and may change.
docs.title: Webhooks

docs.text: Delivery is off until the deployment enables it: set TUVL_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=true . Without it nothing is queued and nothing is sent, whatever the workflows declare.

docs.text: spec: webhooks: - name: ops-pager url: ${OPS_WEBHOOK_URL} # an environment reference, or an https:// literal secret: ${OPS_WEBHOOK_SECRET} # at least 32 bytes; only an environment reference events: [completed, failed, waiting] stages: [classify] # also notify each time this agent finishes Field name Unique in the workflow; shown in the delivery list url ${ENV} (read when sent) or an https:// URL without credentials secret ${ENV} reference holding at least 32 bytes. It signs every call; it is never written in the YAML previous_secret ${ENV} of the secret being replaced. While set, each call is signed with both (see Rotation) events completed , failed , aborted , waiting (a person or an approval is needed) stages Agent ids. One notification each time one of them finishes allow_private Permit an internal address or plain http:// (a receiver inside your network). tuvl lint project warns A webhook must subscribe to something ( events or stages ). tuvl lint project checks the stage ids (V038).

The receiver pulls the run: GET /api/runs/{id} (or the events from the journal position) with its own token, so the usual scopes and tenant checks decide what it may read. A service token with runs:read is enough.

docs.text: Federated Login (OAuth2) ¶ tuvl supports OAuth2 Authorization Code flow for Google, GitHub, and Microsoft (Entra ID). Federation providers are configured as YAML files in the federation/ directory and managed via the Federation page in the tuvl UI. How It Works ¶ sequenceDiagram participant Browser participant tuvl participant Provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft) Browser->>tuvl: GET /auth/oauth/{provider}/start tuvl->>tuvl: Generate CSRF state token (Redis or memory) tuvl-->>Browser: 302 Redirect → Provider auth URL Browser->>Provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft): User logs in + consents Provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft)-->>Browser: 302 Redirect → /auth/oauth/{provider}/callback?code=...&state=... Browser->>tuvl: GET /auth/oauth/{provider}/callback tuvl->>tuvl: Validate CSRF state tuvl->>Provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft): POST token exchange Provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft)-->>tuvl: access_token + id_token tuvl->>Provider (Google / GitHub / Microsoft): GET user profile (email, sub, name) tuvl->>tuvl: Upsert IAMUser (including first_name/last_name) + auto-assign default_role (if configured) tuvl-->>Browser: 302 Redirect → TUVL_OAUTH_UI_REDIRECT_URL?token=<jwt> CSRF state tokens are stored in Redis (when configured) or in-process memory. In multi-worker deployments you must configure a Redis datasource to share state across workers. Provider Configuration ¶ File Layout ¶ Each federation provider is a YAML file in <project>/federation/ : project/ └── federation/ ├── google.yaml ├── github.yaml └── microsoft.yaml Google ¶ kind: FederationProvider version: v1 metadata: name: google description: Google OAuth2 enabled: true spec: provider: google client_id: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET} scope: "openid email profile" # Restrict login to users whose email domain is in this list. # Omit to allow any address from the provider. # allowed_domains: # - example.com # Role to assign automatically when a brand-new federated user logs in. # The role must already exist in the IAM database. # Omit to leave new users with no roles (admin must assign manually). # default_role: member Environment variables: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=GOCSPX-... Built-in OAuth2 URLs (no override needed): Setting Value auth_url https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth token_url https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token userinfo_url https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo Google Cloud Console setup: Create a project at console.cloud.google.com Enable the People API or Google+ API Create an OAuth2 Client ID (Web Application) Add {TUVL_OAUTH_BASE_URL}/auth/oauth/google/callback to Authorized Redirect URIs GitHub ¶ kind: FederationProvider version: v1 metadata: name: github spec: provider: github client_id: ${GITHUB_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET} scope: "read:user user:email" Environment variables: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=Iv1.xxxxxxxxxxxx GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=xxxxxxxxxxxx Private emails If the user's GitHub email is set to private, tuvl automatically calls GET https://api.github.com/user/emails to find their primary verified address. GitHub App setup: Go to Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New Set Homepage URL to your base URL Set Authorization callback URL to {TUVL_OAUTH_BASE_URL}/auth/oauth/github/callback Microsoft (Entra ID) ¶ kind: FederationProvider version: v1 metadata: name: microsoft spec: provider: microsoft client_id: ${AZURE_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET} scope: "openid email profile User.Read" tenant_id: ${AZURE_TENANT_ID:common} # "common" allows any MS account Environment variables: AZURE_CLIENT_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-secret AZURE_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id # or "common" / "organizations" / "consumers" Azure Portal setup: Register an app in Azure Active Directory → App registrations Under Authentication , add {TUVL_OAUTH_BASE_URL}/auth/oauth/microsoft/callback as a redirect URI Add a client secret under Certificates & secrets Set the required tenant_id (use common to allow any Microsoft account) Custom Provider ¶ For any OpenID Connect-compatible provider, supply all URLs explicitly: kind: FederationProvider version: v1 metadata: name: okta spec: provider: custom client_id: ${OKTA_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET} scope: "openid email profile" auth_url: https://{your-domain}.okta.com/oauth2/v1/authorize token_url: https://{your-domain}.okta.com/oauth2/v1/token userinfo_url: https://{your-domain}.okta.com/oauth2/v1/userinfo Required Environment Variable ¶ TUVL_OAUTH_BASE_URL=https://your-tuvl-instance.example.com This tells tuvl what base URL to use when constructing the redirect URI sent to the provider. In local development set it to http://localhost:8885 . TUVL_OAUTH_UI_REDIRECT_URL=https://app.example.com/auth/callback After a successful OAuth login the browser is redirected to this URL with ?token=<jwt> appended. Your frontend reads the token from the query string and passes it to TuvlClient . When unset the callback returns JSON instead (useful for server-side and CLI flows). Admin API ¶ Federation provider files can be managed without filesystem access via the admin API. Note All federation admin endpoints require the iam:admin scope. List Configured Providers ¶ GET /auth/admin/federation Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns an array of provider names: ["google", "github"] Get Provider Config ¶ GET /auth/admin/federation/{name} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns the raw YAML content. The client_secret field is always redacted ( "***" ) in the response regardless of whether it was set as a literal or an env-var reference. Create / Update Provider ¶ PUT /auth/admin/federation/{name} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Content-Type: application/json Accepts the YAML object as JSON. The file is saved to <project>/federation/{name}.yaml and the registry is reloaded immediately. Delete Provider ¶ DELETE /auth/admin/federation/{name} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Removes the YAML file and un-registers the provider immediately (no restart needed). Account Linking ¶ When a federated login succeeds, tuvl looks up a iam_users record by email: Found — the existing account is reused. federated_provider and federated_sub are updated on the record if not already set. Not found — a new user record is created with is_active=true . The account has no password (federated-only). The returned access token carries whatever roles the user has been assigned in the database. First-time federated users have no roles by default When a user logs in via OAuth for the first time they arrive with zero permissions . Any workflow call that requires a scope will return 403 Forbidden . To avoid this, add a default_role field to the provider YAML: spec: provider: google client_id: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET} default_role: member # role must exist in the IAM database tuvl will auto-assign that role the moment the user record is created. The role assignment is permanent — it is not removed if you later remove default_role from the YAML. Domain Restriction ¶ Use allowed_domains to limit login to specific email domains: spec: provider: google client_id: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET} allowed_domains: - acme.com - acme.org Users whose email domain is not in the list receive a 403 Forbidden at the callback step. Leave the field absent (or empty) to allow any domain. Restricting GitHub logins by handle ¶ For the github provider, allowed_users limits login to specific GitHub handles (case-insensitive). It combines with allowed_domains : a login must satisfy every restriction that is set. spec: provider: github client_id: ${GITHUB_CLIENT_ID} client_secret: ${GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET} allowed_users: - octocat Device login for command-line tools ¶ A CLI can sign in without a browser callback. POST /auth/oauth/github/device/start returns a handle , a user_code , a verification_uri , an interval and expires_in ; GitHub's device code stays on the server. The user opens the URI and enters the code while the client polls POST /auth/oauth/github/device/poll {"handle": …} : 428 while pending, 200 with a token once approved (same account linking as the browser flow), 400 when denied or expired. A handle is single-use. Tick Enable Device Flow on the GitHub OAuth app. tuvl register project and Insight's Register dialog use this flow. When TUVL_OAUTH_UI_REDIRECT_URL is set, the browser callback now returns the token in the URL fragment ( #token=… ), not the query string, so it never reaches a server log.

docs.text: Identity & Access Management (IAM) ¶ tuvl has a built-in IAM system based on users , roles , and scopes . Access tokens are Ed25519-signed JWTs that carry identity, group membership, and fine-grained permission scopes — see Access Tokens . Concepts ¶ Users ¶ A User is a principal that can authenticate with tuvl. Users can use: Password auth — email (or phone number) + bcrypt-hashed password via POST /auth/token Federated auth — OAuth2 login via Google, GitHub, or Microsoft ( see Federation ) Both — a user may link both methods to the same account Roles ¶ A Role is a named bundle of scopes. Examples: Role Scopes superadmin iam:admin (all admin operations) hr_manager requisition:write , candidate:read recruiter candidate:read , interview:read Scopes ¶ Scopes are arbitrary resource:action strings that your workflows and endpoints check. The only built-in scope is iam:admin , which gates all /auth/admin/* endpoints. Authorization Surfaces ¶ Scopes and groups gate two built-in surfaces beyond any custom endpoints you protect yourself (see Protecting Your Own Endpoints ): the auto-generated model CRUD API and workflow triggers. Model CRUD ¶ Every /models/{model}/… route requires a valid access token by default. Scope names default to {modelname.lower()}:read / :write / :delete , overridable per model with spec.access.{read,write,delete}_scope in the ModelDefinition . spec.access.{read,write,delete}_groups (a list, or a bare group name) layers an IAM group requirement on top of the scope check — both the scope and the group must pass. A tier left undeclared cascades from the next-more-privileged tier ( write_groups falls back to read_groups , delete_groups falls back to write_groups ), so pinning only read_groups never leaves mutations open to a wider audience than reads. Declaring no groups at all is scope-only. iam:admin bypasses every scope and group check. kind: ModelDefinition metadata: name: Candidate spec: access: read_scope: candidate:read write_scope: candidate:write read_groups: recruiter # bare string or a list write_groups: [hr_manager] # delete_groups falls back to this Use GET /admin/scopes to see every enforceable scope grouped by source ( crud , workflows , system ) — its crud_api_enabled field also reports whether the CRUD kill switch is currently on. Disabling CRUD entirely The whole /models/* surface can be turned off project-wide with spec.api.expose_model_crud: false — see Configuration Overview . When disabled, the routes are absent, not merely scope-denied. Workflow Triggers ¶ Workflow triggers are gated by metadata.required_scope and/or metadata.required_group in the workflow YAML. Every way of starting a run — the workflow's HTTP route, POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs , and MCP export — requires a valid bearer token by default, even for a workflow that declares neither. Anonymous access is an explicit opt-in via spec.trigger.http.public: true . Combining public: true with a declared required_scope or required_group is a tuvl lint project error — the engine fails closed and always enforces the declared scope/group over public at runtime. kind: Workflow version: tuvl/v2 metadata: name: register_user spec: trigger: http: { path: /api/register, method: POST, public: true } # anonymous — no required_scope/required_group alongside In dev mode ( tuvl dev ), workflows with no scope/group requirement stay tokenless so quickstarts run without a login step. An IAM role's name is the token's group : required_group: finance_lead admits users who hold the finance_lead role. The role's scopes travel in the token too, and iam:admin passes every check. People who follow runs and decide human steps ¶ Starting a run is one grant; following it and deciding its human steps are separate scopes: To… The caller needs read the runs they started and their events (e.g. poll a 202 run) nothing beyond signing in — iam:admin reads everyone's pause, resume, abort or steer a run runs:control see and decide approvals approvals:decide and the step's human.required_group , if it has one A reviewer role therefore carries both: name it after the group the human step requires and give it the scope. Insight's approver picker flags a role without approvals:decide and grants it in one click. curl -X POST http://localhost:8885/auth/admin/roles -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"name": "finance_lead", "scopes": ["approvals:decide"]}' On a group-gated step, the person who started the run can't approve it. Every decision is journaled with who made it. When access changes ¶ Taking access away is immediate. Deactivating a user, changing their password, deleting them, removing one of their roles, or deleting or narrowing a role they hold ends their sessions : tokens issued before that are refused ( 401 Session ended — sign in again. ), and the next sign-in gets the current roles. Granting a role or adding scopes ends nothing — the user picks it up at their next sign-in. Users and roles that are in use can be deleted; their role links go with them. Bootstrap ¶ On a fresh installation with no users, the bootstrap endpoint creates the first superadmin: curl -X POST http://localhost:8885/auth/bootstrap \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "email": "admin@example.com", "password": "change-me-now" }' { "access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer" } One-time only Bootstrap fails with 409 Conflict if any user already exists. It is a one-time setup operation intended only for empty databases. Authentication ¶ Password Login ¶ POST /auth/token Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded username=admin@example.com&password=change-me-now OAuth2 form format /auth/token follows the OAuth2 password-grant standard — it expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded with fields username and password (not JSON). The username field accepts either an email address or a phone number. This makes it compatible with the Swagger UI Authorize button. Response: { "access_token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer" } Use the token in subsequent requests: curl http://localhost:8885/auth/admin/users \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" Token Refresh ¶ Exchange the current token for a new one with a fresh TTL (the old token is immediately revoked): curl -X POST http://localhost:8885/auth/refresh \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <old_token>" Returns a new TokenResponse . The old token is added to the blacklist and can no longer be used. Logout ¶ Revoke the current token immediately: curl -X POST http://localhost:8885/auth/logout \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" Returns 204 No Content . The token is added to the blacklist. Using the TypeScript SDK ¶ The @tuvl/client package ships a TuvlAuth helper that wraps all /auth/* endpoints — no manual fetch required. Install ¶ npm install @tuvl/client Password login ¶ import { TuvlAuth, TuvlClient } from "@tuvl/client"; const auth = new TuvlAuth({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:8885" }); const { access_token } = await auth.loginWithPassword("admin@example.com", "secret"); // Attach the token to the workflow client const client = new TuvlClient({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:8885", token: access_token }); OAuth2 login (browser) ¶ // 1. Redirect the browser to the provider const auth = new TuvlAuth({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:8885" }); window.location.href = auth.getOAuthLoginUrl("google"); // 2. After login the server redirects to TUVL_OAUTH_UI_REDIRECT_URL?token=<jwt> // On that landing page, extract the token: const token = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("token")!; const client = new TuvlClient({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:8885", token }); Configure the redirect Set TUVL_OAUTH_UI_REDIRECT_URL in your server .env to the URL of the page that should receive the token after OAuth completes. Without it the callback returns JSON (suitable for server-side and CLI flows). TUVL_OAUTH_UI_REDIRECT_URL=https://app.example.com/auth/callback Token refresh ¶ const { access_token: newToken } = await auth.refresh(currentToken); client.setToken(newToken); // update the workflow client in-place Logout ¶ await auth.logout(token); // discard the token from storage after this call Full bootstrap → login → call example ¶ import { TuvlAuth, TuvlClient } from "@tuvl/client"; const BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8885"; const auth = new TuvlAuth({ baseUrl: BASE_URL }); // Step 1 — on a fresh install: bootstrap the first admin // (curl -X POST .../auth/bootstrap or via the tuvl UI) // Step 2 — login const { access_token } = await auth.loginWithPassword("admin@example.com", "secret"); // Step 3 — use the token for workflow calls const client = new TuvlClient({ baseUrl: BASE_URL, token: access_token }); const result = await client.execute("hello"); // Step 4 — refresh before expiry (default TTL: 24 h) const { access_token: fresh } = await auth.refresh(access_token); client.setToken(fresh); Admin: Users ¶ All user management endpoints require the iam:admin scope. Create User ¶ POST /auth/admin/users Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Content-Type: application/json { "email": "jane@example.com", "password": "secure-password", "is_active": true } password is optional — omit it for federated-only accounts. Returns 201 Created with the user object. List Users ¶ GET /auth/admin/users Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns an array of user objects including their assigned roles. Get Single User ¶ GET /auth/admin/users/{user_id} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Update User ¶ PATCH /auth/admin/users/{user_id} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Content-Type: application/json { "password": "new-password", "is_active": false } Both fields are optional. Omit a field to leave it unchanged. Delete User ¶ DELETE /auth/admin/users/{user_id} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns 204 No Content . Also removes all role assignments for the user. Admin: Roles ¶ Create Role ¶ POST /auth/admin/roles Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "hr_manager", "description": "Can manage job requisitions and review candidates", "scopes": ["requisition:write", "candidate:read"] } List Roles ¶ GET /auth/admin/roles Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Update Role Scopes ¶ Replace the complete scope list for a role: PATCH /auth/admin/roles/{role_id}/scopes Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Content-Type: application/json { "scopes": ["requisition:write", "candidate:read", "interview:read"] } This operation is atomic — all existing scopes are deleted and the new list is inserted in one transaction. Delete Role ¶ DELETE /auth/admin/roles/{role_id} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns 204 No Content . Admin: Role Assignment ¶ Assign Role to User ¶ POST /auth/admin/users/{user_id}/roles/{role_id} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns 200 OK . The user's next token (on refresh or re-login) will include the new role's scopes. Revoke Role from User ¶ DELETE /auth/admin/users/{user_id}/roles/{role_id} Authorization: Bearer <admin_token> Returns 204 No Content . Protecting Your Own Endpoints ¶ Require Authentication ¶ Use verify_token + get_current_user as FastAPI dependencies: from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends from tuvl.core.auth.access import get_current_user from tuvl.core.auth.schemas import TokenUser router = APIRouter() @router.get("/my-endpoint") async def my_endpoint(user: TokenUser = Depends(get_current_user)): return {"user_id": user.user_id, "scopes": user.scopes} Require a Specific Scope ¶ from tuvl.core.auth.access import require_scope @router.post("/requisitions") async def create_requisition( user: TokenUser = Depends(require_scope("requisition:write")), ): ... require_scope raises 403 Forbidden if the token does not carry the required scope. Require Group Membership ¶ from tuvl.core.auth.access import require_groups @router.get("/admin-panel") async def admin_panel( user: TokenUser = Depends(require_groups(["hr_manager", "superadmin"])), ): ... require_groups raises 403 Forbidden unless the token carries at least one of the listed groups. Database Tables ¶ The IAM system creates four tables on startup: Table Purpose tuvl_system_iam_users User credentials (email, phone number, names, bcrypt hash, federation fields) tuvl_system_iam_roles Named roles with optional description tuvl_system_iam_user_roles Many-to-many: user ↔ role assignments tuvl_system_iam_role_scopes One row per scope per role Tables are created automatically via SQLModel's create_all during startup — no migration tool required for initial setup. Dev Mode ¶ In tuvl dev , the dev API key (auto-generated and shown on startup) is accepted on all /auth/* endpoints as a synthetic superuser with the iam:admin scope. This removes the need to create a user or manage tokens during local development. # Both of these work in dev mode: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <dev_api_key>" http://localhost:8885/dev/files curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <dev_api_key>" http://localhost:8885/auth/admin/users

docs.text: tuvl has a built-in IAM system based on users , roles , and scopes . Access tokens are Ed25519-signed JWTs that carry identity, group membership, and fine-grained permission scopes — see Access Tokens .
docs.title: Identity & Access Management (IAM)

docs.text: A User is a principal that can authenticate with tuvl. Users can use: Password auth — email (or phone number) + bcrypt-hashed password via POST /auth/token Federated auth — OAuth2 login via Google, GitHub, or Microsoft ( see Federation ) Both — a user may link both methods to the same account
docs.title: Users

docs.text: A Role is a named bundle of scopes. Examples: Role Scopes superadmin iam:admin (all admin operations) hr_manager requisition:write , candidate:read recruiter candidate:read , interview:read
docs.title: Roles

docs.text: Scopes are arbitrary resource:action strings that your workflows and endpoints check. The only built-in scope is iam:admin , which gates all /auth/admin/* endpoints.
docs.title: Scopes

docs.text: Scopes and groups gate two built-in surfaces beyond any custom endpoints you protect yourself (see Protecting Your Own Endpoints ): the auto-generated model CRUD API and workflow triggers.
docs.title: Authorization Surfaces

docs.text: Every /models/{model}/… route requires a valid access token by default. Scope names default to {modelname.lower()}:read / :write / :delete , overridable per model with spec.access.{read,write,delete}_scope in the ModelDefinition . spec.access.{read,write,delete}_groups (a list, or a bare group name) layers an IAM group requirement on top of the scope check — both the scope and the group must pass. A tier left undeclared cascades from the next-more-privileged tier ( write_groups falls back to read_groups , delete_groups falls back to write_groups ), so pinning only read_groups never leaves mutations open to a wider audience than reads. Declaring no groups at all is scope-only. iam:admin bypasses every scope and group check. kind: ModelDefinition metadata: name: Candidate spec: access: read_scope: candidate:read write_scope: candidate:write read_groups: recruiter # bare string or a list write_groups: [hr_manager] # delete_groups falls back to this Use GET /admin/scopes to see every enforceable scope grouped by source ( crud , workflows , system ) — its crud_api_enabled field also reports whether the CRUD kill switch is currently on. Disabling CRUD entirely The whole /models/* surface can be turned off project-wide with spec.api.expose_model_crud: false — see Configuration Overview . When disabled, the routes are absent, not merely scope-denied.
docs.title: Model CRUD

docs.text: Workflow triggers are gated by metadata.required_scope and/or metadata.required_group in the workflow YAML. Every way of starting a run — the workflow's HTTP route, POST /api/workflows/{name}/runs , and MCP export — requires a valid bearer token by default, even for a workflow that declares neither. Anonymous access is an explicit opt-in via spec.trigger.http.public: true . Combining public: true with a declared required_scope or required_group is a tuvl lint project error — the engine fails closed and always enforces the declared scope/group over public at runtime. kind: Workflow version: tuvl/v2 metadata: name: register_user spec: trigger: http: { path: /api/register, method: POST, public: true } # anonymous — no required_scope/required_group alongside In dev mode ( tuvl dev ), workflows with no scope/group requirement stay tokenless so quickstarts run without a login step. An IAM role's name is the token's group : required_group: finance_lead admits users who hold the finance_lead role. The role's scopes travel in the token too, and iam:admin passes every check.
